\begin{abstract}
\texttt{WHIZARD} is an application of the \texttt{VAMP} algorithm:
Adaptive multi-channel integration and event generation. The bare
\texttt{VAMP} library is augmented by modules for Lorentz algebra,
particles, phase space, etc., such that physical processes with
arbitrary complex final states [well, in principle\ldots] can be
integrated and \emph{unweighted} events be generated.
\end{abstract}

\chapter{Utilities}
\includemodulegraph{utilities}

These modules are intended as part of WHIZARD, but in fact they are
generic and could be useful for any purpose.

The modules depend only on modules from the {\Tt{}basics\nwendquote} set.
\begin{description}
\item[file\_utils]
  Procedures that deal with external files, if not covered by Fortran
  built-ins.
\item[file\_registries]
  Manage files that are accessed by their name.
\item[string\_utils]
  Some string-handling utilities.  Includes conversion to C string.
\item[format\_utils]
  Utilities for pretty-printing.
\item[format\_defs]
  Predefined format strings.
\item[numeric\_utils]
  Utilities for comparing numerical values.
\end{description}

\LA{}File header\RA{}

module file_utils

  use io_units

\LA{}Standard module head\RA{}

\LA{}File utils: public\RA{}

\LA{}File utils: procedures\RA{}

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{2}\nwdocspar
\subsection{Deleting a file}
Fortran does not contain a command for deleting a file.  Here, we
provide a subroutine that deletes a file if it exists.  We do not
handle the subtleties, so we assume that it is writable if it exists.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{3}\moddef{File utils: public}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  public :: delete_file
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{4}\moddef{File utils: procedures}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine delete_file (name)
    character(*), intent(in) :: name
    logical :: exist
    integer :: u
    inquire (file = name, exist = exist)
    if (exist) then
       u = free_unit ()
       open (unit = u, file = name)
       close (u, status = "delete")
    end if
  end subroutine delete_file

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{5}\nwdocspar
%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\section{File Registries}

This module provides a file-registry facility.  We can open and close
files multiple times without inadvertedly accessing a single file by two
different I/O unit numbers.  Opening a file the first time enters it
into the registry.  Opening again just returns the associated I/O
unit.  The registry maintains a reference count, so closing a file
does not actually complete until the last reference is released.

File access will always be sequential, however.  The file can't be
opened at different positions simultaneously.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{6}\moddef{\code{}file{\_}registries.f90\edoc{}}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
\LA{}File header\RA{}

module file_registries

\LA{}Use strings\RA{}
  use io_units

\LA{}Standard module head\RA{}

\LA{}File registries: public\RA{}

\LA{}File registries: types\RA{}

contains

\LA{}File registries: procedures\RA{}

end module file_registries
\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{7}\nwdocspar
\subsection{File handle}
This object holds a filename (fully qualified), the associated
unit, and a reference count.  The idea is that the object should be
deleted when the reference count drops to zero.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{8}\moddef{File registries: types}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  type :: file_handle_t
     type(string_t) :: file
     integer :: unit = 0
     integer :: refcount = 0
   contains
   \LA{}File registries: file handle: TBP\RA{}
  end type file_handle_t

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{9}Debugging output:
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{10}\moddef{File registries: file handle: TBP}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure :: write => file_handle_write
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{11}\moddef{File registries: procedures}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine file_handle_write (handle, u, show_unit)
    class(file_handle_t), intent(in) :: handle
    integer, intent(in) :: u
    logical, intent(in), optional :: show_unit
    logical :: show_u
    show_u = .false.;  if (present (show_unit))  show_u = show_unit
    if (show_u) then
       write (u, "(3x,A,1x,I0,1x,'(',I0,')')")  &
            char (handle%file), handle%unit, handle%refcount
    else
       write (u, "(3x,A,1x,'(',I0,')')")  &
            char (handle%file), handle%refcount
    end if
  end subroutine file_handle_write

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{12}Initialize with a file name, don't open the file yet:
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{13}\moddef{File registries: file handle: TBP}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure :: init => file_handle_init
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{14}\moddef{File registries: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine file_handle_init (handle, file)
    class(file_handle_t), intent(out) :: handle
    type(string_t), intent(in) :: file
    handle%file = file
  end subroutine file_handle_init

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{15}We check the {\Tt{}refcount\nwendquote} before actually opening the file.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{16}\moddef{File registries: file handle: TBP}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure :: open => file_handle_open
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{17}\moddef{File registries: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine file_handle_open (handle)
    class(file_handle_t), intent(inout) :: handle
    if (handle%refcount == 0) then
       handle%unit = free_unit ()
       open (unit = handle%unit, file = char (handle%file), action = "read", &
            status = "old")
    end if
    handle%refcount = handle%refcount + 1
  end subroutine file_handle_open

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{18}Analogously, close if the refcount drops to zero.  The caller may
then delete the object.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{19}\moddef{File registries: file handle: TBP}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure :: close => file_handle_close
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{20}\moddef{File registries: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine file_handle_close (handle)
    class(file_handle_t), intent(inout) :: handle
    handle%refcount = handle%refcount - 1
    if (handle%refcount == 0) then
       close (handle%unit)
       handle%unit = 0
    end if
  end subroutine file_handle_close

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{21}The I/O unit will be nonzero when the file is open.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{22}\moddef{File registries: file handle: TBP}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure :: is_open => file_handle_is_open
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{23}\moddef{File registries: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  function file_handle_is_open (handle) result (flag)
    class(file_handle_t), intent(in) :: handle
    logical :: flag
    flag = handle%unit /= 0
  end function file_handle_is_open

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{24}Return the filename, so we can identify the entry.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{25}\moddef{File registries: file handle: TBP}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure :: get_file => file_handle_get_file
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{26}\moddef{File registries: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  function file_handle_get_file (handle) result (file)
    class(file_handle_t), intent(in) :: handle
    type(string_t) :: file
    file = handle%file
  end function file_handle_get_file

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{27}For debugging, return the I/O unit number.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{28}\moddef{File registries: file handle: TBP}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure :: get_unit => file_handle_get_unit
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{29}\moddef{File registries: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  function file_handle_get_unit (handle) result (unit)
    class(file_handle_t), intent(in) :: handle
    integer :: unit
    unit = handle%unit
  end function file_handle_get_unit

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{30}\nwdocspar
\subsection{File handles registry}
This is implemented as a doubly-linked list.  The list exists only
once in the program, as a private module variable.

Extend the handle type to become a list entry:
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{31}\moddef{File registries: types}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  type, extends (file_handle_t) :: file_entry_t
     type(file_entry_t), pointer :: prev => null ()
     type(file_entry_t), pointer :: next => null ()
  end type file_entry_t

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{32}The actual registry.  We need only the pointer to the first entry.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{33}\moddef{File registries: public}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  public :: file_registry_t
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{34}\moddef{File registries: types}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  type :: file_registry_t
     type(file_entry_t), pointer :: first => null ()
   contains
   \LA{}File registries: file registry: TBP\RA{}
  end type file_registry_t

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{35}Debugging output.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{36}\moddef{File registries: file registry: TBP}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure :: write => file_registry_write
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{37}\moddef{File registries: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine file_registry_write (registry, unit, show_unit)
    class(file_registry_t), intent(in) :: registry
    integer, intent(in), optional :: unit
    logical, intent(in), optional :: show_unit
    type(file_entry_t), pointer :: entry
    integer :: u
    u = given_output_unit (unit)
    if (associated (registry%first)) then
       write (u, "(1x,A)")  "File registry:"
       entry => registry%first
       do while (associated (entry))
          call entry%write (u, show_unit)
          entry => entry%next
       end do
    else
       write (u, "(1x,A)")  "File registry: [empty]"
    end if
  end subroutine file_registry_write

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{38}Open a file: find the appropriate entry.  Create a new entry and add
to the list if necessary.  The list is extended at the beginning.
Return the I/O unit number for the records.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{39}\moddef{File registries: file registry: TBP}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure :: open => file_registry_open
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{40}\moddef{File registries: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine file_registry_open (registry, file, unit)
    class(file_registry_t), intent(inout) :: registry
    type(string_t), intent(in) :: file
    integer, intent(out), optional :: unit
    type(file_entry_t), pointer :: entry
    entry => registry%first
    FIND_ENTRY: do while (associated (entry))
       if (entry%get_file () == file)  exit FIND_ENTRY
       entry => entry%next
    end do FIND_ENTRY
    if (.not. associated (entry)) then
       allocate (entry)
       call entry%init (file)
       if (associated (registry%first)) then
          registry%first%prev => entry
          entry%next => registry%first
       end if
       registry%first => entry
    end if
    call entry%open ()
    if (present (unit))  unit = entry%get_unit ()
  end subroutine file_registry_open

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{41}Close a file: find the appropriate entry.  Delete the entry if there
is no file connected to it anymore.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{42}\moddef{File registries: file registry: TBP}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure :: close => file_registry_close
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{43}\moddef{File registries: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine file_registry_close (registry, file)
    class(file_registry_t), intent(inout) :: registry
    type(string_t), intent(in) :: file
    type(file_entry_t), pointer :: entry
    entry => registry%first
    FIND_ENTRY: do while (associated (entry))
       if (entry%get_file () == file)  exit FIND_ENTRY
       entry => entry%next
    end do FIND_ENTRY
    if (associated (entry)) then
       call entry%close ()
       if (.not. entry%is_open ()) then
          if (associated (entry%prev)) then
             entry%prev%next => entry%next
          else
             registry%first => entry%next
          end if
          if (associated (entry%next)) then
             entry%next%prev => entry%prev
          end if
          deallocate (entry)
       end if
    end if
  end subroutine file_registry_close

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{44}\nwdocspar

\section{String Utilities}

This module provides tools associated with strings
(built-in and variable).  Currently:
\begin{itemize}
\item
  Upper and lower case for strings
\item
  Convert to null-terminated C string
\end{itemize}
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{45}\moddef{\code{}string{\_}utils.f90\edoc{}}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
\LA{}File header\RA{}

module string_utils

  use, intrinsic :: iso_c_binding

\LA{}Use kinds\RA{}
\LA{}Use strings\RA{}

\LA{}Standard module head\RA{}

\LA{}String utils: public\RA{}

\LA{}String utils: interfaces\RA{}

contains

\LA{}String utils: procedures\RA{}

end module string_utils
\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{46}\nwdocspar
\subsection{Upper and Lower Case}
These are, unfortunately, not part of Fortran.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{47}\moddef{String utils: public}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  public :: upper_case
  public :: lower_case
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{48}\moddef{String utils: interfaces}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  interface upper_case
     module procedure upper_case_char, upper_case_string
  end interface
  interface lower_case
     module procedure lower_case_char, lower_case_string
  end interface
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{49}\moddef{String utils: procedures}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  function upper_case_char (string) result (new_string)
    character(*), intent(in) :: string
    character(len(string)) :: new_string
    integer :: pos, code
    integer, parameter :: offset = ichar('A')-ichar('a')
    do pos = 1, len (string)
       code = ichar (string(pos:pos))
       select case (code)
       case (ichar('a'):ichar('z'))
          new_string(pos:pos) = char (code + offset)
       case default
          new_string(pos:pos) = string(pos:pos)
       end select
    end do
  end function upper_case_char

  function lower_case_char (string) result (new_string)
    character(*), intent(in) :: string
    character(len(string)) :: new_string
    integer :: pos, code
    integer, parameter :: offset = ichar('a')-ichar('A')
    do pos = 1, len (string)
       code = ichar (string(pos:pos))
       select case (code)
       case (ichar('A'):ichar('Z'))
          new_string(pos:pos) = char (code + offset)
       case default
          new_string(pos:pos) = string(pos:pos)
       end select
    end do
  end function lower_case_char

  function upper_case_string (string) result (new_string)
    type(string_t), intent(in) :: string
    type(string_t) :: new_string
    new_string = upper_case_char (char (string))
  end function upper_case_string

  function lower_case_string (string) result (new_string)
    type(string_t), intent(in) :: string
    type(string_t) :: new_string
    new_string = lower_case_char (char (string))
  end function lower_case_string

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{50}\nwdocspar
\subsection{C-compatible Output}
Convert a FORTRAN string into a zero terminated C string.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{51}\moddef{String utils: public}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  public :: string_f2c
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{52}\moddef{String utils: interfaces}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  interface string_f2c
     module procedure string_f2c_char, string_f2c_var_str
  end interface string_f2c
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{53}\moddef{String utils: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  pure function string_f2c_char (i) result (o)
    character(*), intent(in) :: i
    character(kind=c_char, len=len (i) + 1) :: o
    o = i // c_null_char
  end function string_f2c_char

  pure function string_f2c_var_str (i) result (o)
    type(string_t), intent(in) :: i
    character(kind=c_char, len=len (i) + 1) :: o
    o = char (i) // c_null_char
  end function string_f2c_var_str

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{54}\nwdocspar
\subsection{Number Conversion}
Create a string from a number.  We use fixed format for the reals
and variable format for integers.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{55}\moddef{String utils: public}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  public :: str
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{56}\moddef{String utils: interfaces}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  interface str
     module procedure str_log, str_logs, str_int, str_ints, &
            str_real, str_reals, str_complex, str_complexs
  end interface
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{57}\moddef{String utils: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  function str_log (l) result (s)
    logical, intent(in) :: l
    type(string_t) :: s
    if (l) then
       s = "True"
    else
       s = "False"
    end if
  end function str_log

  function str_logs (x) result (s)
    logical, dimension(:), intent(in) :: x
    \LA{}concatenate strings\RA{}
  end function str_logs

  function str_int (i) result (s)
    integer, intent(in) :: i
    type(string_t) :: s
    character(32) :: buffer
    write (buffer, "(I0)")  i
    s = var_str (trim (adjustl (buffer)))
  end function str_int

  function str_ints (x) result (s)
    integer, dimension(:), intent(in) :: x
    \LA{}concatenate strings\RA{}
  end function str_ints

  function str_real (x) result (s)
    real(default), intent(in) :: x
    type(string_t) :: s
    character(32) :: buffer
    write (buffer, "(ES17.10)")  x
    s = var_str (trim (adjustl (buffer)))
  end function str_real

  function str_reals (x) result (s)
    real(default), dimension(:), intent(in) :: x
    \LA{}concatenate strings\RA{}
  end function str_reals

  function str_complex (x) result (s)
    complex(default), intent(in) :: x
    type(string_t) :: s
    s = str_real (real (x)) // " + i " // str_real (aimag (x))
  end function str_complex

  function str_complexs (x) result (s)
    complex(default), dimension(:), intent(in) :: x
    \LA{}concatenate strings\RA{}
  end function str_complexs

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{58}\moddef{concatenate strings}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
type(string_t) :: s
integer :: i
s = '['
do i = 1, size(x) - 1
   s = s // str(x(i)) // ', '
end do
s = s // str(x(size(x))) // ']'
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{59}\nwdocspar
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegindocs{60}Auxiliary: Read real, integer, string value.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{61}\moddef{String utils: public}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  public :: read_rval
  public :: read_ival
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{62}\moddef{String utils: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  function read_rval (s) result (rval)
    real(default) :: rval
    type(string_t), intent(in) :: s
    character(80) :: buffer
    buffer = s
    read (buffer, *)  rval
  end function read_rval

  function read_ival (s) result (ival)

    type(string_t), intent(in) :: s
    character(80) :: buffer
    buffer = s
    read (buffer, *)  ival
  end function read_ival

\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{63}\nwdocspar
\subsection{String splitting}
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{64}\moddef{String utils: public}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  public :: string_contains_word
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{65}\moddef{String utils: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  function string_contains_word (str, word) result (val)
    logical :: val
    type(string_t), intent(in) :: str, word
    type(string_t) :: str_tmp, str_out
    str_tmp = str
    call split (str_tmp, str_out, word)
    val = str_out /= ""
  end function string_contains_word

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{66}Create an array of strings using a separator.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{67}\moddef{String utils: public}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  public :: split_string
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{68}\moddef{String utils: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine split_string (str, separator, str_array)
    type(string_t), dimension(:), allocatable, intent(out) :: str_array
    type(string_t), intent(in) :: str, separator
    type(string_t) :: str_tmp, str_out
    integer :: n_str
    n_str = 0; str_tmp = str
    do while (string_contains_word (str_tmp, separator))
       n_str = n_str + 1
       call split (str_tmp, str_out, separator)
    end do
    allocate (str_array (n_str))
    n_str = 1; str_tmp = str
    do while (string_contains_word (str_tmp, separator))
       call split (str_tmp, str_array (n_str), separator)
       n_str = n_str + 1
    end do
  end subroutine split_string

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{69}\nwdocspar
%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\section{Format Utilities}

This module provides miscellaneous tools associated with formatting and
pretty-printing.
\begin{itemize}
\item
  Horizontal separator lines in output
\item
  Indenting an output line
\item
  Formatting a number for \TeX\ output.
\item
  Formatting a number for MetaPost output.
\item
  Alternate numeric formats.
\end{itemize}
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{70}\moddef{\code{}format{\_}utils.f90\edoc{}}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
\LA{}File header\RA{}

module format_utils

\LA{}Use kinds\RA{}
\LA{}Use strings\RA{}
  use string_utils, only: lower_case
  use io_units, only: given_output_unit

\LA{}Standard module head\RA{}

\LA{}Format utils: public\RA{}

contains

\LA{}Format utils: procedures\RA{}

end module format_utils
\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{71}\nwdocspar
\subsection{Line Output}
Write a separator line.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{72}\moddef{Format utils: public}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  public :: write_separator
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{73}\moddef{Format utils: procedures}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine write_separator (u, mode)
    integer, intent(in) :: u
    integer, intent(in), optional :: mode
    integer :: m
    m = 1;  if (present (mode))  m = mode
    select case (m)
    case default
       write (u, "(A)")  repeat ("-", 72)
    case (1)
       write (u, "(A)")  repeat ("-", 72)
    case (2)
       write (u, "(A)")  repeat ("=", 72)
    end select
  end subroutine write_separator

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{74}\nwdocspar
Indent the line with given number of blanks.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{75}\moddef{Format utils: public}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  public :: write_indent
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{76}\moddef{Format utils: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine write_indent (unit, indent)
    integer, intent(in) :: unit
    integer, intent(in), optional :: indent
    if (present (indent)) then
       write (unit, "(1x,A)", advance="no")  repeat ("  ", indent)
    end if
  end subroutine write_indent

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{77}\nwdocspar
\subsection{Array Output}
Write an array of integers.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{78}\moddef{Format utils: public}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  public :: write_integer_array
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{79}\moddef{Format utils: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine write_integer_array (array, unit, n_max)
    integer, intent(in), dimension(:) :: array
    integer, intent(in), optional :: unit
    integer, intent(in), optional :: n_max
    integer :: u, i, n
    u = given_output_unit (unit)
    if (present (n_max)) then
       n = n_max
    else
       n = size (array)
    end if
    do i = 1, n
       if (i < n) then
          write (u, "(I0, A)", advance = "no") array(i), ", "
       else
          write (u, "(I0)") array(i)
       end if
    end do
  end subroutine write_integer_array

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{80}\nwdocspar
\subsection{\TeX-compatible Output}
Quote underscore characters for use in \TeX\ output.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{81}\moddef{Format utils: public}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  public :: quote_underscore
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{82}\moddef{Format utils: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  function quote_underscore (string) result (quoted)
    type(string_t) :: quoted
    type(string_t), intent(in) :: string
    type(string_t) :: part
    type(string_t) :: buffer
    buffer = string
    quoted = ""
    do
      call split (part, buffer, "_")
      quoted = quoted // part
      if (buffer == "")  exit
      quoted = quoted // "\\_"
    end do
  end function quote_underscore

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{83}Format a number with $n$ significant digits for use in \TeX\ documents.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{84}\moddef{Format utils: public}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  public :: tex_format
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{85}\moddef{Format utils: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  function tex_format (rval, n_digits) result (string)
    type(string_t) :: string
    real(default), intent(in) :: rval
    integer, intent(in) :: n_digits
    integer :: e, n, w, d
    real(default) :: absval
    real(default) :: mantissa
    character :: sign
    character(20) :: format
    character(80) :: cstr
    n = min (abs (n_digits), 16)
    if (rval == 0) then
       string = "0"
    else
       absval = abs (rval)
       e = int (log10 (absval))
       if (rval < 0) then
          sign = "-"
       else
          sign = ""
       end if
       select case (e)
       case (:-3)
          d = max (n - 1, 0)
          w = max (d + 2, 2)
          write (format, "('(F',I0,'.',I0,',A,I0,A)')")  w, d
          mantissa = absval * 10._default ** (1 - e)
          write (cstr, fmt=format)  mantissa, "\\times 10^\{", e - 1, "\}"
       case (-2:0)
          d = max (n - e, 1 - e)
          w = max (d + e + 2, d + 2)
          write (format, "('(F',I0,'.',I0,')')")  w, d
          write (cstr, fmt=format)  absval
       case (1:2)
          d = max (n - e - 1, -e, 0)
          w = max (d + e + 2, d + 2, e + 2)
          write (format, "('(F',I0,'.',I0,')')")  w, d
          write (cstr, fmt=format)  absval
       case default
          d = max (n - 1, 0)
          w = max (d + 2, 2)
          write (format, "('(F',I0,'.',I0,',A,I0,A)')")  w, d
          mantissa = absval * 10._default ** (- e)
          write (cstr, fmt=format)  mantissa, "\\times 10^\{", e, "\}"
       end select
       string = sign // trim (cstr)
    end if
  end function tex_format

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{86}\nwdocspar
\subsection{Metapost-compatible Output}
Write a number for use in Metapost code:
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{87}\moddef{Format utils: public}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  public :: mp_format
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{88}\moddef{Format utils: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  function mp_format (rval) result (string)
    type(string_t) :: string
    real(default), intent(in) :: rval
    character(16) :: tmp
    write (tmp, "(G16.8)")  rval
    string = lower_case (trim (adjustl (trim (tmp))))
  end function mp_format

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{89}\nwdocspar
\subsection{Conditional Formatting}
Conditional format string, intended for switchable numeric precision.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{90}\moddef{Format utils: public}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  public :: pac_fmt
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{91}\moddef{Format utils: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine pac_fmt (fmt, fmt_orig, fmt_pac, pacify)
    character(*), intent(in) :: fmt_orig, fmt_pac
    character(*), intent(out) :: fmt
    logical, intent(in), optional :: pacify
    logical :: pacified
    pacified = .false.
    if (present (pacify))  pacified = pacify
    if (pacified) then
       fmt = fmt_pac
    else
       fmt = fmt_orig
    end if
  end subroutine pac_fmt

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{92}\nwdocspar
\subsection{Compressed output of integer arrays}
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{93}\moddef{Format utils: public}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  public :: write_compressed_integer_array
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{94}\moddef{Format utils: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine write_compressed_integer_array (chars, array)
    character(len=*), intent(out) :: chars
    integer, intent(in), allocatable, dimension(:) :: array
    logical, dimension(:), allocatable :: used
    character(len=16) :: tmp
    type(string_t) :: string
    integer :: i, j, start_chain, end_chain
    chars = '[none]'
    string = ""
    if (allocated (array)) then
       if (size (array) > 0) then
          allocate (used (size (array)))
          used = .false.
          do i = 1, size (array)
             if (.not. used(i)) then
                start_chain = array(i)
                end_chain = array(i)
                used(i) = .true.
                EXTEND: do
                   do j = 1, size (array)
                      if (array(j) == end_chain + 1) then
                         end_chain = array(j)
                         used(j) = .true.
                         cycle EXTEND
                      end if
                      if (array(j) == start_chain - 1) then
                         start_chain = array(j)
                         used(j) = .true.
                         cycle EXTEND
                      end if
                   end do
                   exit
                end do EXTEND
                if (end_chain - start_chain > 0) then
                   write (tmp, "(I0,A,I0)") start_chain, "-", end_chain
                else
                   write (tmp, "(I0)") start_chain
                end if
                string = string // trim (tmp)
                if (any (.not. used)) then
                   string = string // ','
                end if
             end if
          end do
          chars = string
       end if
    end if
    chars = adjustr (chars)
  end subroutine write_compressed_integer_array

\eatline

\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{101}\nwdocspar
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{102}\moddef{Numeric utils: public}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  public :: assert
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{103}\moddef{Numeric utils: procedures}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine assert (unit, ok, description, exit_on_fail)
    integer, intent(in) :: unit
    logical, intent(in) :: ok
    character(*), intent(in), optional :: description
    logical, intent(in), optional :: exit_on_fail
    logical :: ef
    ef = .false.;  if (present (exit_on_fail)) ef = exit_on_fail
    if (.not. ok) then
       if (present(description)) then
          write (unit, "(A)") "* FAIL: " // description
       else
          write (unit, "(A)") "* FAIL: Assertion error"
       end if
       if (ef)  stop 1
    end if
  end subroutine assert

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{104}Compare numbers and output error message if not equal.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{105}\moddef{Numeric utils: public}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  public:: assert_equal
  interface assert_equal
     module procedure assert_equal_integer, assert_equal_integers, &
            assert_equal_real, assert_equal_reals, &
            assert_equal_complex, assert_equal_complexs
  end interface

\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{106}\nwdocspar
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{107}\moddef{Numeric utils: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine assert_equal_integer (unit, lhs, rhs, description, exit_on_fail)
    integer, intent(in) :: unit
    integer, intent(in) :: lhs, rhs
    character(*), intent(in), optional :: description
    logical, intent(in), optional :: exit_on_fail
    type(string_t) :: desc
    logical :: ok
    ok = lhs == rhs
    desc = '';  if (present (description)) desc = var_str(description) // ": "
    call assert (unit, ok, char(desc // str (lhs) // " /= " // str (rhs)), exit_on_fail)
  end subroutine assert_equal_integer

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{108}\nwdocspar
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{109}\moddef{Numeric utils: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine assert_equal_integers (unit, lhs, rhs, description, exit_on_fail)
    integer, intent(in) :: unit
    integer, dimension(:), intent(in) :: lhs, rhs
    character(*), intent(in), optional :: description
    logical, intent(in), optional :: exit_on_fail
    type(string_t) :: desc
    logical :: ok
    ok = all(lhs == rhs)
    desc = '';  if (present (description)) desc = var_str(description) // ": "
    call assert (unit, ok, char(desc // str (lhs) // " /= " // str (rhs)), exit_on_fail)
  end subroutine assert_equal_integers

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{110}\nwdocspar
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{111}\moddef{Numeric utils: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine assert_equal_real (unit, lhs, rhs, description, &
                                abs_smallness, rel_smallness, exit_on_fail)
    integer, intent(in) :: unit
    real(default), intent(in) :: lhs, rhs
    character(*), intent(in), optional :: description
    real(default), intent(in), optional :: abs_smallness, rel_smallness
    logical, intent(in), optional :: exit_on_fail
    type(string_t) :: desc
    logical :: ok
    ok = nearly_equal (lhs, rhs, abs_smallness, rel_smallness)
    desc = '';  if (present (description)) desc = var_str(description) // ": "
    call assert (unit, ok, char(desc // str (lhs) // " /= " // str (rhs)), exit_on_fail)
  end subroutine assert_equal_real

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{112}\nwdocspar
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{113}\moddef{Numeric utils: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine assert_equal_reals (unit, lhs, rhs, description, &
                                abs_smallness, rel_smallness, exit_on_fail)
    integer, intent(in) :: unit
    real(default), dimension(:), intent(in) :: lhs, rhs
    character(*), intent(in), optional :: description
    real(default), intent(in), optional :: abs_smallness, rel_smallness
    logical, intent(in), optional :: exit_on_fail
    type(string_t) :: desc
    logical :: ok
    ok = all(nearly_equal (lhs, rhs, abs_smallness, rel_smallness))
    desc = '';  if (present (description)) desc = var_str(description) // ": "
    call assert (unit, ok, char(desc // str (lhs) // " /= " // str (rhs)), exit_on_fail)
  end subroutine assert_equal_reals

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{114}\nwdocspar
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{115}\moddef{Numeric utils: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine assert_equal_complex (unit, lhs, rhs, description, &
                                abs_smallness, rel_smallness, exit_on_fail)
    integer, intent(in) :: unit
    complex(default), intent(in) :: lhs, rhs
    character(*), intent(in), optional :: description
    real(default), intent(in), optional :: abs_smallness, rel_smallness
    logical, intent(in), optional :: exit_on_fail
    type(string_t) :: desc
    logical :: ok
    ok = nearly_equal (real(lhs), real(rhs), abs_smallness, rel_smallness) &
         .and. nearly_equal (aimag(lhs), aimag(rhs), abs_smallness, rel_smallness)
    desc = '';  if (present (description)) desc = var_str(description) // ": "
    call assert (unit, ok, char(desc // str (lhs) // " /= " // str (rhs)), exit_on_fail)
  end subroutine assert_equal_complex

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{116}\nwdocspar
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{117}\moddef{Numeric utils: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine assert_equal_complexs (unit, lhs, rhs, description, &
                                abs_smallness, rel_smallness, exit_on_fail)
    integer, intent(in) :: unit
    complex(default), dimension(:), intent(in) :: lhs, rhs
    character(*), intent(in), optional :: description
    real(default), intent(in), optional :: abs_smallness, rel_smallness
    logical, intent(in), optional :: exit_on_fail
    type(string_t) :: desc
    logical :: ok
    ok = all (nearly_equal (real(lhs), real(rhs), abs_smallness, rel_smallness)) &
         .and. all (nearly_equal (aimag(lhs), aimag(rhs), abs_smallness, rel_smallness))
    desc = '';  if (present (description)) desc = var_str(description) // ": "
    call assert (unit, ok, char(desc // str (lhs) // " /= " // str (rhs)), exit_on_fail)
  end subroutine assert_equal_complexs

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{118}Note that this poor man's check will be disabled if someone compiles
with {\Tt{}-ffast-math\nwendquote} or similar optimizations.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{119}\moddef{Numeric utils: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  elemental function ieee_is_nan (x) result (yorn)
    logical :: yorn
    real(default), intent(in) :: x
    yorn = (x /= x)
  end function ieee_is_nan

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{120}This is still not perfect but should work in most cases.  Usually one
wants to compare to a relative epsilon {\Tt{}rel{\_}smallness\nwendquote}, except for
numbers close to zero defined by {\Tt{}abs{\_}smallness\nwendquote}.  Both might need
adaption to specific use cases but have reasonable defaults.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{121}\moddef{Numeric utils: public}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  public :: nearly_equal
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{122}\moddef{Numeric utils: interfaces}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  interface nearly_equal
     module procedure nearly_equal_real
     module procedure nearly_equal_complex
  end interface nearly_equal

\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{123}\moddef{Numeric utils: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  elemental function nearly_equal_real (a, b, abs_smallness, rel_smallness) result (r)
    logical :: r
    real(default), intent(in) :: a, b
    real(default), intent(in), optional :: abs_smallness, rel_smallness
    real(default) :: abs_a, abs_b, diff, abs_small, rel_small
    abs_a = abs (a)
    abs_b = abs (b)
    diff = abs (a - b)
    ! shortcut, handles infinities and nans
    if (a == b) then
       r = .true.
       return
    else if (ieee_is_nan (a) .or. ieee_is_nan (b) .or. ieee_is_nan (diff)) then
       r = .false.
       return
    end if
    abs_small = tiny_13; if (present (abs_smallness)) abs_small = abs_smallness
    rel_small = tiny_10; if (present (rel_smallness)) rel_small = rel_smallness
    if (abs_a < abs_small .and. abs_b < abs_small) then
       r = diff < abs_small
    else
       r = diff / max (abs_a, abs_b) < rel_small
    end if
  end function nearly_equal_real

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{124}\moddef{Numeric utils: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  elemental function nearly_equal_complex (a, b, abs_smallness, rel_smallness) result (r)
    logical :: r
    complex(default), intent(in) :: a, b
    real(default), intent(in), optional :: abs_smallness, rel_smallness
    r = nearly_equal_real (real (a), real (b), abs_smallness, rel_smallness) .and. &
        nearly_equal_real (aimag (a), aimag(b), abs_smallness, rel_smallness)
  end function nearly_equal_complex

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{125}Often we will need to check whether floats vanish:
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{126}\moddef{Numeric utils: public}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  public:: vanishes
  interface vanishes
     module procedure vanishes_real, vanishes_complex
  end interface
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{127}\nwdocspar
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{128}\moddef{Numeric utils: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  elemental function vanishes_real (x, abs_smallness, rel_smallness) result (r)
    logical :: r
    real(default), intent(in) :: x
    real(default), intent(in), optional :: abs_smallness, rel_smallness
    r = nearly_equal (x, zero, abs_smallness, rel_smallness)
  end function vanishes_real

  elemental function vanishes_complex (x, abs_smallness, rel_smallness) result (r)
    logical :: r
    complex(default), intent(in) :: x
    real(default), intent(in), optional :: abs_smallness, rel_smallness
    r = vanishes_real (abs (x), abs_smallness, rel_smallness)
  end function vanishes_complex

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{129}\nwdocspar
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{130}\moddef{Numeric utils: public}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  public :: expanded_amp2
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{131}\moddef{Numeric utils: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  pure function expanded_amp2 (amp_tree, amp_blob) result (amp2)
    real(default) :: amp2
    complex(default), dimension(:), intent(in) :: amp_tree, amp_blob
    amp2 = sum (amp_tree * conjg (amp_tree) + &
                amp_tree * conjg (amp_blob) + &
                amp_blob * conjg (amp_tree))
  end function expanded_amp2

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{132}\nwdocspar
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{133}\moddef{Numeric utils: public}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  public :: abs2
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{134}\moddef{Numeric utils: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  elemental function abs2 (c) result (c2)
    real(default) :: c2
    complex(default), intent(in) :: c
    c2 = real (c * conjg(c))
  end function abs2

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{135}Remove all duplicates from a list of integers.
This method does not really fit into this module. It could be part of a
larger module which deals with list manipulations.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{136}\moddef{Numeric utils: public}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  public :: remove_duplicates_from_list
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{137}\moddef{Numeric utils: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  function remove_duplicates_from_list (list) result (list_clean)
    integer, dimension(:), allocatable :: list_clean
    integer, intent(in), dimension(:) :: list
    integer, parameter :: N_MAX = 20
    integer, dimension(N_MAX) :: buf
    integer :: i_buf, i_list, n_buf
    buf = -1; i_buf = 1
    if (size (list) > N_MAX) return
    do i_list = 1, size (list)
       if (.not. any (list(i_list) == buf)) then
          buf(i_buf) = list(i_list)
          i_buf = i_buf + 1
       end if
    end do
    n_buf = count (buf >= 0)
    allocate (list_clean (n_buf))
    list_clean = buf (1 : n_buf)
  end function remove_duplicates_from_list

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{138}\nwdocspar
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{139}\moddef{Numeric utils: public}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  public :: extend_integer_array
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{140}\moddef{Numeric utils: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine extend_integer_array (list, incr, initial_value)
    integer, intent(inout), dimension(:), allocatable :: list
    integer, intent(in) :: incr
    integer, intent(in), optional :: initial_value
    integer, dimension(:), allocatable :: list_store
    integer :: n, ini
    ini = 0; if (present (initial_value)) ini = initial_value
    n = size (list)
    allocate (list_store (n))
    list_store = list
    deallocate (list)
    allocate (list (n+incr))
    list(1:n) = list_store
    list(1+n : n+incr) = ini
    deallocate (list_store)
  end subroutine extend_integer_array

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{141}\nwdocspar
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{142}\moddef{Numeric utils: public}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  public :: crop_integer_array
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{143}\moddef{Numeric utils: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine crop_integer_array (list, i_crop)
    integer, intent(inout), dimension(:), allocatable :: list
    integer, intent(in) :: i_crop
    integer, dimension(:), allocatable :: list_store
    allocate (list_store (i_crop))
    list_store = list(1:i_crop)
    deallocate (list)
    allocate (list (i_crop))
    list = list_store
    deallocate (list_store)
  end subroutine crop_integer_array

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{144}\nwdocspar

% WHIZARD code as NOWEB source
\chapter{Testing}
\includemodulegraph{testing}

This part contains tools for automatic testing.
\begin{description}
\item[unit\_tests]
  A handler that executes test procedures and compares and collects results.
\end{description}

%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\section{Unit tests}
We provide functionality for automated unit tests.  Each test is
required to produce output which is compared against a reference
file.  If the two are identical, we signal success.  Otherwise, we
signal failure and write the output to a file.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{1}\moddef{\code{}unit{\_}tests.f90\edoc{}}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
\LA{}File header\RA{}

module unit_tests

\LA{}Use strings\RA{}
  use io_units

\LA{}Standard module head\RA{}

\LA{}Tests: public\RA{}

\LA{}Tests: parameters\RA{}

\LA{}Tests: types\RA{}

\LA{}Tests: interfaces\RA{}

contains

\LA{}Tests: procedures\RA{}

end module unit_tests
\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{2}\nwdocspar
\subsection{Parameters}
Building blocks of file names.  The directory names and suffixes are
hard-coded here, and they must reflect actual Makefile targets where
applicable.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{3}\moddef{Tests: parameters}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  character(*), parameter :: ref_prefix = "ref-output/"
  character(*), parameter :: ref = ".ref"

  character(*), parameter :: err_prefix = "err-output/"
  character(*), parameter :: err = ".out"

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{4}\nwdocspar
\subsection{Type for storing test results}
We store the results of the individual unit tests in a linked list.
Here is the entry:
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{5}\moddef{Tests: public}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  public :: test_results_t
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{6}\moddef{Tests: types}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  type :: test_result_t
     logical :: success = .false.
     type(string_t) :: name
     type(string_t) :: description
     type(test_result_t), pointer :: next => null ()
  end type test_result_t

  type :: test_results_t
     private
     type(test_result_t), pointer :: first => null ()
     type(test_result_t), pointer :: last => null ()
     integer :: n_success = 0
     integer :: n_failure = 0
   contains
   \LA{}Tests: test results: TBP\RA{}
  end type test_results_t

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{7}Add a test result.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{8}\moddef{Tests: test results: TBP}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure, private :: add => test_results_add
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{9}\moddef{Tests: procedures}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine test_results_add (list, name, description, success)
    class(test_results_t), intent(inout) :: list
    character(len=*), intent(in) :: name
    character(len=*), intent(in) :: description
    logical, intent(in) :: success
    type(test_result_t), pointer :: result
    allocate (result)
    result%success = success
    result%name = name
    result%description = description
    if (associated (list%first)) then
       list%last%next => result
    else
       list%first => result
    end if
    list%last => result
    if (success) then
       list%n_success = list%n_success + 1
    else
       list%n_failure = list%n_failure + 1
    end if
  end subroutine test_results_add

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{10}Display the current state.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{11}\moddef{Tests: test results: TBP}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure, private :: write => test_results_write
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{12}\moddef{Tests: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine test_results_write (list, u)
    class(test_results_t), intent(in) :: list
    integer, intent(in) :: u
    type(test_result_t), pointer :: result
    write (u, "(A)")  "*** Test Summary ***"
    if (list%n_success > 0) then
       write (u, "(2x,A)")  "Success:"
       result => list%first
       do while (associated (result))
          if (result%success)  write (u, "(4x,A,': ',A)")  &
               char (result%name), char (result%description)
          result => result%next
       end do
    end if
    if (list%n_failure > 0) then
       write (u, "(2x,A)")  "Failure:"
       result => list%first
       do while (associated (result))
          if (.not. result%success)  write (u, "(4x,A,': ',A)")  &
               char (result%name), char (result%description)
          result => result%next
       end do
    end if
    write (u, "(A,I0)")  "Total   = ", list%n_success + list%n_failure
    write (u, "(A,I0)")  "Success = ", list%n_success
    write (u, "(A,I0)")  "Failure = ", list%n_failure
    write (u, "(A)")  "*** End of test Summary ***"
  end subroutine test_results_write

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{13}Return true if all tests were successful (or no test).
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{14}\moddef{Tests: test results: TBP}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure, private :: report => test_results_report
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{15}\moddef{Tests: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine test_results_report (list, success)
    class(test_results_t), intent(in) :: list
    logical, intent(out) :: success
    success = list%n_failure == 0
  end subroutine test_results_report

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{16}Delete the list.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{17}\moddef{Tests: test results: TBP}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure, private :: final => test_results_final
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{18}\moddef{Tests: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine test_results_final (list)
    class(test_results_t), intent(inout) :: list
    type(test_result_t), pointer :: result
    do while (associated (list%first))
       result => list%first
       list%first => result%next
       deallocate (result)
    end do
    list%last => null ()
    list%n_success = 0
    list%n_failure = 0
  end subroutine test_results_final

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{19}\nwdocspar
\subsection{Wrapup}
This will write results, report status, and finalize.  This is the
only method which we need to access from outside.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{20}\moddef{Tests: test results: TBP}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure :: wrapup => test_results_wrapup
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{21}\moddef{Tests: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine test_results_wrapup (list, u, success)
    class(test_results_t), intent(inout) :: list
    integer, intent(in) :: u
    logical, intent(out), optional :: success
    call list%write (u)
    if (present (success))  call list%report (success)
    call list%final ()
  end subroutine test_results_wrapup

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{22}\nwdocspar
\subsection{Tool for Unit Tests}
This procedure takes a test routine as an argument.  It runs the test,
output directed to a temporary file.  Then, it compares the file
against a reference file.

The test routine must take the output unit as argument.  We export
this abstract interface, so the test drivers can reference it for
declaring the actual test routines.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{23}\moddef{Tests: public}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  public :: unit_test
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{24}\moddef{Tests: interfaces}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  abstract interface
     subroutine unit_test (u)
       integer, intent(in) :: u
     end subroutine unit_test
  end interface

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{25}The test routine can print to screen and, optionally, to a logging unit.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{26}\moddef{Tests: public}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  public :: test
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{27}\moddef{Tests: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine test (test_proc, name, description, u_log, results)
    procedure(unit_test) :: test_proc
    character(*), intent(in) :: name
    character(*), intent(in) :: description
    integer, intent(in) :: u_log
    type(test_results_t), intent(inout) :: results
    integer :: u_test, u_ref, u_err
    logical :: exist
    character(256) :: buffer1, buffer2
    integer :: iostat1, iostat2
    logical :: success
    write (*, "(A)", advance="no")  "Running test: " // name
    write (u_log, "(A)")  "Test: " // name
    u_test = free_unit ()
    open (u_test, status="scratch", action="readwrite")
    call test_proc (u_test)
    rewind (u_test)
    inquire (file=ref_prefix//name//ref, exist=exist)
    if (exist) then
       u_ref = free_unit ()
       open (u_ref, file=ref_prefix//name//ref, status="old", action="read")
       COMPARE_FILES: do
          read (u_test, "(A)", iostat=iostat1)  buffer1
          read (u_ref, "(A)", iostat=iostat2)  buffer2
          if (iostat1 /= iostat2) then
             success = .false.
             exit COMPARE_FILES
          else if (iostat1 < 0) then
             success = .true.
             exit COMPARE_FILES
          else if (buffer1 /= buffer2) then
             success = .false.
             exit COMPARE_FILES
          end if
       end do COMPARE_FILES
       close (u_ref)
    else
       write (*, "(A)", advance="no") " ... no reference output available"
       write (u_log, "(A)") "  No reference output available."
       success = .false.
    end if
    if (success) then
       write (*, "(A)") " ... success."
       write (u_log, "(A)")  "  Success."
    else
       write (*, "(A)") " ... failure.  See: " // err_prefix//name//err
       write (u_log, "(A)")  "  Failure."
       rewind (u_test)
       u_err = free_unit ()
       open (u_err, file=err_prefix//name//err, &
            action="write", status="replace")
       WRITE_OUTPUT: do
          read (u_test, "(A)", end=1) buffer1
          write (u_err, "(A)")  trim (buffer1)
       end do WRITE_OUTPUT
1      close (u_err)
    end if
    close (u_test)
    call results%add (name, description, success)
  end subroutine test

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwfilename{../../../src/system/system.nw}\nwbegindocs{0}% -*- ess-noweb-default-code-mode: f90-mode; noweb-default-code-mode: f90-mode; -*-

\chapter{System: Interfaces and Handlers}
\includemodulegraph{system}

Here, we collect modules that deal with the ``system'':
operating-system interfaces, error handlers and diagnostics.
\begin{description}
\item[system\_defs]
  Constants relevant for the modules in this set.
\item[diagnostics]
  Error and diagnostic message handling.  Any
  messages and errors issued by WHIZARD functions are handled by the
  subroutines in this module, if possible.
\item[os\_interface]
  Execute system calls, build and link external object files and libraries.
\item[cputime]
  Timer data type and methods, for measuring performance.
\end{description}

%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\section{Constants}
The parameters here are used in various parts of the program,
starting from the modules in the current chapter.  Some of them may be
modified if the need arises.

\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{12}\nwdocspar
%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\section{C wrapper for sigaction}
This implements calls to {\Tt{}sigaction\nwendquote} and the appropriate signal handlers in
C.  The functionality is needed for the {\Tt{}diagnostics\nwendquote} module.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{13}\moddef{\code{}signal{\_}interface.c\edoc{}}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
/*
\LA{}File header\RA{}
*/
#include <signal.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

extern int wo_sigint;
extern int wo_sigterm;
extern int wo_sigxcpu;
extern int wo_sigxfsz;

static void wo_handler_sigint (int sig) \{
  wo_sigint = sig;
\}

static void wo_handler_sigterm (int sig) \{
  wo_sigterm = sig;
\}

static void wo_handler_sigxcpu (int sig) \{
  wo_sigxcpu = sig;
\}

static void wo_handler_sigxfsz (int sig) \{
  wo_sigxfsz = sig;
\}

int wo_mask_sigint () \{
  struct sigaction sa;
  sigset_t blocks;
  sigfillset (&blocks);
  sa.sa_flags = 0;
  sa.sa_mask = blocks;
  sa.sa_handler = wo_handler_sigint;
  return sigaction(SIGINT, &sa, NULL);
\}

int wo_mask_sigterm () \{
  struct sigaction sa;
  sigset_t blocks;
  sigfillset (&blocks);
  sa.sa_flags = 0;
  sa.sa_mask = blocks;
  sa.sa_handler = wo_handler_sigterm;
  return sigaction(SIGTERM, &sa, NULL);
\}

int wo_mask_sigxcpu () \{
  struct sigaction sa;
  sigset_t blocks;
  sigfillset (&blocks);
  sa.sa_flags = 0;
  sa.sa_mask = blocks;
  sa.sa_handler = wo_handler_sigxcpu;
  return sigaction(SIGXCPU, &sa, NULL);
\}

int wo_mask_sigxfsz () \{
  struct sigaction sa;
  sigset_t blocks;
  sigfillset (&blocks);
  sa.sa_flags = 0;
  sa.sa_mask = blocks;
  sa.sa_handler = wo_handler_sigxfsz;
  return sigaction(SIGXFSZ, &sa, NULL);
\}

int wo_release_sigint () \{
  struct sigaction sa;
  sigset_t blocks;
  sigfillset (&blocks);
  sa.sa_flags = 0;
  sa.sa_mask = blocks;
  sa.sa_handler = SIG_DFL;
  return sigaction(SIGINT, &sa, NULL);
\}

int wo_release_sigterm () \{
  struct sigaction sa;
  sigset_t blocks;
  sigfillset (&blocks);
  sa.sa_flags = 0;
  sa.sa_mask = blocks;
  sa.sa_handler = SIG_DFL;
  return sigaction(SIGTERM, &sa, NULL);
\}

int wo_release_sigxcpu () \{
  struct sigaction sa;
  sigset_t blocks;
  sigfillset (&blocks);
  sa.sa_flags = 0;
  sa.sa_mask = blocks;
  sa.sa_handler = SIG_DFL;
  return sigaction(SIGXCPU, &sa, NULL);
\}

int wo_release_sigxfsz () \{
  struct sigaction sa;
  sigset_t blocks;
  sigfillset (&blocks);
  sa.sa_flags = 0;
  sa.sa_mask = blocks;
  sa.sa_handler = SIG_DFL;
  return sigaction(SIGXFSZ, &sa, NULL);
\}
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{14}\nwdocspar
%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\section{C wrapper for printf}
The {\Tt{}printf\nwendquote} family of functions is implemented in C with an undefined
number of arguments.  This is not supported by the {\Tt{}bind(C)\nwendquote} interface.  We
therefore write wrappers for the versions of {\Tt{}sprintf\nwendquote} that
we will actually use.

This is used by the {\Tt{}formats\nwendquote} module.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{15}\moddef{\code{}sprintf{\_}interface.c\edoc{}}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
/*
\LA{}File header\RA{}
*/
#include <stdio.h>

int sprintf_none(char* str, const char* format) \{
  return sprintf(str, format);
\}

int sprintf_int(char* str, const char* format, int val) \{
  return sprintf(str, format, val);
\}

int sprintf_double(char* str, const char* format, double val) \{
  return sprintf(str, format, val);
\}

int sprintf_str(char* str, const char* format, const char* val) \{
  return sprintf(str, format, val);
\}

\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{16}\moddef{sprintf interfaces}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  interface
    function sprintf_none (str, fmt) result (stat) bind(C)
      use iso_c_binding !NODEP!
      integer(c_int) :: stat
      character(c_char), dimension(*), intent(inout) :: str
      character(c_char), dimension(*), intent(in) :: fmt
    end function sprintf_none
  end interface

  interface
    function sprintf_int (str, fmt, val) result (stat) bind(C)
      use iso_c_binding !NODEP!
      integer(c_int) :: stat
      character(c_char), dimension(*), intent(inout) :: str
      character(c_char), dimension(*), intent(in) :: fmt
      integer(c_int), value :: val
    end function sprintf_int
  end interface

  interface
    function sprintf_double (str, fmt, val) result (stat) bind(C)
      use iso_c_binding !NODEP!
      integer(c_int) :: stat
      character(c_char), dimension(*), intent(inout) :: str
      character(c_char), dimension(*), intent(in) :: fmt
      real(c_double), value :: val
    end function sprintf_double
  end interface

  interface
    function sprintf_str(str, fmt, val) result (stat) bind(C)
      use iso_c_binding !NODEP!
      integer(c_int) :: stat
      character(c_char), dimension(*), intent(inout) :: str
      character(c_char), dimension(*), intent(in) :: fmt
      character(c_char), dimension(*), intent(in) :: val
    end function sprintf_str
  end interface

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{17}\nwdocspar
%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\section{Error, Message and Signal Handling}
We are not so ambitious as to do proper exception handling in
{\Tt{}WHIZARD\nwendquote}, but at least it may be useful to have a common interface
for diagnostics: Results, messages, warnings, and such.  As module
variables we keep a buffer where the current message may be written to
and a level indicator which tells which messages should be written on
screen and which ones should be skipped.  Alternatively, a string may
be directly supplied to the message routine: this overrides the
buffer, avoiding the necessety of formatted I/O in trivial cases.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{18}\moddef{\code{}diagnostics.f90\edoc{}}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
\LA{}File header\RA{}

module diagnostics

  use, intrinsic :: iso_c_binding !NODEP!
  use, intrinsic :: iso_fortran_env, only: output_unit !NODEP!

\LA{}Use kinds\RA{}
\LA{}Use strings\RA{}
  use string_utils, only: str
  use io_units

  use system_dependencies
  use system_defs, only: BUFFER_SIZE, MAX_ERRORS

\LA{}Standard module head\RA{}

\LA{}Diagnostics: public\RA{}

\LA{}Diagnostics: parameters\RA{}

\LA{}Diagnostics: types\RA{}

\LA{}Diagnostics: variables\RA{}

\LA{}Diagnostics: interfaces\RA{}

contains

\LA{}Diagnostics: procedures\RA{}

end module diagnostics
\eatline

  function d_area_of_string (string) result (i)
    integer :: i
    type(string_t), intent(in) :: string
    select case (char (string))
    case ("particles")
       i = D_PARTICLES
    case ("events")
       i = D_EVENTS
    case ("shower")
       i = D_SHOWER
    case ("model_features")
       i = D_MODEL_F
    case ("matching")
       i = D_MATCHING
    case ("transforms")
       i = D_TRANSFORMS
    case ("subtraction")
       i = D_SUBTRACTION
    case ("virtual")
       i = D_VIRTUAL
    case ("threshold")
       i = D_THRESHOLD
    case ("phasespace")
       i = D_PHASESPACE
    case ("mismatch")
       i = D_MISMATCH
    case ("me_methods")
       i = D_ME_METHODS
    case ("process_integration")
       i = D_PROCESS_INTEGRATION
    case ("tauola")
       i = D_TAUOLA
    case ("core")
       i = D_CORE
    case default
       print "(A)", "Possible values for --debug are:"
       do i = 1, D_LAST
          print "(A)", char ('  ' // d_area_to_string(i))
       end do
       call msg_fatal ("Please use one of the listed areas")
    end select
  end function d_area_of_string

  elemental function d_area_to_string (i) result (string)
    type(string_t) :: string
    integer, intent(in) :: i
    select case (i)
    case (D_PARTICLES)
       string = "particles"
    case (D_EVENTS)
       string = "events"
    case (D_SHOWER)
       string = "shower"
    case (D_MODEL_F)
       string = "model_features"
    case (D_MATCHING)
       string = "matching"
    case (D_TRANSFORMS)
       string = "transforms"
    case (D_SUBTRACTION)
       string = "subtraction"
    case (D_VIRTUAL)
       string = "virtual"
    case (D_THRESHOLD)
       string = "threshold"
    case (D_PHASESPACE)
       string = "phasespace"
    case (D_MISMATCH)
       string = "mismatch"
    case (D_ME_METHODS)
       string = "me_methods"
    case (D_PROCESS_INTEGRATION)
       string = "process_integration"
    case (D_TAUOLA)
       string = "tauola"
    case (D_CORE)
       string = "core"
    case default
       string = "undefined"
    end select
  end function d_area_to_string

\eatline

  function term_col_int (col_int) result (color)
    type(terminal_color_t) :: color
    integer, intent(in) :: col_int
    color%color = col_int
  end function term_col_int

  function term_col_char (col_char) result (color)
    type(terminal_color_t) :: color
    character(len=*), intent(in) :: col_char
    type(string_t) :: buf
    select case (col_char)
    case ('Grey')
       color%color = COL_GREY
    case ('Peach')
       color%color = COL_PEACH
    case ('Light Green')
       color%color = COL_LIGHT_GREEN
    case ('Light Yellow')
       color%color = COL_LIGHT_YELLOW
    case ('Light Blue')
       color%color = COL_LIGHT_BLUE
    case ('Pink')
       color%color = COL_PINK
    case ('Light Aqua')
       color%color = COL_LIGHT_AQUA
    case ('Pearl White')
       color%color = COL_PEARL_WHITE
    case ('Black')
       color%color = COL_BLACK
    case ('Red')
       color%color = COL_RED
    case ('Green')
       color%color = COL_GREEN
    case ('Yellow')
       color%color = COL_YELLOW
    case ('Blue')
       color%color = COL_BLUE
    case ('Purple')
       color%color = COL_PURPLE
    case ('Aqua')
       color%color = COL_AQUA
    case default
       buf = var_str ('Color ') // var_str (col_char) // var_str (' is not defined')
       call msg_warning (char (buf))
       color%color = COL_UNDEFINED
    end select
  end function term_col_char

\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{47}\nwdocspar
Keep track of errors.  This might be used for exception handling,
later.  The counter is incremented only for screen messages, to avoid
double counting.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{48}\moddef{Diagnostics: public}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  public :: msg_count
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{49}\moddef{Diagnostics: variables}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  integer, dimension(TERMINATE:WARNING), save :: msg_count = 0
\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{50}Keep a list of all errors and warnings.  Since we do not know the number of
entries beforehand, we use a linked list.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{51}\moddef{Diagnostics: types}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  type :: string_list
     character(len=BUFFER_SIZE) :: string
     type(string_list), pointer :: next
  end type string_list
  type :: string_list_pointer
     type(string_list), pointer :: first, last
  end type string_list_pointer

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{52}\moddef{Diagnostics: variables}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup

       & msg_list = string_list_pointer (null(), null())
\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{53}Create a format string indicating color

\nwenddocs{}\nwbegindocs{54}Add the current message buffer contents to the internal list.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{55}\moddef{Diagnostics: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine msg_add (level)
    integer, intent(in) :: level
    type(string_list), pointer :: message
    select case (level)
    case (TERMINATE:WARNING)
       allocate (message)
       message%string = msg_buffer
       nullify (message%next)
       if (.not.associated (msg_list(level)%first)) &
            & msg_list(level)%first => message
       if (associated (msg_list(level)%last)) &
            & msg_list(level)%last%next => message
       msg_list(level)%last => message
       msg_count(level) = msg_count(level) + 1
    end select
  end subroutine msg_add

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{56}\nwdocspar
Initialization:
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{57}\moddef{Diagnostics: public}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  public :: msg_list_clear
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{58}\moddef{Diagnostics: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine msg_list_clear
    integer :: level
    type(string_list), pointer :: message
    do level = TERMINATE, WARNING
       do while (associated (msg_list(level)%first))
          message => msg_list(level)%first
          msg_list(level)%first => message%next
          deallocate (message)
       end do
       nullify (msg_list(level)%last)
    end do
    msg_count = 0
  end subroutine msg_list_clear

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{59}Display the summary of errors and warnings (no need to count
fatals\ldots)
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{60}\moddef{Diagnostics: public}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  public :: msg_summary
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{61}\moddef{Diagnostics: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine msg_summary (unit)
    integer, intent(in), optional :: unit
    call expect_summary (unit)
1   format (A,1x,I2,1x,A,I2,1x,A)
    if (msg_count(ERROR) > 0 .and. msg_count(WARNING) > 0) then
       write (msg_buffer, 1) "There were", &
            & msg_count(ERROR), "error(s) and  ", &
            & msg_count(WARNING), "warning(s)."
       call msg_message (unit=unit)
    else if (msg_count(ERROR) > 0) then
       write (msg_buffer, 1) "There were", &
            & msg_count(ERROR), "error(s) and no warnings."
       call msg_message (unit=unit)
    else if (msg_count(WARNING) > 0) then
       write (msg_buffer, 1) "There were no errors and  ", &
            & msg_count(WARNING), "warning(s)."
       call msg_message (unit=unit)
    end if
  end subroutine msg_summary

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{62}Print the list of all messages of a given level.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{63}\moddef{Diagnostics: public}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  public :: msg_listing
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{64}\moddef{Diagnostics: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine msg_listing (level, unit, prefix)
    integer, intent(in) :: level
    integer, intent(in), optional :: unit
    character(len=*), intent(in), optional :: prefix
    type(string_list), pointer :: message
    integer :: u
    u = given_output_unit (unit);  if (u < 0)  return
    if (present (unit))  u = unit
    message => msg_list(level)%first
    do while (associated (message))
       if (present (prefix)) then
          write (u, "(A)") prefix // trim (message%string)
       else
          write (u, "(A)") trim (message%string)
       end if
       message => message%next
    end do
    flush (u)
  end subroutine msg_listing

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{65}The message buffer:
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{66}\moddef{Diagnostics: public}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
