% WHIZARD code as NOWEB source: combinatorics and such
\chapter{Combinatorics}
\includemodulegraph{combinatorics}

These modules implement standard algorithms (sorting, hashing, etc.)
that are not available in Fortran.

Fortran doesn't support generic programming, therefore the algorithms
are implemented only for specific data types.
\begin{description}
\item[bytes]
  Derived types for bytes and words.
\item[hashes]
  Types and tools for setting up hashtables.
\item[md5]
  The MD5 algorithm for message digest.
\item[permutations]
  Permuting an array of integers.
\item[sorting]
  Sorting integer and real values.
\item[grids]
  $d$-dimensional grids can be saved to disk and used for interpolation,
  maximum finding, etc.
\end{description}


%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\section{Bytes and such}
In a few instances we will need the notion of a byte (8-bit) and a word
(32 bit), even a 64-bit word.  A block of 512 bit is also needed (for
MD5).

We rely on integers up to 64 bit being supported by the processor.
The main difference to standard integers is the interpretation as
unsigned integers.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{1}\moddef{\code{}bytes.f90\edoc{}}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
\LA{}File header\RA{}

module bytes

  use kinds, only: i8, i32, i64
  use io_units

\LA{}Standard module head\RA{}

\LA{}Bytes: public\RA{}

\LA{}Bytes: types\RA{}

\LA{}Bytes: parameters\RA{}

\LA{}Bytes: interfaces\RA{}

contains

\LA{}Bytes: procedures\RA{}

end module bytes
\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{2}\nwdocspar
\subsection{8-bit words: bytes}
This is essentially a wrapper around 8-bit integers.  The wrapper
emphasises their special interpretation as a sequence of bits.
However, we interpret bytes as unsigned integers.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{3}\moddef{Bytes: public}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  public :: byte_t
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{4}\moddef{Bytes: types}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  type :: byte_t
     private
     integer(i8) :: i
  end type byte_t

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{5}\moddef{Bytes: public}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  public :: byte_zero
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{6}\moddef{Bytes: parameters}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  type(byte_t), parameter :: byte_zero = byte_t (0_i8)

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{7}Set a byte from 8-bit integer:
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{8}\moddef{Bytes: public}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  public :: assignment(=)
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{9}\moddef{Bytes: interfaces}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  interface assignment(=)
     module procedure set_byte_from_i8
  end interface
\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{10}\moddef{Bytes: procedures}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine set_byte_from_i8 (b, i)
    type(byte_t), intent(out) :: b
    integer(i8), intent(in) :: i
    b%i = i
  end subroutine set_byte_from_i8

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{11}Write a byte in one of two formats: either as a hexadecimal number
(two digits, default) or as a decimal number (one to three digits).
The decimal version is nontrivial because bytes are unsigned integers.
Optionally append a newline.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{12}\moddef{Bytes: public}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  public :: byte_write
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{13}\moddef{Bytes: interfaces}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  interface byte_write
     module procedure byte_write_unit, byte_write_string
  end interface
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{14}\moddef{Bytes: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine byte_write_unit (b, unit, decimal, newline)
    type(byte_t), intent(in), optional :: b
    integer, intent(in), optional :: unit
    logical, intent(in), optional :: decimal, newline
    logical :: dc, nl
    type(word32_t) :: w
    integer :: u
    u = given_output_unit (unit);  if (u < 0)  return
    dc = .false.;  if (present (decimal))  dc = decimal
    nl = .false.;  if (present (newline))  nl = newline
    if (dc) then
       w = b
       write (u, '(I3)', advance='no')  w%i
    else
       write (u, '(z2.2)', advance='no')  b%i
    end if
    if (nl) write (u, *)
  end subroutine byte_write_unit

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{15}The string version is hex-only
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{16}\moddef{Bytes: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine byte_write_string (b, s)
    type(byte_t), intent(in) :: b
    character(len=2), intent(inout) :: s
    write (s, '(z2.2)')  b%i
  end subroutine byte_write_string

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{17}\nwdocspar
\subsection{32-bit words}
This is not exactly a 32-bit integer.  A word is to be filled with
bytes, and it may be partially filled.  The filling is done lowest-byte
first, highest-byte last.  We count the bits, so {\Tt{}fill\nwendquote} should be
either 0, 8, 16, 24, or 32.
In printing words, we correspondingly
distinguish between printing zeros and printing blanks.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{18}\moddef{Bytes: public}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  public :: word32_t
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{19}\moddef{Bytes: types}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  type :: word32_t
     private
     integer(i32) :: i
     integer :: fill = 0
  end type word32_t

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{20}Assignment: the word is filled by inserting a 32-bit integer
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{21}\moddef{Bytes: interfaces}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  interface assignment(=)
     module procedure word32_set_from_i32
     module procedure word32_set_from_byte
  end interface
\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{22}\moddef{Bytes: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine word32_set_from_i32 (w, i)
    type(word32_t), intent(out) :: w
    integer(i32), intent(in) :: i
    w%i = i
    w%fill = 32
  end subroutine word32_set_from_i32

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{23}Reverse assignment to a 32-bit integer.  We do not check the fill
status.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{24}\moddef{Bytes: interfaces}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  interface assignment(=)
     module procedure i32_from_word32
  end interface
\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{25}\moddef{Bytes: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine i32_from_word32 (i, w)
    integer(i32), intent(out) :: i
    type(word32_t), intent(in) :: w
    i = w%i
  end subroutine i32_from_word32

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{26}Filling with a 8-bit integer is slightly tricky, because in this
interpretation integers are unsigned.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{27}\moddef{Bytes: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine word32_set_from_byte (w, b)
    type(word32_t), intent(out) :: w
    type(byte_t), intent(in) :: b
    if (b%i >= 0_i8) then
       w%i = b%i
    else
       w%i = 2_i32*(huge(0_i8)+1_i32) + b%i
    end if
    w%fill = 32
  end subroutine word32_set_from_byte

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{28}Check the fill status
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{29}\moddef{Bytes: public}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  public :: word32_empty, word32_filled, word32_fill
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{30}\moddef{Bytes: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  function word32_empty (w)
    type(word32_t), intent(in) :: w
    logical :: word32_empty
    word32_empty = (w%fill == 0)
  end function word32_empty

  function word32_filled (w)
    type(word32_t), intent(in) :: w
    logical :: word32_filled
    word32_filled = (w%fill == 32)
  end function word32_filled

  function word32_fill (w)
    type(word32_t), intent(in) :: w
    integer :: word32_fill
    word32_fill = w%fill
  end function word32_fill

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{31}Partial assignment: append a byte to a partially filled word.
(Note: no assignment if the word is filled, so check this before if
necessary.)
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{32}\moddef{Bytes: public}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  public :: word32_append_byte
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{33}\moddef{Bytes: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine word32_append_byte (w, b)
    type(word32_t), intent(inout) :: w
    type(byte_t), intent(in) :: b
    type(word32_t) :: w1
    if (.not. word32_filled (w)) then
       w1 = b
       call mvbits (w1%i, 0, 8, w%i, w%fill)
       w%fill = w%fill + 8
    end if
  end subroutine word32_append_byte

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{34}Extract a byte from a word.  The argument {\Tt{}i\nwendquote} is the position,
which may be 0, 1, 2, or 3.

For the final assignment, we set the highest bit separately.
Otherwise, we might trigger an overflow condition for a compiler with
strict checking turned on.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{35}\moddef{Bytes: public}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  public :: byte_from_word32
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{36}\moddef{Bytes: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  function byte_from_word32 (w, i) result (b)
    type(word32_t), intent(in) :: w
    integer, intent(in) :: i
    type(byte_t) :: b
    integer(i32) :: j
    j = 0
    if (i >= 0 .and. i*8 < w%fill) then
       call mvbits (w%i, i*8, 8, j, 0)
    end if
    b%i = int (ibclr (j, 7), kind=i8)
    if (btest (j, 7))  b%i = ibset (b%i, 7)
  end function byte_from_word32

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{37}Write a word to file or STDOUT.  We understand words as unsigned
integers, therefore we cannot use the built-in routine unchanged.
However, we can make use of the existence of 64-bit integers and their
output routine.

In hexadecimal format, the default version prints eight hex
characters, highest-first.  The {\Tt{}bytes\nwendquote} version prints four bytes
(two-hex characters), lowest first, with spaces in-between.  The
decimal bytes version is analogous.  In the {\Tt{}bytes\nwendquote} version, missing
bytes are printed as whitespace.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{38}\moddef{Bytes: public}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  public :: word32_write
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{39}\moddef{Bytes: interfaces}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  interface word32_write
     module procedure word32_write_unit
  end interface
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{40}\moddef{Bytes: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine word32_write_unit (w, unit, bytes, decimal, newline)
    type(word32_t), intent(in) :: w
    integer, intent(in), optional :: unit
    logical, intent(in), optional :: bytes, decimal, newline
    logical :: dc, by, nl
    type(word64_t) :: ww
    integer :: i, u
    u = given_output_unit (unit);  if (u < 0)  return
    by = .false.;  if (present (bytes))   by = bytes
    dc = .false.;  if (present (decimal)) dc = decimal
    nl = .false.;  if (present (newline)) nl = newline
    if (by) then
       do i = 0, 3
          if (i>0)  write (u, '(1x)', advance='no')
          if (8*i < w%fill) then
             call byte_write (byte_from_word32 (w, i), unit, decimal=decimal)
          else if (dc) then
             write (u, '(3x)', advance='no')
          else
             write (u, '(2x)', advance='no')
          end if
       end do
    else if (dc) then
       ww = w
       write (u, '(I10)', advance='no') ww%i
    else
       select case (w%fill)
       case ( 0)
       case ( 8);  write (6, '(1x,z8.2)', advance='no') ibits (w%i, 0, 8)
       case (16);  write (6, '(1x,z8.4)', advance='no') ibits (w%i, 0,16)
       case (24);  write (6, '(1x,z8.6)', advance='no') ibits (w%i, 0,24)
       case (32);  write (6, '(1x,z8.8)', advance='no') ibits (w%i, 0,32)
       end select
    end if
    if (nl) write (u, *)
  end subroutine word32_write_unit

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{41}\nwdocspar
\subsection{Operations on 32-bit words}
Define the usual logical operations, as well as addition (mod
$2^{32}$).  We assume that all operands are completely filled.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{42}\moddef{Bytes: public}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  public :: not, ior, ieor, iand, ishft, ishftc
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{43}\moddef{Bytes: interfaces}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  interface not
     module procedure word_not
  end interface
  interface ior
     module procedure word_or
  end interface
  interface ieor
     module procedure word_eor
  end interface
  interface iand
     module procedure word_and
  end interface
  interface ishft
     module procedure word_shft
  end interface
  interface ishftc
     module procedure word_shftc
  end interface
\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{44}\moddef{Bytes: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  function word_not (w1) result (w2)
    type(word32_t), intent(in) :: w1
    type(word32_t) :: w2
    w2 = not (w1%i)
  end function word_not

  function word_or (w1, w2) result (w3)
    type(word32_t), intent(in) :: w1, w2
    type(word32_t) :: w3
    w3 = ior (w1%i, w2%i)
  end function word_or

  function word_eor (w1, w2) result (w3)
    type(word32_t), intent(in) :: w1, w2
    type(word32_t) :: w3
    w3 = ieor (w1%i, w2%i)
  end function word_eor

  function word_and (w1, w2) result (w3)
    type(word32_t), intent(in) :: w1, w2
    type(word32_t) :: w3
    w3 = iand (w1%i, w2%i)
  end function word_and

  function word_shft (w1, s) result (w2)
    type(word32_t), intent(in) :: w1
    integer, intent(in) :: s
    type(word32_t) :: w2
    w2 = ishft (w1%i, s)
  end function word_shft

  function word_shftc (w1, s) result (w2)
    type(word32_t), intent(in) :: w1
    integer, intent(in) :: s
    type(word32_t) :: w2
    w2 = ishftc (w1%i, s, 32)
  end function word_shftc

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{45}Addition is defined mod $2^{32}$, i.e., without overflow checking.
This means that we have to work around a possible overflow check enforced by
the compiler.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{46}\moddef{Bytes: public}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  public :: operator(+)
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{47}\moddef{Bytes: interfaces}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  interface operator(+)
     module procedure word_add
     module procedure word_add_i8
     module procedure word_add_i32
  end interface
\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{48}\nwdocspar
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{49}\moddef{Bytes: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  function word_add (w1, w2) result (w3)
    type(word32_t), intent(in) :: w1, w2
    type(word32_t) :: w3
    integer(i64) :: j
    j = int (ibclr (w1%i, 31), i64) + int (ibclr (w2%i, 31), i64)
    w3 = int (ibclr (j, 31), kind=i32)
    if (btest (j, 31)) then
       if (btest (w1%i, 31) .eqv. btest (w2%i, 31))  w3 = ibset (w3%i, 31)
    else
       if (btest (w1%i, 31) .neqv. btest (w2%i, 31))  w3 = ibset (w3%i, 31)
    end if
  end function word_add

  function word_add_i8 (w1, i) result (w3)
    type(word32_t), intent(in) :: w1
    integer(i8), intent(in) :: i
    type(word32_t) :: w3
    integer(i64) :: j
    j = int (ibclr (w1%i, 31), i64) + int (ibclr (i, 7), i64)
    if (btest (i, 7))  j = j + 128
    w3 = int (ibclr (j, 31), kind=i32)
    if (btest (j, 31) .neqv. btest (w1%i, 31))  w3 = ibset (w3%i, 31)
  end function word_add_i8

  function word_add_i32 (w1, i) result (w3)
    type(word32_t), intent(in) :: w1
    integer(i32), intent(in) :: i
    type(word32_t) :: w3
    integer(i64) :: j
    j = int (ibclr (w1%i, 31), i64) + int (ibclr (i, 31), i64)
    w3 = int (ibclr (j, 31), kind=i32)
    if (btest (j, 31)) then
       if (btest (w1%i, 31) .eqv. btest (i, 31))  w3 = ibset (w3%i, 31)
    else
       if (btest (w1%i, 31) .neqv. btest (i, 31))  w3 = ibset (w3%i, 31)
    end if
  end function word_add_i32

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{50}\nwdocspar
\subsection{64-bit words}
These objects consist of two 32-bit words.  They thus can hold integer
numbers larger than $2^{32}$ (to be exact, $2^{31}$ since FORTRAN
integers are signed).  The order is low-word, high-word.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{51}\moddef{Bytes: public}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  public :: word64_t
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{52}\moddef{Bytes: types}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  type :: word64_t
     private
     integer(i64) :: i
  end type word64_t

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{53}Set a 64 bit word:
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{54}\moddef{Bytes: interfaces}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  interface assignment(=)
     module procedure word64_set_from_i64
     module procedure word64_set_from_word32
  end interface
\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{55}\moddef{Bytes: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine word64_set_from_i64 (ww, i)
    type(word64_t), intent(out) :: ww
    integer(i64), intent(in) :: i
    ww%i = i
  end subroutine word64_set_from_i64

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{56}Filling with a 32-bit word:
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{57}\moddef{Bytes: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine word64_set_from_word32 (ww, w)
    type(word64_t), intent(out) :: ww
    type(word32_t), intent(in) :: w
    if (w%i >= 0_i32) then
       ww%i = w%i
    else
       ww%i = 2_i64*(huge(0_i32)+1_i64) + w%i
    end if
  end subroutine word64_set_from_word32

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{58}Extract a byte from a word.  The argument {\Tt{}i\nwendquote} is the position,
which may be between 0 and 7.

For the final assignment, we set the highest bit separately.
Otherwise, we might trigger an overflow condition for a compiler with
strict checking turned on.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{59}\moddef{Bytes: public}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  public :: byte_from_word64, word32_from_word64
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{60}\moddef{Bytes: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  function byte_from_word64 (ww, i) result (b)
    type(word64_t), intent(in) :: ww
    integer, intent(in) :: i
    type(byte_t) :: b
    integer(i64) :: j
    j = 0
    if (i >= 0 .and. i*8 < 64) then
       call mvbits (ww%i, i*8, 8, j, 0)
    end if
    b%i = int (ibclr (j, 7), kind=i8)
    if (btest (j, 7))  b%i = ibset (b%i, 7)
  end function byte_from_word64

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{61}Extract a 32-bit word from a 64-bit word.  The position is either 0
or 1.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{62}\moddef{Bytes: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  function word32_from_word64 (ww, i) result (w)
    type(word64_t), intent(in) :: ww
    integer, intent(in) :: i
    type(word32_t) :: w
    integer(i64) :: j
    j = 0
    select case (i)
    case (0);  call mvbits (ww%i,  0, 32, j, 0)
    case (1);  call mvbits (ww%i, 32, 32, j, 0)
    end select
    w = int (ibclr (j, 31), kind=i32)
    if (btest (j, 31))  w = ibset (w%i, 31)
  end function word32_from_word64

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{63}Print a 64-bit word.  Decimal version works up to $2^{63}$.
The {\Tt{}words\nwendquote} version uses the 'word32' printout, separated by two
spaces.  The low-word is printed first.  The {\Tt{}bytes\nwendquote} version also
uses the 'word32' printout.  This implies that the lowest byte is
first.  The default version prints a hexadecimal
number without spaces, highest byte first.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{64}\moddef{Bytes: public}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  public :: word64_write
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{65}\moddef{Bytes: interfaces}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  interface word64_write
     module procedure word64_write_unit
  end interface
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{66}\moddef{Bytes: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine word64_write_unit (ww, unit, words, bytes, decimal, newline)
    type(word64_t), intent(in) :: ww
    integer, intent(in), optional :: unit
    logical, intent(in), optional :: words, bytes, decimal, newline
    logical :: wo, by, dc, nl
    integer :: u
    u = given_output_unit (unit);  if (u < 0)  return
    wo = .false.;  if (present (words))    wo = words
    by = .false.;  if (present (bytes))    by = bytes
    dc = .false.;  if (present (decimal))  dc = decimal
    nl = .false.;  if (present (newline))  nl = newline
    if (wo .or. by) then
       call word32_write_unit (word32_from_word64 (ww, 0), unit, by, dc)
       write (u, '(2x)', advance='no')
       call word32_write_unit (word32_from_word64 (ww, 1), unit, by, dc)
    else if (dc) then
       write (u, '(I19)', advance='no') ww%i
    else
       write (u, '(Z16)', advance='no') ww%i
    end if
    if (nl) write (u, *)
  end subroutine word64_write_unit

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{67}\nwdocspar
%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\section{Hashtables}
Hash tables, like lists, are not part of Fortran and must be defined
on a per-case basis.  In this section we define a module that contains
a hash function.

Furthermore, for reference there is a complete framework of hashtable
type definitions and access functions.  This code is to be replicated
where hash tables are used, mutatis mutandis.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{68}\moddef{\code{}hashes.f90\edoc{}}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
\LA{}File header\RA{}

module hashes

  use kinds, only: i8, i32
  use bytes

\LA{}Standard module head\RA{}

\LA{}Hashes: public\RA{}

contains

\LA{}Hashes: procedures\RA{}

end module hashes
\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{69}\nwdocspar
\subsection{The hash function}
This is the one-at-a-time hash function by Bob Jenkins (from
Wikipedia), re-implemented in Fortran.  The function works on an array
of bytes (8-bit integers), as could be produced by, e.g., the
{\Tt{}transfer\nwendquote} function, and returns a single 32-bit integer.  For
determining the position in a hashtable, one can pick the lower bits
of the result as appropriate to the hashtable size (which should be a
power of 2).  Note that we are working on signed integers, so the
interpretation of values differs from the C version.  This should not
matter in practice, however.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{70}\moddef{Hashes: public}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  public :: hash
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{71}\moddef{Hashes: procedures}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  function hash (key) result (hashval)
    integer(i32) :: hashval
    integer(i8), dimension(:), intent(in) :: key
    type(word32_t) :: w
    integer :: i
    w = 0_i32
    do i = 1, size (key)
       w = w + key(i)
       w = w + ishft (w, 10)
       w = ieor (w, ishft (w, -6))
    end do
    w = w + ishft (w, 3)
    w = ieor (w, ishft (w, -11))
    w = w + ishft (w, 15)
    hashval = w
  end function hash

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{72}\nwdocspar
\subsection{The hash table}
We define a generic hashtable type (that depends on the
{\Tt{}hash{\_}data{\_}t\nwendquote} type) together with associated methods.

This is a template:
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{73}\moddef{Hashtables: types}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  type :: hash_data_t
     integer :: i
  end type hash_data_t

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{74}Associated methods:
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{75}\moddef{Hashtables: procedures}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine hash_data_final (data)
    type(hash_data_t), intent(inout) :: data
  end subroutine hash_data_final

  subroutine hash_data_write (data, unit)
    type(hash_data_t), intent(in) :: data
    integer, intent(in), optional :: unit
    integer :: u
    u = given_output_unit (unit);  if (u < 0)  return
    write (u, *) data%i
  end subroutine hash_data_write

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{76}Each hash entry stores the unmasked hash value, the key, and points to
actual data if present.  Note that this could be an allocatable scalar
in principle, but making it a pointer avoids deep copy when expanding
the hashtable.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{77}\moddef{Hashtables: types}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  type :: hash_entry_t
     integer(i32) :: hashval = 0
     integer(i8), dimension(:), allocatable :: key
     type(hash_data_t), pointer :: data => null ()
  end type hash_entry_t

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{78}The hashtable object holds the actual table, the number of filled
entries and the number of entries after which the size should be
doubled.  The mask is equal to the table size minus one and thus
coincides with the upper bound of the table index, which starts at zero.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{79}\moddef{Hashtables: types}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  type :: hashtable_t
     integer :: n_entries = 0
     real :: fill_ratio = 0
     integer :: n_entries_max = 0
     integer(i32) :: mask = 0
     type(hash_entry_t), dimension(:), allocatable :: entry
  end type hashtable_t

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{80}Initializer: The size has to be a power of two, the fill ratio is a
real (machine-default!) number between 0 and 1.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{81}\moddef{Hashtables: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine hashtable_init (hashtable, size, fill_ratio)
    type(hashtable_t), intent(out) :: hashtable
    integer, intent(in) :: size
    real, intent(in) :: fill_ratio
    hashtable%fill_ratio = fill_ratio
    hashtable%n_entries_max = size * fill_ratio
    hashtable%mask = size - 1
    allocate (hashtable%entry (0:hashtable%mask))
  end subroutine hashtable_init

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{82}Finalizer: This calls a {\Tt{}hash{\_}data{\_}final\nwendquote} subroutine which must
exist.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{83}\moddef{Hashtables: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine hashtable_final (hashtable)
    type(hashtable_t), intent(inout) :: hashtable
    integer :: i
    do i = 0, hashtable%mask
       if (associated (hashtable%entry(i)%data)) then
          call hash_data_final (hashtable%entry(i)%data)
          deallocate (hashtable%entry(i)%data)
       end if
    end do
    deallocate (hashtable%entry)
  end subroutine hashtable_final

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{84}Output.  Here, we refer to a {\Tt{}hash{\_}data{\_}write\nwendquote} subroutine.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{85}\moddef{Hashtables: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine hashtable_write (hashtable, unit)
    type(hashtable_t), intent(in) :: hashtable
    integer, intent(in), optional :: unit
    integer :: u, i
    u = given_output_unit (unit);  if (u < 0)  return
    do i = 0, hashtable%mask
       if (associated (hashtable%entry(i)%data)) then
          write (u, *) i, "(hash =", hashtable%entry(i)%hashval, ")", &
               hashtable%entry(i)%key
          call hash_data_write (hashtable%entry(i)%data, unit)
       end if
    end do
  end subroutine hashtable_write

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{86}\nwdocspar
\subsection{Hashtable insertion}
Insert a single entry with the hash value as trial place.  If the
table is filled, first expand it.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{87}\moddef{Hashtables: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine hashtable_insert (hashtable, key, data)
    type(hashtable_t), intent(inout) :: hashtable
    integer(i8), dimension(:), intent(in) :: key
    type(hash_data_t), intent(in), target :: data
    integer(i32) :: h
    if (hashtable%n_entries >= hashtable%n_entries_max) &
         call hashtable_expand (hashtable)
    h = hash (key)
    call hashtable_insert_rec (hashtable, h, h, key, data)
  end subroutine hashtable_insert

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{88}We need this auxiliary routine for doubling the size of the
hashtable.  We rely on the fact that default assignment copies
the data pointer, not the data themselves.  The temporary array must
not be finalized; it is deallocated automatically together with its
allocatable components.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{89}\moddef{Hashtables: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine hashtable_expand (hashtable)
    type(hashtable_t), intent(inout) :: hashtable
    type(hash_entry_t), dimension(:), allocatable :: table_tmp
    integer :: i, s
    allocate (table_tmp (0:hashtable%mask))
    table_tmp = hashtable%entry
    deallocate (hashtable%entry)
    s = 2 * size (table_tmp)
    hashtable%n_entries = 0
    hashtable%n_entries_max = s * hashtable%fill_ratio
    hashtable%mask = s - 1
    allocate (hashtable%entry (0:hashtable%mask))
    do i = 0, ubound (table_tmp, 1)
       if (associated (table_tmp(i)%data)) then
          call hashtable_insert_rec (hashtable, table_tmp(i)%hashval, &
               table_tmp(i)%hashval, table_tmp(i)%key, table_tmp(i)%data)
       end if
    end do
  end subroutine hashtable_expand

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{90}Insert a single entry at a trial place {\Tt{}h\nwendquote}, reduced to the table
size.  Collision resolution is done simply by choosing the next
element, recursively until the place is empty.  For bookkeeping, we
preserve the original hash value.  For a good hash function, there
should be no clustering.

Note that if the new key exactly matches an existing key, nothing is done.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{91}\moddef{Hashtables: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  recursive subroutine hashtable_insert_rec (hashtable, h, hashval, key, data)
    type(hashtable_t), intent(inout) :: hashtable
    integer(i32), intent(in) :: h, hashval
    integer(i8), dimension(:), intent(in) :: key
    type(hash_data_t), intent(in), target :: data
    integer(i32) :: i
    i = iand (h, hashtable%mask)
    if (associated (hashtable%entry(i)%data)) then
       if (size (hashtable%entry(i)%key) /= size (key)) then
          call hashtable_insert_rec (hashtable, h + 1, hashval, key, data)
       else if (any (hashtable%entry(i)%key /= key)) then
          call hashtable_insert_rec (hashtable, h + 1, hashval, key, data)
       end if
    else
       hashtable%entry(i)%hashval = hashval
       allocate (hashtable%entry(i)%key (size (key)))
       hashtable%entry(i)%key = key
       hashtable%entry(i)%data => data
       hashtable%n_entries = hashtable%n_entries + 1
    end if
  end subroutine hashtable_insert_rec

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{92}\nwdocspar
\subsection{Hashtable lookup}
The lookup function has to parallel the insert function.  If the place
is filled, check if the key matches.  Yes: return the pointer; no:
increment the hash value and check again.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{93}\moddef{Hashtables: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  function hashtable_lookup (hashtable, key) result (ptr)
    type(hash_data_t), pointer :: ptr
    type(hashtable_t), intent(in) :: hashtable
    integer(i8), dimension(:), intent(in) :: key
    ptr => hashtable_lookup_rec (hashtable, hash (key), key)
  end function hashtable_lookup

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{94}\moddef{Hashtables: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  recursive function hashtable_lookup_rec (hashtable, h, key) result (ptr)
    type(hash_data_t), pointer :: ptr
    type(hashtable_t), intent(in) :: hashtable
    integer(i32), intent(in) :: h
    integer(i8), dimension(:), intent(in) :: key
    integer(i32) :: i
    i = iand (h, hashtable%mask)
    if (associated (hashtable%entry(i)%data)) then
       if (size (hashtable%entry(i)%key) == size (key)) then
          if (all (hashtable%entry(i)%key == key)) then
             ptr => hashtable%entry(i)%data
          else
             ptr => hashtable_lookup_rec (hashtable, h + 1, key)
          end if
       else
          ptr => hashtable_lookup_rec (hashtable, h + 1, key)
       end if
    else
       ptr => null ()
    end if
  end function hashtable_lookup_rec

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{95}\moddef{Hashtables: public}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  public :: hashtable_test
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{96}\moddef{Hashtables: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine hashtable_test ()
    type(hash_data_t), pointer :: data
    type(hashtable_t) :: hashtable
    integer(i8) :: i
    call hashtable_init (hashtable, 16, 0.25)
    do i = 1, 10
       allocate (data)
       data%i = i*i
       call hashtable_insert (hashtable, [i, i+i], data)
    end do
    call hashtable_insert (hashtable, [2_i8, 4_i8], data)
    call hashtable_write (hashtable)
    data => hashtable_lookup (hashtable, [5_i8, 10_i8])
    if (associated (data)) then
       print *, "lookup:", data%i
    else
       print *, "lookup: --"
    end if
    data => hashtable_lookup (hashtable, [6_i8, 12_i8])
    if (associated (data)) then
       print *, "lookup:", data%i
    else
       print *, "lookup: --"
    end if
    data => hashtable_lookup (hashtable, [4_i8, 9_i8])
    if (associated (data)) then
       print *, "lookup:", data%i
    else
       print *, "lookup: --"
    end if
    call hashtable_final (hashtable)
  end subroutine hashtable_test

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{97}\nwdocspar
%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\section{MD5 Checksums}
Implementing MD5 checksums allows us
to check input/file integrity on the basis of a well-known standard.
The building blocks have been introduced in the {\Tt{}bytes\nwendquote} module.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{98}\moddef{\code{}md5.f90\edoc{}}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
\LA{}File header\RA{}

module md5

  use kinds, only: i8, i32, i64
  use io_units
  use system_defs, only: BUFFER_SIZE
  use system_defs, only: LF, EOR, EOF
  use diagnostics
  use bytes

\LA{}Standard module head\RA{}

\LA{}MD5: public\RA{}

\LA{}MD5: types\RA{}

\LA{}MD5: variables\RA{}

\LA{}MD5: interfaces\RA{}

contains

\LA{}MD5: procedures\RA{}

end module md5
\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{99}\nwdocspar
\subsection{Blocks}
A block is a sequence of 16 words (64 bytes or 512 bits).  We
anticipate that blocks will be linked, so include a pointer to the
next block.  There is a fill status (word counter), as there is one
for each word.  The fill status is equal to the number of bytes that
are in, so it may be between 0 and 64.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{100}\moddef{MD5: types}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  type :: block_t
     private
     type(word32_t), dimension(0:15) :: w
     type(block_t), pointer :: next => null ()
     integer :: fill = 0
  end type block_t

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{101}Check if a block is completely filled or empty:
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{102}\moddef{MD5: procedures}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  function block_is_empty (b)
    type(block_t), intent(in) :: b
    logical :: block_is_empty
    block_is_empty = (b%fill == 0 .and. word32_empty (b%w(0)))
  end function block_is_empty

  function block_is_filled (b)
    type(block_t), intent(in) :: b
    logical :: block_is_filled
    block_is_filled = (b%fill == 64)
  end function block_is_filled

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{103}Append a single byte to a block.  Works only if the block is not yet
filled.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{104}\moddef{MD5: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine block_append_byte (bl, by)
    type(block_t), intent(inout) :: bl
    type(byte_t), intent(in) :: by
    if (.not. block_is_filled (bl)) then
       call word32_append_byte (bl%w(bl%fill/4), by)
       bl%fill = bl%fill + 1
    end if
  end subroutine block_append_byte

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{105}The printing routine allows for printing as sequences of words or
bytes, decimal or hex.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{106}\moddef{MD5: interfaces}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  interface block_write
     module procedure block_write_unit
  end interface
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{107}\moddef{MD5: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine block_write_unit (b, unit, bytes, decimal)
    type(block_t), intent(in) :: b
    integer, intent(in), optional :: unit
    logical, intent(in), optional :: bytes, decimal
    logical :: by, dc
    integer :: i, u
    u = given_output_unit (unit);  if (u < 0)  return
    by = .false.;  if (present (bytes))    by = bytes
    dc = .false.;  if (present (decimal))  dc = decimal
    do i = 0, b%fill/4 - 1
       call newline_or_blank (u, i, by, dc)
       call word32_write (b%w(i), unit, bytes, decimal)
    end do
    if (.not. block_is_filled (b)) then
       i = b%fill/4
       if (.not. word32_empty (b%w(i))) then
          call newline_or_blank (u, i, by, dc)
          call word32_write (b%w(i), unit, bytes, decimal)
       end if
    end if
    write (u, *)
  contains
    subroutine newline_or_blank (u, i, bytes, decimal)
      integer, intent(in) :: u, i
      logical, intent(in) :: bytes, decimal
      if (decimal) then
         select case (i)
         case (0)
         case (2,4,6,8,10,12,14);  write (u, *)
         case default
            write (u, '(2x)', advance='no')
         end select
      else if (bytes) then
         select case (i)
         case (0)
         case (4,8,12);  write (u, *)
         case default
            write (u, '(2x)', advance='no')
         end select
      else
         if (i == 8)  write (u, *)
      end if
    end subroutine newline_or_blank
  end subroutine block_write_unit

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{108}\nwdocspar
\subsection{Messages}
A message (within this module) is a linked list of blocks.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{109}\moddef{MD5: types}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  type :: message_t
     private
     type(block_t), pointer :: first => null ()
     type(block_t), pointer :: last => null ()
     integer :: n_blocks = 0
  end type message_t

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{110}Clear the message list
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{111}\moddef{MD5: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine message_clear (m)
    type(message_t), intent(inout) :: m
    type(block_t), pointer :: b
    nullify (m%last)
    do
       b => m%first
       if (.not.(associated (b))) exit
       m%first => b%next
       deallocate (b)
    end do
    m%n_blocks = 0
  end subroutine message_clear

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{112}Append an empty block to the message list
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{113}\moddef{MD5: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine message_append_new_block (m)
    type(message_t), intent(inout) :: m
    if (associated (m%last)) then
       allocate (m%last%next)
       m%last => m%last%next
       m%n_blocks = m%n_blocks + 1
    else
       allocate (m%first)
       m%last => m%first
       m%n_blocks = 1
    end if
  end subroutine message_append_new_block

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{114}Initialize: clear and allocate the first (empty) block.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{115}\moddef{MD5: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine message_init (m)
    type(message_t), intent(inout) :: m
    call message_clear (m)
    call message_append_new_block (m)
  end subroutine message_init

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{116}Append a single byte to a message.  If necessary, allocate a new
block.  If the message is empty, initialize it.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{117}\moddef{MD5: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine message_append_byte (m, b)
    type(message_t), intent(inout) :: m
    type(byte_t), intent(in) :: b
    if (.not. associated (m%last)) then
       call message_init (m)
    else if (block_is_filled (m%last)) then
       call message_append_new_block (m)
    end if
    call block_append_byte (m%last, b)
  end subroutine message_append_byte

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{118}Append zero bytes until the current block is filled up to the required
position.  If we are already beyond that, append a new block and fill
that one.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{119}\moddef{MD5: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine message_pad_zero (m, i)
    type(message_t), intent(inout) :: m
    integer, intent(in) :: i
    type(block_t), pointer :: b
    integer :: j
    if (associated (m%last)) then
       b => m%last
       if (b%fill > i) then
          do j = b%fill + 1, 64 + i
             call message_append_byte (m, byte_zero)
          end do
       else
          do j = b%fill + 1, i
             call message_append_byte (m, byte_zero)
          end do
       end if
    end if
  end subroutine message_pad_zero

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{120}This returns the number of bits within a message.  We need a 64-bit
word for the result since it may be more than $2^{31}$.  This is also
required by the MD5 standard.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{121}\moddef{MD5: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  function message_bits (m) result (length)
    type(message_t), intent(in) :: m
    type(word64_t) :: length
    type(block_t), pointer :: b
    integer(i64) :: n_blocks_filled, n_bytes_extra
    if (m%n_blocks > 0) then
       b => m%last
       if (block_is_filled (b)) then
          n_blocks_filled = m%n_blocks
          n_bytes_extra = 0
       else
          n_blocks_filled = m%n_blocks - 1
          n_bytes_extra = b%fill
       end if
       length = n_blocks_filled * 512 + n_bytes_extra * 8
    else
       length = 0_i64
    end if
  end function message_bits

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{122}\nwdocspar
\subsection{Message I/O}
Append the contents of a string to a message.  We first cast the
character string into a 8-bit integer array and the append this byte
by byte.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{123}\moddef{MD5: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine message_append_string (m, s)
    type(message_t), intent(inout) :: m
    character(len=*), intent(in) :: s
    integer(i64) :: i, n_bytes
    integer(i8), dimension(:), allocatable :: buffer
    integer(i8), dimension(1) :: mold
    type(byte_t) :: b
    n_bytes = size (transfer (s, mold))
    allocate (buffer (n_bytes))
    buffer = transfer (s, mold)
    do i = 1, size (buffer)
       b = buffer(i)
       call message_append_byte (m, b)
    end do
    deallocate (buffer)
  end subroutine message_append_string

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{124}Append the contents of a 32-bit integer to a message.  We first cast the
32-bit integer into a 8-bit integer array and the append this byte
by byte.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{125}\moddef{MD5: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine message_append_i32 (m, x)
    type(message_t), intent(inout) :: m
    integer(i32), intent(in) :: x
    integer(i8), dimension(4) :: buffer
    type(byte_t) :: b
    integer :: i
    buffer = transfer (x, buffer, size(buffer))
    do i = 1, size (buffer)
       b = buffer(i)
       call message_append_byte (m, b)
    end do
  end subroutine message_append_i32

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{126}Append one line from file to a message.  Include the newline character.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{127}\moddef{MD5: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine message_append_from_unit (m, u, iostat)
    type(message_t), intent(inout) :: m
    integer, intent(in) :: u
    integer, intent(out) :: iostat
    character(len=BUFFER_SIZE) :: buffer
    read (u, *, iostat=iostat) buffer
    call message_append_string (m, trim (buffer))
    call message_append_string (m, LF)
  end subroutine message_append_from_unit

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{128}Fill a message from file.  (Each line counts as a string.)
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{129}\moddef{MD5: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine message_read_from_file (m, f)
    type(message_t), intent(inout) :: m
    character(len=*), intent(in) :: f
    integer :: u, iostat
    u = free_unit ()
    open (file=f, unit=u, action='read')
    do
       call message_append_from_unit (m, u, iostat=iostat)
       if (iostat < 0) exit
    end do
    close (u)
  end subroutine message_read_from_file

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{130}Write a message.  After each block, insert an empty line.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{131}\moddef{MD5: interfaces}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  interface message_write
     module procedure message_write_unit
  end interface
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{132}\moddef{MD5: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine message_write_unit (m, unit, bytes, decimal)
    type(message_t), intent(in) :: m
    integer, intent(in), optional :: unit
    logical, intent(in), optional :: bytes, decimal
    type(block_t), pointer :: b
    integer :: u
    u = given_output_unit (unit);  if (u < 0)  return
    b => m%first
    if (associated (b)) then
       do
          call block_write_unit (b, unit, bytes, decimal)
          b => b%next
          if (.not. associated (b))  exit
          write (u, *)
       end do
    end if
  end subroutine message_write_unit

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{133}\nwdocspar
\subsection{Auxiliary functions}
These four functions on three words are defined in the MD5 standard:
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{134}\moddef{MD5: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  function ff (x, y, z)
    type(word32_t), intent(in) :: x, y, z
    type(word32_t) :: ff
    ff = ior (iand (x, y), iand (not (x), z))
  end function ff

  function fg (x, y, z)
    type(word32_t), intent(in) :: x, y, z
    type(word32_t) :: fg
    fg = ior (iand (x, z), iand (y, not (z)))
  end function fg

  function fh (x, y, z)
    type(word32_t), intent(in) :: x, y, z
    type(word32_t) :: fh
    fh = ieor (ieor (x, y), z)
  end function fh

  function fi (x, y, z)
    type(word32_t), intent(in) :: x, y, z
    type(word32_t) :: fi
    fi = ieor (y, ior (x, not (z)))
  end function fi

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{135}\nwdocspar
\subsection{Auxiliary stuff}
This defines and initializes the table of transformation constants:
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{136}\moddef{MD5: variables}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  type(word32_t), dimension(64), save :: t
  logical, save :: table_initialized = .false.
\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{137}\moddef{MD5: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine table_init
    type(word64_t) :: ww
    integer :: i
    if (.not.table_initialized) then
       do i = 1, 64
          ww = int (4294967296d0 * abs (sin (i * 1d0)), kind=i64)
          t(i) = word32_from_word64 (ww, 0)
       end do
       table_initialized = .true.
    end if
  end subroutine table_init

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{138}This encodes the message digest (4 words) into a 32-character
string.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{139}\moddef{MD5: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  function digest_string (aa) result (s)
    type(word32_t), dimension (0:3), intent(in) :: aa
    character(len=32) :: s
    integer :: i, j
    do i = 0, 3
       do j = 0, 3
          call byte_write (byte_from_word32 (aa(i), j), s(i*8+j*2+1:i*8+j*2+2))
       end do
    end do
  end function digest_string

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{140}\nwdocspar
\subsection{MD5 algorithm}
Pad the message with a byte {\Tt{}x80\nwendquote} and then pad zeros up to a full
block minus two words; in these words, insert the message length
(before padding) as a 64-bit word, low-word first.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{141}\moddef{MD5: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine message_pad (m)
    type(message_t), intent(inout) :: m
    type(word64_t) :: length
    integer(i8), parameter :: ipad = -128  ! z'80'
    type(byte_t) :: b
    integer :: i
    length = message_bits (m)
    b = ipad
    call message_append_byte (m, b)
    call message_pad_zero (m, 56)
    do i = 0, 7
       call message_append_byte (m, byte_from_word64 (length, i))
    end do
  end subroutine message_pad

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{142}Apply a series of transformations onto a state {\Tt{}a,b,c,d\nwendquote}, where
the transform function uses each word of the message together with the
predefined words.  Finally, encode the state as a 32-character string.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{143}\moddef{MD5: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine message_digest (m, s)
    type(message_t), intent(in) :: m
    character(len=32), intent(out) :: s
    integer(i32), parameter :: ia =  1732584193  ! z'67452301'
    integer(i32), parameter :: ib =  -271733879  ! z'efcdab89'
    integer(i32), parameter :: ic = -1732584194  ! z'98badcfe'
    integer(i32), parameter :: id =   271733878  ! z'10325476'
    type(word32_t) :: a, b, c, d
    type(word32_t) :: aa, bb, cc, dd
    type(word32_t), dimension(0:15) :: x
    type(block_t), pointer :: bl
    call table_init
    a = ia;  b = ib;  c = ic;  d = id
    bl => m%first
    do
       if (.not.associated (bl)) exit
       x = bl%w
       aa = a;  bb = b;  cc = c;  dd = d
       call transform (ff, a, b, c, d,  0,  7,  1)
       call transform (ff, d, a, b, c,  1, 12,  2)
       call transform (ff, c, d, a, b,  2, 17,  3)
       call transform (ff, b, c, d, a,  3, 22,  4)
       call transform (ff, a, b, c, d,  4,  7,  5)
       call transform (ff, d, a, b, c,  5, 12,  6)
       call transform (ff, c, d, a, b,  6, 17,  7)
       call transform (ff, b, c, d, a,  7, 22,  8)
       call transform (ff, a, b, c, d,  8,  7,  9)
       call transform (ff, d, a, b, c,  9, 12, 10)
       call transform (ff, c, d, a, b, 10, 17, 11)
       call transform (ff, b, c, d, a, 11, 22, 12)
       call transform (ff, a, b, c, d, 12,  7, 13)
       call transform (ff, d, a, b, c, 13, 12, 14)
       call transform (ff, c, d, a, b, 14, 17, 15)
       call transform (ff, b, c, d, a, 15, 22, 16)
       call transform (fg, a, b, c, d,  1,  5, 17)
       call transform (fg, d, a, b, c,  6,  9, 18)
       call transform (fg, c, d, a, b, 11, 14, 19)
       call transform (fg, b, c, d, a,  0, 20, 20)
       call transform (fg, a, b, c, d,  5,  5, 21)
       call transform (fg, d, a, b, c, 10,  9, 22)
       call transform (fg, c, d, a, b, 15, 14, 23)
       call transform (fg, b, c, d, a,  4, 20, 24)
       call transform (fg, a, b, c, d,  9,  5, 25)
       call transform (fg, d, a, b, c, 14,  9, 26)
       call transform (fg, c, d, a, b,  3, 14, 27)
       call transform (fg, b, c, d, a,  8, 20, 28)
       call transform (fg, a, b, c, d, 13,  5, 29)
       call transform (fg, d, a, b, c,  2,  9, 30)
       call transform (fg, c, d, a, b,  7, 14, 31)
       call transform (fg, b, c, d, a, 12, 20, 32)
       call transform (fh, a, b, c, d,  5,  4, 33)
       call transform (fh, d, a, b, c,  8, 11, 34)
       call transform (fh, c, d, a, b, 11, 16, 35)
       call transform (fh, b, c, d, a, 14, 23, 36)
       call transform (fh, a, b, c, d,  1,  4, 37)
       call transform (fh, d, a, b, c,  4, 11, 38)
       call transform (fh, c, d, a, b,  7, 16, 39)
       call transform (fh, b, c, d, a, 10, 23, 40)
       call transform (fh, a, b, c, d, 13,  4, 41)
       call transform (fh, d, a, b, c,  0, 11, 42)
       call transform (fh, c, d, a, b,  3, 16, 43)
       call transform (fh, b, c, d, a,  6, 23, 44)
       call transform (fh, a, b, c, d,  9,  4, 45)
       call transform (fh, d, a, b, c, 12, 11, 46)
       call transform (fh, c, d, a, b, 15, 16, 47)
       call transform (fh, b, c, d, a,  2, 23, 48)
       call transform (fi, a, b, c, d,  0,  6, 49)
       call transform (fi, d, a, b, c,  7, 10, 50)
       call transform (fi, c, d, a, b, 14, 15, 51)
       call transform (fi, b, c, d, a,  5, 21, 52)
       call transform (fi, a, b, c, d, 12,  6, 53)
       call transform (fi, d, a, b, c,  3, 10, 54)
       call transform (fi, c, d, a, b, 10, 15, 55)
       call transform (fi, b, c, d, a,  1, 21, 56)
       call transform (fi, a, b, c, d,  8,  6, 57)
       call transform (fi, d, a, b, c, 15, 10, 58)
       call transform (fi, c, d, a, b,  6, 15, 59)
       call transform (fi, b, c, d, a, 13, 21, 60)
       call transform (fi, a, b, c, d,  4,  6, 61)
       call transform (fi, d, a, b, c, 11, 10, 62)
       call transform (fi, c, d, a, b,  2, 15, 63)
       call transform (fi, b, c, d, a,  9, 21, 64)
       a = a + aa
       b = b + bb
       c = c + cc
       d = d + dd
       bl => bl%next
    end do
    s = digest_string ([a, b, c, d])
  contains
  \LA{}MD5: Internal subroutine transform\RA{}
  end subroutine message_digest

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{144}And this is the actual transformation that depends on one of the
previous functions, four words, and three integers.  The implicit
arguments are {\Tt{}x\nwendquote}, the word from the message to digest, and {\Tt{}t\nwendquote},
the entry in the predefined table.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{145}\moddef{MD5: Internal subroutine transform}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine transform (f, a, b, c, d, k, s, i)
    interface
       function f (x, y, z)
         import word32_t
         type(word32_t), intent(in) :: x, y, z
         type(word32_t) :: f
       end function f
    end interface
    type(word32_t), intent(inout) :: a
    type(word32_t), intent(in) :: b, c, d
    integer, intent(in) :: k, s, i
    a = b + ishftc (a + f(b, c, d) + x(k) + t(i), s)
  end subroutine transform

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{146}\nwdocspar
\subsection{User interface}
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{147}\moddef{MD5: public}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  public :: md5sum
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{148}\moddef{MD5: interfaces}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  interface md5sum
     module procedure md5sum_from_string
     module procedure md5sum_from_unit
  end interface
\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{149}This function computes the MD5 sum of the input string and returns it
as a 32-character string
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{150}\moddef{MD5: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  function md5sum_from_string (s) result (digest)
    character(len=*), intent(in) :: s
    character(len=32) :: digest
    type(message_t) :: m
    call message_append_string (m, s)
    call message_pad (m)
    call message_digest (m, digest)
    call message_clear (m)
  end function md5sum_from_string

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{151}This funct. reads from unit u (an unformmated sequence of
integers) and computes the MD5 sum.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{152}\moddef{MD5: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  function md5sum_from_unit (u) result (digest)
    integer, intent(in) :: u
    character(len=32) :: digest
    type(message_t) :: m
    character :: char
    integer :: iostat
    READ_CHARS: do
       read (u, "(A)", advance="no", iostat=iostat)  char
       select case (iostat)
       case (0)
          call message_append_string (m, char)
       case (EOR)
          call message_append_string (m, LF)
       case (EOF)
          exit READ_CHARS
       case default
          call msg_fatal &
               ("Computing MD5 sum: I/O error while reading from scratch file")
       end select
    end do READ_CHARS
    call message_pad (m)
    call message_digest (m, digest)
    call message_clear (m)
  end function md5sum_from_unit

\eatline

\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{160}This function checks the implementation by computing the checksum of
certain strings and comparing them with the known values.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{161}\moddef{MD5: execute tests}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  call test (md5_1, "md5_1", &
       "check MD5 sums", &
       u, results)
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{162}\moddef{MD5: test declarations}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  public :: md5_1
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{163}\moddef{MD5: tests}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine md5_1 (u)
    integer, intent(in) :: u
    character(32) :: s
    integer, parameter :: n = 7
    integer :: i
    character(80), dimension(n) :: teststring
    data teststring(1) /""/
    data teststring(2) /"a"/
    data teststring(3) /"abc"/
    data teststring(4) /"message digest"/
    data teststring(5) /"abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz"/
    data teststring(6) /"ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789"/
    data teststring(7) /"12345678901234567890123456789012345678901234567890123456789012345678901234567890"/
    character(32), dimension(n) :: result
    data result(1) /"D41D8CD98F00B204E9800998ECF8427E"/
    data result(2) /"0CC175B9C0F1B6A831C399E269772661"/
    data result(3) /"900150983CD24FB0D6963F7D28E17F72"/
    data result(4) /"F96B697D7CB7938D525A2F31AAF161D0"/
    data result(5) /"C3FCD3D76192E4007DFB496CCA67E13B"/
    data result(6) /"D174AB98D277D9F5A5611C2C9F419D9F"/
    data result(7) /"57EDF4A22BE3C955AC49DA2E2107B67A"/

    write (u, "(A)")  "* Test output: MD5"
    write (u, "(A)")  "*   Purpose: test MD5 sums"
    write (u, "(A)")

    do i = 1, n
       write (u, "(A)") "MD5 test string = " // '"'// &
            trim (teststring(i)) // '"'
       s = md5sum (trim (teststring(i)))
       write (u, "(A)") "MD5 check sum   = " // trim (s)
       write (u, "(A)") "Ref check sum   = " // result(i)
       if (s == result(i)) then
          call msg_message ("=> ok", u)
       else
          call msg_message ("=> MD5 sum self-test failed", u)
       end if
    end do
    call msg_message ("=============================================================================|", unit=u)
  end subroutine md5_1

\eatline

\section{Permutations}
Permute arrays of integers (of specific kind).
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{165}\moddef{\code{}permutations.f90\edoc{}}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
\LA{}File header\RA{}

module permutations

  use kinds, only: TC

\LA{}Standard module head\RA{}

\LA{}Permutations: public\RA{}

\LA{}Permutations: types\RA{}

\LA{}Permutations: interfaces\RA{}

contains

\LA{}Permutations: procedures\RA{}

end module permutations
\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{166}\nwdocspar
\subsection{Permutations}
A permutation is an array of integers.  Each integer between one and
{\Tt{}size\nwendquote} should occur exactly once.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{167}\moddef{Permutations: public}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  public :: permutation_t
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{168}\moddef{Permutations: types}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  type :: permutation_t
     private
     integer, dimension(:), allocatable :: p
  end type permutation_t

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{169}\nwdocspar
Initialize with the identity permutation.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{170}\moddef{Permutations: public}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  public :: permutation_init
  public :: permutation_final
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{171}\moddef{Permutations: procedures}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  elemental subroutine permutation_init (p, size)
    type(permutation_t), intent(inout) :: p
    integer, intent(in) :: size
    integer :: i
    allocate (p%p (size))
    forall (i = 1:size)
       p%p(i) = i
    end forall
  end subroutine permutation_init

  elemental subroutine permutation_final (p)
    type(permutation_t), intent(inout) :: p
    deallocate (p%p)
  end subroutine permutation_final

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{172}I/O:
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{173}\moddef{Permutations: public}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  public :: permutation_write
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{174}\moddef{Permutations: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine permutation_write (p, u)
    type(permutation_t), intent (in) :: p
    integer, intent(in) :: u
    integer :: i
    do i = 1, size (p%p)
       if (size (p%p) < 10) then
          write (u,"(1x,I1)", advance="no") p%p(i)
       else
          write (u,"(1x,I3)", advance="no") p%p(i)
       end if
    end do
    write (u, *)
  end subroutine permutation_write

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{175}\nwdocspar
Administration:
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{176}\moddef{Permutations: public}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  public :: permutation_size
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{177}\moddef{Permutations: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  elemental function permutation_size (perm) result (s)
    type(permutation_t), intent(in) :: perm
    integer :: s
    s = size (perm%p)
  end function permutation_size

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{178}Extract an entry in a permutation.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{179}\moddef{Permutations: public}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  public :: permute
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{180}\moddef{Permutations: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  elemental function permute (i, p) result (j)
    integer, intent(in) :: i
    type(permutation_t), intent(in) :: p
    integer :: j
    if (i > 0 .and. i <= size (p%p)) then
       j = p%p(i)
    else
       j = 0
    end if
  end function permute

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{181}\nwdocspar
Check whether a permutation is valid: Each integer in the range occurs
exactly once.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{182}\moddef{Permutations: public}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  public :: permutation_ok
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{183}\moddef{Permutations: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  elemental function permutation_ok (perm) result (ok)
    type(permutation_t), intent(in) :: perm
    logical :: ok
    integer :: i
    logical, dimension(:), allocatable :: set
    ok = .true.
    allocate (set (size (perm%p)))
    set = .false.
    do i = 1, size (perm%p)
       ok = (perm%p(i) > 0 .and. perm%p(i) <= size (perm%p))
       if (.not.ok) return
       set(perm%p(i)) = .true.
    end do
    ok = all (set)
  end function permutation_ok

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{184}Find the permutation that transforms the second array into the first
one.  We assume that this is possible and unique and all bounds are
set correctly.

This cannot be elemental.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{185}\moddef{Permutations: public}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  public :: permutation_find
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{186}\moddef{Permutations: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine permutation_find (perm, a1, a2)
    type(permutation_t), intent(inout) :: perm
    integer, dimension(:), intent(in) :: a1, a2
    integer :: i, j
    if (allocated (perm%p))  deallocate (perm%p)
    allocate (perm%p (size (a1)))
    do i = 1, size (a1)
       do j = 1, size (a2)
          if (a1(i) == a2(j)) then
             perm%p(i) = j
             exit
          end if
          perm%p(i) = 0
       end do
    end do
  end subroutine permutation_find

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{187}\nwdocspar
Find all permutations that transform an array of integers into
itself.  The resulting permutation list is allocated with the correct
length and filled.

The first step is to count the number of different entries in
{\Tt{}code\nwendquote}.  Next, we scan {\Tt{}code\nwendquote} again and assign a mask to each
different entry, true for all identical entries.  Finally, we
recursively permute the identity for each possible mask.

The permutation is done as follows:  A list of all permutations of the
initial one with respect to the current mask is generated, then the
permutations are generated in turn for each permutation in this list
with the next mask.  The result is always stored back into the main
list, starting from the end of the current list.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{188}\moddef{Permutations: public}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  public :: permutation_array_make
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{189}\moddef{Permutations: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine permutation_array_make (pa, code)
    type(permutation_t), dimension(:), allocatable, intent(out) :: pa
    integer, dimension(:), intent(in) :: code
    logical, dimension(size(code)) :: mask
    logical, dimension(:,:), allocatable :: imask
    integer, dimension(:), allocatable :: n_i
    type(permutation_t) :: p_init
    type(permutation_t), dimension(:), allocatable :: p_tmp
    integer :: psize, i, j, k, n_different, n, nn_k
    psize = size (code)
    mask = .true.
    n_different = 0
    do i=1, psize
       if (mask(i)) then
          n_different = n_different + 1
          mask = mask .and. (code /= code(i))
       end if
    end do
    allocate (imask(psize, n_different), n_i(n_different))
    mask = .true.
    k = 0
    do i=1, psize
       if (mask(i)) then
          k = k + 1
          imask(:,k) = (code == code(i))
          n_i(k) = factorial (count(imask(:,k)))
          mask = mask .and. (code /= code(i))
       end if
    end do
    n = product (n_i)
    allocate (pa (n))
    call permutation_init (p_init, psize)
    pa(1) = p_init
    nn_k = 1
    do k = 1, n_different
       allocate (p_tmp (n_i(k)))
       do i = nn_k, 1, -1
          call permutation_array_with_mask (p_tmp, imask(:,k), pa(i))
          do j = n_i(k), 1, -1
             pa((i-1)*n_i(k) + j) = p_tmp(j)
          end do
       end do
       deallocate (p_tmp)
       nn_k = nn_k * n_i(k)
    end do
    call permutation_final (p_init)
    deallocate (imask, n_i)
  end subroutine permutation_array_make

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{190}Make a list of permutations of the elements marked true in the
{\Tt{}mask\nwendquote} array.  The final permutation list must be allocated with the
correct length ($n!$).  The third argument is the initial
permutation to start with, which must have the same length as the
{\Tt{}mask\nwendquote} array (this is not checked).
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{191}\moddef{Permutations: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine permutation_array_with_mask (pa, mask, p_init)
    type(permutation_t), dimension(:), intent(inout) :: pa
    logical, dimension(:), intent(in) :: mask
    type(permutation_t), intent(in) :: p_init
    integer :: plen
    integer :: i, ii, j, fac_i, k, x
    integer, dimension(:), allocatable :: index
    plen = size (pa)
    allocate (index(count(mask)))
    ii = 0
    do i = 1, size (mask)
       if (mask(i)) then
          ii = ii + 1
          index(ii) = i
       end if
    end do
    pa = p_init
    ii = 0
    fac_i = 1
    do i = 1, size (mask)
       if (mask(i)) then
          ii = ii + 1
          fac_i = fac_i * ii
          x = permute (i, p_init)
          do j = 1, plen
             k = ii - mod (((j-1)*fac_i)/plen, ii)
             call insert (pa(j), x, k, ii, index)
          end do
       end if
    end do
    deallocate (index)
  contains
    subroutine insert (p, x, k, n, index)
      type(permutation_t), intent(inout) :: p
      integer, intent(in) :: x, k, n
      integer, dimension(:), intent(in) :: index
      integer :: i
      do i = n, k+1, -1
         p%p(index(i)) = p%p(index(i-1))
      end do
      p%p(index(k)) = x
    end subroutine insert
  end subroutine permutation_array_with_mask

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{192}The factorial function is needed for pre-determining the number of
permutations that will be generated:
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{193}\moddef{Permutations: public}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  public :: factorial
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{194}\moddef{Permutations: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  function factorial (n) result (f)
    integer, intent(in) :: n
    integer :: f
    integer :: i
    f = 1
    do i=2, abs(n)
       f = f*i
    end do
  end function factorial

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{195}\nwdocspar
\subsection{Operations on binary codes}
Binary codes are needed for phase-space trees.  Since the permutation
function uses permutations, and no other special type is involved, we
put the functions here.

This is needed for phase space trees: permute bits in a tree binary
code.  If no permutation is given, leave as is.  (We may want to
access the permutation directly here if this is efficiency-critical.)
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{196}\moddef{Permutations: public}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  public :: tc_permute
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{197}\moddef{Permutations: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  function tc_permute (k, perm, mask_in) result (pk)
    integer(TC), intent(in) :: k, mask_in
    type(permutation_t), intent(in) :: perm
    integer(TC) :: pk
    integer :: i
    pk = iand (k, mask_in)
    do i = 1, size (perm%p)
       if (btest(k,i-1))  pk = ibset (pk, perm%p(i)-1)
    end do
  end function tc_permute

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{198}\nwdocspar
This routine returns the number of set bits in the tree code value
{\Tt{}k\nwendquote}.  Hence, it is the number of externals connected to the current
line.  If {\Tt{}mask\nwendquote} is present, the complement of the tree code is also
considered, and the smaller number is returned.  This gives the true
distance from the external states, taking into account the initial
particles.  The complement number is increased by one, since for a
scattering diagram the vertex with the sum of all final-state codes is
still one point apart from the initial particles.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{199}\moddef{Permutations: public}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  public :: tc_decay_level
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{200}\moddef{Permutations: interfaces}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  interface tc_decay_level
     module procedure decay_level_simple
     module procedure decay_level_complement
  end interface
\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{201}\moddef{Permutations: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  function decay_level_complement (k, mask) result (l)
    integer(TC), intent(in) :: k, mask
    integer :: l
    l = min (decay_level_simple (k), &
         &   decay_level_simple (ieor (k, mask)) + 1)
  end function decay_level_complement

  function decay_level_simple (k) result(l)
    integer(TC), intent(in) :: k
    integer :: l
    integer :: i
    l = 0
    do i=0, bit_size(k)-1
       if (btest(k,i)) l = l+1
    end do
  end function decay_level_simple

\eatline

\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{204}\nwdocspar
\subsection{Implementation}
The {\Tt{}sort\nwendquote} function returns, for a given integer or real array, the
array sorted by increasing value.  The current implementation is
\emph{mergesort}, which has $O(n\ln n)$ behavior in all cases, and is
stable for elements of equal value.

The {\Tt{}sort{\_}abs\nwendquote} variant sorts by increasing absolute value, where for
identical absolute value, the positive number comes first.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{205}\moddef{Sorting: public}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  public :: sort
  public :: sort_abs
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{206}\moddef{Sorting: interfaces}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  interface sort
     module procedure sort_int
     module procedure sort_real
  end interface

  interface sort_abs
     module procedure sort_int_abs
  end interface

\eatline

\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{216}We start by individual elements, merge them to pairs, merge those to
four-element subarrays, and so on.  The last subarray can extend only
up to the original array bound, of course, and the second of the
subarrays to merge should contain at least one element.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{217}\moddef{Sorting: order}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
\LA{}Sorting: order1\RA{}
        call merge (idx(b1:e2), idx(b1:e1), idx(b2:e2), val)
\LA{}Sorting: order2\RA{}

\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{219}\moddef{Sorting: order abs}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
\LA{}Sorting: order1\RA{}
        call merge_abs (idx(b1:e2), idx(b1:e1), idx(b2:e2), val)
\LA{}Sorting: order2\RA{}
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{220}\nwdocspar
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{221}\moddef{Sorting: order1}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  integer :: n, i, s, b1, b2, e1, e2
  n = size (idx)
  !!! !!! !!! Work around ifort 16.0.(0/1) compiler bug
  !forall (i = 1:n)
     !idx(i) = i
  !end forall
  do i = 1, n
     idx(i) = i
  end do
  s = 1
  do while (s < n)
     do b1 = 1, n-s, 2*s
        b2 = b1 + s
        e1 = b2 - 1
        e2 = min (e1 + s, n)
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{222}\nwdocspar
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{223}\moddef{Sorting: order2}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
     end do
     s = 2 * s
  end do
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{224}The merging step does the actual sorting.  We take two sorted array
sections and merge them to a sorted result array.  We are working on
the indices, and comparing is done by taking the associated {\Tt{}val\nwendquote}
which is real or integer.

\LA{}Sorting: merge2\RA{}
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{228}We keep the elements if the absolute values are strictly ordered.
If they are equal in magnitude, we keep them if the larger value
comes first, or if they are equal.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{229}\moddef{Sorting: merge abs}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
\LA{}Sorting: merge1\RA{}
     if (abs (val(src1(i1))) < abs (val(src2(i2))) .or. &
        (abs (val(src1(i1))) == abs (val(src2(i2))) .and. &
        val(src1(i1)) >= val(src2(i2)))) then
\LA{}Sorting: merge2\RA{}
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{230}\nwdocspar
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{231}\moddef{Sorting: merge1}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  integer :: i1, i2, i
  i1 = 1
  i2 = 1
  do i = 1, size (tmp)
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{232}\nwdocspar
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{233}\moddef{Sorting: merge2}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
        tmp(i) = src1(i1);  i1 = i1 + 1
        if (i1 > size (src1)) then
           tmp(i+1:) = src2(i2:)
           exit
        end if
     else
        tmp(i) = src2(i2);  i2 = i2 + 1
        if (i2 > size (src2)) then
           tmp(i+1:) = src1(i1:)
           exit
        end if
     end if
  end do
  res = tmp
