\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{655}\moddef{Prc Threshold: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine prc_threshold_compute_sqme_virt (object, i_flv, &
         p, ren_scale, sqme, bad_point)
    class(prc_threshold_t), intent(in) :: object
    integer, intent(in) :: i_flv
    type(vector4_t), dimension(:), intent(in) :: p
    real(default), intent(in) :: ren_scale
    real(default), dimension(4), intent(out) :: sqme
    real(c_default_float), dimension(:,:), allocatable, save :: parray
    logical, intent(out) :: bad_point
    integer :: n_tot, i
    real(default) :: mu
    real(c_default_float), dimension(4) :: sqme_c
    real(c_default_float) :: mu_c, acc_c, alpha_s_c
    integer(c_int) :: i_flv_c
    call msg_debug2 (D_ME_METHODS, "prc_threshold_compute_sqme_virt")
    n_tot = size (p)
    if (allocated (parray)) then
       if (size(parray) /= n_tot) deallocate (parray)
    end if
    if (.not. allocated (parray))  allocate (parray (0:3, n_tot))
    forall (i = 1:n_tot)  parray(:,i) = p(i)%p

    if (vanishes (ren_scale)) then
      mu = sqrt (2* (p(1)*p(2)))
    else
      mu = ren_scale
    end if
    mu_c = mu
    alpha_s_c = object%qcd%alpha%get (mu)
    i_flv_c = i_flv
    select type (driver => object%driver)
    class is (threshold_driver_t)
       if (associated (driver%olp_eval2)) then
          call driver%olp_eval2 (i_flv_c, alpha_s_c, &
             parray, mu_c, sqme_c, acc_c)
          bad_point = real(acc_c, kind=default) > object%maximum_accuracy
          sqme = sqme_c
       else
          sqme = 0._default
          bad_point = .true.
       end if
    end select
  end subroutine prc_threshold_compute_sqme_virt

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{656}\nwdocspar
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{657}\moddef{Prc Threshold: prc threshold: TBP}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure :: init => prc_threshold_init
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{658}\moddef{Prc Threshold: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine prc_threshold_init (object, def, lib, id, i_component)
    class(prc_threshold_t), intent(inout) :: object
    class(prc_core_def_t), intent(in), target :: def
    type(process_library_t), intent(in), target :: lib
    type(string_t), intent(in) :: id
    integer, intent(in) :: i_component
    integer :: n_tot
    call object%base_init (def, lib, id, i_component)
    n_tot = object%data%n_in + object%data%n_out
    allocate (object%parray_ofs (0:3,n_tot), object%parray_ons (0:3,n_tot))
    if (n_tot == 4) then
       call object%set_process_mode (PROC_MODE_TT)
    else
       call object%set_process_mode (PROC_MODE_WBWB)
    end if
    call object%activate_parameters ()
  end subroutine prc_threshold_init

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{659}Activate the stored parameters by transferring them to the external
matrix element.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{660}\moddef{Prc Threshold: prc threshold: TBP}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure :: activate_parameters => prc_threshold_activate_parameters
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{661}\moddef{Prc Threshold: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine prc_threshold_activate_parameters (object)
    class (prc_threshold_t), intent(inout) :: object
    call msg_debug (D_ME_METHODS, "prc_threshold_activate_parameters")
    if (allocated (object%driver)) then
       if (allocated (object%par)) then
          select type (driver => object%driver)
          type is (threshold_driver_t)
             if (associated (driver%init)) then
                call driver%init (object%par, object%scheme)
             end if
          end select
       else
          call msg_bug ("prc_threshold_activate: parameter set is not allocated")
       end if
    else
       call msg_bug ("prc_threshold_activate: driver is not allocated")
    end if
  end subroutine prc_threshold_activate_parameters

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{662}\nwdocspar
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{663}\moddef{Prc Threshold: prc threshold: TBP}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure :: create_and_load_extra_libraries => prc_threshold_create_and_load_extra_libraries
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{664}\moddef{Prc Threshold: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine prc_threshold_create_and_load_extra_libraries ( &
         core, flv_states, var_list, os_data, libname, model, i_core)
    class(prc_threshold_t), intent(inout) :: core
    integer, intent(in), dimension(:,:), allocatable :: flv_states
    type(var_list_t), intent(in) :: var_list
    type(os_data_t), intent(in) :: os_data
    type(string_t), intent(in) :: libname
    type(model_data_t), intent(in), target :: model
    integer, intent(in) :: i_core
    call msg_debug (D_ME_METHODS, "prc_threshold_create_and_load_extra_libraries")
    if (allocated (core%driver)) then
       select type (driver => core%driver)
       type is (threshold_driver_t)
          if (driver%nlo_type == NLO_VIRTUAL) call driver%start_openloops ()
       end select
    else
       call msg_bug ("prc_threshold_create_and_load_extra_libraries: driver is not allocated")
    end if
  end subroutine prc_threshold_create_and_load_extra_libraries

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{665}\nwdocspar

\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{667}\moddef{Prc Threshold: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  function prc_threshold_includes_polarization (object) result (polarized)
    logical :: polarized

  end function prc_threshold_includes_polarization

% WHIZARD code as NOWEB source: event handling objects
%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\chapter{Generic Event Handling}
\includemodulegraph{events}

Event records allow the MC to communicate with the outside world.  The
event record should exhibit the observable contents of a physical
event.  We should be able to read and write events.  The actual
implementation of the event need not be defined yet, for that purpose.

We have the following basic modules:
\begin{description}
\item[event\_base]
  Abstract base type for event records.  The base type contains a
  reference to a {\Tt{}particle{\_}set{\_}t\nwendquote} object as the event core, and it
  holds some data that we should always expect, such as the squared
  matrix element and event weight.
\item[eio\_data]
  Transparent container for the metadata of an event sample.
\item[eio\_base]
  Abstract base type for event-record input and output.  The
  implementations of this base type represent specific event I/O
  formats.
\end{description}

These are the implementation modules:
\begin{description}
\item[eio\_checkpoints]
  Auxiliary output format.  The only purpose is to provide screen
  diagnostics during event output.
\item[eio\_callback]
  Auxiliary output format.  The only purpose is to execute a callback
  procedure, so we have a hook for external access during event output.
\item[eio\_weights]
  Print some event summary data, no details.  The main use if for
  testing purposes.
\item[eio\_dump]
  Dump the contents of WHIZARD's {\Tt{}particle{\_}set\nwendquote} internal record,
  using the {\Tt{}write\nwendquote} method of that record as-is.  The main use if for
  testing purposes.
\item[hep\_common]
  Implements traditional HEP common blocks that are (still) used by
  some of the event I/O formats below.
\item[hepmc\_interface]
  Access particle objects of the HepMC package.  Functional only if this
  package is linked.
\item[lcio\_interface]
  Access objects of the LCIO package.  Functional only if this
  package is linked.
\item[hep\_events]
  Interface between the event record and the common blocks.
\item[eio\_ascii]
  Collection of event output formats that write ASCII files.
\item[eio\_lhef]
  LHEF for input and output.
\item[eio\_stdhep]
  Support for the StdHEP format (binary, machine-independent).
\item[eio\_hepmc]
  Support for the HepMC format (C++).
\item[eio\_lcio]
  Support for the LCIO format (C++).
\end{description}

%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\section{Generic Event Handling}
We introduce events first in form of an abstract type, together with
some utilities.  Abstract events can be used by other modules, in
particular event I/O, without introducing an explicit dependency on
the event implementation.

  use model_data
  use particles

     !private

     integer :: n_alt = 0

     real(default), dimension(:), allocatable :: sqme_alt
     logical :: weight_alt_known = .false.

\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{5}\nwdocspar
\subsection{Initialization}
This determines the number of alternate weights and sqme values.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{6}\moddef{Event base: generic event: TBP}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure :: base_init => generic_event_init
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{7}\moddef{Event base: procedures}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine generic_event_init (event, n_alt)
    class(generic_event_t), intent(out) :: event
    integer, intent(in) :: n_alt
    event%n_alt = n_alt
    allocate (event%sqme_alt (n_alt))
    allocate (event%weight_alt (n_alt))
  end subroutine generic_event_init

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{8}\nwdocspar
\subsection{Access particle set}
The particle set is the core of the event.  We allow access to it via
a pointer, and we maintain the information whether the particle set
is valid, i.e., has been filled with meaningful data.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{9}\moddef{Event base: generic event: TBP}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure :: has_valid_particle_set => generic_event_has_valid_particle_set
  procedure :: accept_particle_set => generic_event_accept_particle_set
  procedure :: discard_particle_set => generic_event_discard_particle_set
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{10}\moddef{Event base: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  function generic_event_has_valid_particle_set (event) result (flag)
    class(generic_event_t), intent(in) :: event
    logical :: flag
    flag = event%particle_set_is_valid
  end function generic_event_has_valid_particle_set

  subroutine generic_event_accept_particle_set (event)
    class(generic_event_t), intent(inout) :: event
    event%particle_set_is_valid = .true.
  end subroutine generic_event_accept_particle_set

  subroutine generic_event_discard_particle_set (event)
    class(generic_event_t), intent(inout) :: event
    event%particle_set_is_valid = .false.
  end subroutine generic_event_discard_particle_set

  procedure :: set => generic_event_set

  subroutine generic_event_set (event, &
       weight_ref, weight_prc, weight_alt, &
       excess_prc, &
       sqme_ref, sqme_prc, sqme_alt)
    class(generic_event_t), intent(inout) :: event
    real(default), intent(in), optional :: weight_ref, weight_prc
    real(default), intent(in), optional :: sqme_ref, sqme_prc
    real(default), dimension(:), intent(in), optional :: sqme_alt, weight_alt
    real(default), intent(in), optional :: excess_prc
    if (present (sqme_prc)) then
       call event%set_sqme_prc (sqme_prc)
    end if
    if (present (sqme_ref)) then
       call event%set_sqme_ref (sqme_ref)
    end if
    if (present (sqme_alt)) then
       call event%set_sqme_alt (sqme_alt)
    end if
    if (present (weight_prc)) then
       call event%set_weight_prc (weight_prc)
    end if
    if (present (weight_ref)) then
       call event%set_weight_ref (weight_ref)
    end if
    if (present (weight_alt)) then
       call event%set_weight_alt (weight_alt)
    end if
    if (present (excess_prc)) then
       call event%set_excess_prc (excess_prc)
    end if
  end subroutine generic_event_set

\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{62}\nwdocspar
\subsection{Event normalization}
The parameters for event normalization.  For unweighted events,
{\Tt{}NORM{\_}UNIT\nwendquote} is intended as default, while for weighted events, it is
{\Tt{}NORM{\_}SIGMA\nwendquote}.

Note: the unit test for this is in {\Tt{}eio{\_}data{\_}2\nwendquote} below.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{63}\moddef{Event base: parameters}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  integer, parameter, public :: NORM_UNDEFINED = 0
  integer, parameter, public :: NORM_UNIT = 1
  integer, parameter, public :: NORM_N_EVT = 2
  integer, parameter, public :: NORM_SIGMA = 3
  integer, parameter, public :: NORM_S_N = 4

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{64}These functions translate between the user representation and the
internal one.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{65}\moddef{Event base: public}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  public :: event_normalization_mode
  public :: event_normalization_string
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{66}\moddef{Event base: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  function event_normalization_mode (string, unweighted) result (mode)
    integer :: mode
    type(string_t), intent(in) :: string
    logical, intent(in) :: unweighted
    select case (lower_case (char (string)))
    case ("auto")
       if (unweighted) then
          mode = NORM_UNIT
       else
          mode = NORM_SIGMA
       end if
    case ("1")
       mode = NORM_UNIT
    case ("1/n")
       mode = NORM_N_EVT
    case ("sigma")
       mode = NORM_SIGMA
    case ("sigma/n")
       mode = NORM_S_N
    case default
       call msg_fatal ("Event normalization: unknown value '" &
            // char (string) // "'")
    end select
  end function event_normalization_mode

  function event_normalization_string (norm_mode) result (string)
    integer, intent(in) :: norm_mode
    type(string_t) :: string
    select case (norm_mode)
    case (NORM_UNDEFINED); string = "[undefined]"
    case (NORM_UNIT);      string = "'1'"
    case (NORM_N_EVT);     string = "'1/n'"
    case (NORM_SIGMA);     string = "'sigma'"
    case (NORM_S_N);       string = "'sigma/n'"
    case default;          string = "???"
    end select
  end function event_normalization_string

\eatline
\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{67}We place this here as a generic helper, so we can update event
weights whenever we need, not just in connection with an event sample
data object.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{68}\moddef{Event base: public}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  public :: event_normalization_update
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{69}\moddef{Event base: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine event_normalization_update (weight, sigma, n, mode_new, mode_old)
    real(default), intent(inout) :: weight
    real(default), intent(in) :: sigma
    integer, intent(in) :: n
    integer, intent(in) :: mode_new, mode_old
    if (mode_new /= mode_old) then
       if (sigma > 0 .and. n > 0) then
          weight = weight / factor (mode_old) * factor (mode_new)
       else
          call msg_fatal ("Event normalization update: null sample")
       end if
    end if
  contains
    function factor (mode)
      real(default) :: factor
      integer, intent(in) :: mode
      select case (mode)
      case (NORM_UNIT);   factor = 1._default
      case (NORM_N_EVT);  factor = 1._default / n
      case (NORM_SIGMA);  factor = sigma
      case (NORM_S_N);    factor = sigma / n
      case default
         call msg_fatal ("Event normalization update: undefined mode")
      end select
    end function factor
  end subroutine event_normalization_update

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{70}\nwdocspar
\subsection{Callback container}
This derived type contains a callback procedure that can
be executed during event I/O.  The callback procedure is given the
event object (with class {\Tt{}generic{\_}event\nwendquote}) and an event index.

This is a simple wrapper.  The object is abstract, so the the actual
procedure is introduced by overriding the deferred one.  We use the
PASS attribute, so we may supplement runtime data in the callback object
if desired.

  public :: event_callback_t
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{72}\moddef{Event base: types}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  type, abstract :: event_callback_t
     private
   contains
     procedure(event_callback_write), deferred :: write
     procedure(event_callback_proc), deferred :: proc
  end type event_callback_t

\eatline

     subroutine event_callback_write (event_callback, unit)

  end interface

\eatline

\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{83}\nwdocspar
\subsection{Event Sample Data}
These are data that apply to an event sample as a whole.  They are
given in an easily portable form (no fancy structure) and are used for
initializing event formats.

There are two MD5 sums here.  {\Tt{}md5sum{\_}proc\nwendquote} depends only on the
definition of the contributing processes.  A sample with matching
checksum can be rescanned with modified model parameters, beam
structure etc, to recalculate observables.  {\Tt{}md5sum{\_}config\nwendquote} includes
all relevant data.  Rescanning a sample with matching checksum will
produce identical observables.  (A third checksum might be added which
depends on the event sample itself.  This is not needed, so far.)

If alternate weights are part of the event sample ({\Tt{}n{\_}alt\nwendquote} nonzero),
there is a configuration MD5 sum for each of them.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{84}\moddef{EIO data: public}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  public :: event_sample_data_t
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{85}\moddef{EIO data: types}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  type :: event_sample_data_t
     character(32) :: md5sum_prc = ""
     character(32) :: md5sum_cfg = ""
     logical :: unweighted = .true.
     logical :: negative_weights = .false.
     integer :: norm_mode = NORM_UNDEFINED
     integer :: n_beam = 0
     integer, dimension(2) :: pdg_beam = 0
     real(default), dimension(2) :: energy_beam = 0
     integer :: n_proc = 0
     integer :: n_evt = 0
     integer :: nlo_multiplier = 1
     integer :: split_n_evt = 0
     integer :: split_n_kbytes = 0
     integer :: split_index = 0
     real(default) :: total_cross_section = 0
     integer, dimension(:), allocatable :: proc_num_id
     integer :: n_alt = 0
     character(32), dimension(:), allocatable :: md5sum_alt
     real(default), dimension(:), allocatable :: cross_section
     real(default), dimension(:), allocatable :: error
   contains
   \LA{}EIO data: event sample data: TBP\RA{}
  end type event_sample_data_t

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{86}Initialize: allocate for the number of processes
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{87}\moddef{EIO data: event sample data: TBP}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure :: init => event_sample_data_init
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{88}\moddef{EIO data: procedures}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine event_sample_data_init (data, n_proc, n_alt)
    class(event_sample_data_t), intent(out) :: data
    integer, intent(in) :: n_proc
    integer, intent(in), optional :: n_alt
    data%n_proc = n_proc
    allocate (data%proc_num_id (n_proc), source = 0)
    allocate (data%cross_section (n_proc), source = 0._default)
    allocate (data%error (n_proc), source = 0._default)
    if (present (n_alt)) then
       data%n_alt = n_alt
       allocate (data%md5sum_alt (n_alt))
       data%md5sum_alt = ""
    end if
  end subroutine event_sample_data_init

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{89}Output.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{90}\moddef{EIO data: event sample data: TBP}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure :: write => event_sample_data_write
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{91}\moddef{EIO data: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine event_sample_data_write (data, unit)
    class(event_sample_data_t), intent(in) :: data
    integer, intent(in), optional :: unit
    integer :: u, i
    u = given_output_unit (unit)
    write (u, "(1x,A)")  "Event sample properties:"
    write (u, "(3x,A,A,A)")  "MD5 sum (proc)   = '", data%md5sum_prc, "'"
    write (u, "(3x,A,A,A)")  "MD5 sum (config) = '", data%md5sum_cfg, "'"
    write (u, "(3x,A,L1)")  "unweighted       = ", data%unweighted
    write (u, "(3x,A,L1)")  "negative weights = ", data%negative_weights
    write (u, "(3x,A,A)")   "normalization    = ", &
         char (event_normalization_string (data%norm_mode))
    write (u, "(3x,A,I0)")  "number of beams  = ", data%n_beam
    write (u, "(5x,A,2(1x,I19))")  "PDG    = ", &
         data%pdg_beam(:data%n_beam)
    write (u, "(5x,A,2(1x,ES19.12))")  "Energy = ", &
         data%energy_beam(:data%n_beam)
    if (data%n_evt > 0) then
       write (u, "(3x,A,I0)")  "number of events = ", data%n_evt
    end if
    if (.not. vanishes (data%total_cross_section)) then
       write (u, "(3x,A,ES19.12)")  "total cross sec. = ", &
            data%total_cross_section
    end if
    write (u, "(3x,A,I0)")  "num of processes = ", data%n_proc
    do i = 1, data%n_proc
       write (u, "(3x,A,I0)")  "Process #", data%proc_num_id (i)
       select case (data%n_beam)
       case (1)
          write (u, "(5x,A,ES19.12)")  "Width = ", data%cross_section(i)
       case (2)
          write (u, "(5x,A,ES19.12)")  "CSec  = ", data%cross_section(i)
       end select
       write (u, "(5x,A,ES19.12)")  "Error = ", data%error(i)
    end do
    if (data%n_alt > 0) then
       write (u, "(3x,A,I0)")  "num of alt wgt   = ", data%n_alt
       do i = 1, data%n_alt
          write (u, "(5x,A,A,A,1x,I0)")  "MD5 sum (cfg)  = '", &
               data%md5sum_alt(i), "'", i
       end do
    end if
  end subroutine event_sample_data_write

\eatline

\subsubsection{Event Sample Data}
Print the contents of a sample data block.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{100}\moddef{EIO data: execute tests}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  call test (eio_data_1, "eio_data_1", &
       "event sample data", &
       u, results)
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{101}\moddef{EIO data: test declarations}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  public :: eio_data_1
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{102}\moddef{EIO data: tests}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine eio_data_1 (u)
    integer, intent(in) :: u
    type(event_sample_data_t) :: data

    write (u, "(A)")  "* Test output: eio_data_1"
    write (u, "(A)")  "*   Purpose:  display event sample data"
    write (u, "(A)")

    write (u, "(A)")  "* Decay process, one component"
    write (u, "(A)")

    call data%init (1, 1)
    data%n_beam = 1
    data%pdg_beam(1) = 25
    data%energy_beam(1) = 125

    data%norm_mode = NORM_UNIT

    data%proc_num_id = [42]
    data%cross_section = [1.23e-4_default]
    data%error = 5e-6_default

    data%md5sum_prc = "abcdefghijklmnopabcdefghijklmnop"
    data%md5sum_cfg = "12345678901234561234567890123456"
    data%md5sum_alt(1) = "uuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuu"

    call data%write (u)

    write (u, "(A)")
    write (u, "(A)")  "* Scattering process, two components"
    write (u, "(A)")

    call data%init (2)
    data%n_beam = 2
    data%pdg_beam = [2212, -2212]
    data%energy_beam = [8._default, 10._default]

    data%norm_mode = NORM_SIGMA

    data%proc_num_id = [12, 34]
    data%cross_section = [100._default, 88._default]
    data%error = [1._default, 0.1_default]

    call data%write (u)

    write (u, "(A)")
    write (u, "(A)")  "* Test output end: eio_data_1"

  end subroutine eio_data_1

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{103}\nwdocspar
\subsubsection{Event Normalization}
Check the functions for translating modes and updating weights.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{104}\moddef{EIO data: execute tests}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  call test (eio_data_2, "eio_data_2", &
       "event normalization", &
       u, results)
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{105}\moddef{EIO data: test declarations}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  public :: eio_data_2
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{106}\moddef{EIO data: tests}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine eio_data_2 (u)
    integer, intent(in) :: u
    type(string_t) :: s
    logical :: unweighted
    real(default) :: w, w0, sigma
    integer :: n

    write (u, "(A)")  "* Test output: eio_data_2"
    write (u, "(A)")  "*   Purpose:  handle event normalization"
    write (u, "(A)")

    write (u, "(A)")  "* Normalization strings"
    write (u, "(A)")

    s = "auto"
    unweighted = .true.
    write (u, "(1x,A,1x,L1,1x,A)")  char (s), unweighted, &
         char (event_normalization_string &
         (event_normalization_mode (s, unweighted)))
    s = "AUTO"
    unweighted = .false.
    write (u, "(1x,A,1x,L1,1x,A)")  char (s), unweighted, &
         char (event_normalization_string &
         (event_normalization_mode (s, unweighted)))

    unweighted = .true.

    s = "1"
    write (u, "(2(1x,A))") char (s), char (event_normalization_string &
         (event_normalization_mode (s, unweighted)))
    s = "1/n"
    write (u, "(2(1x,A))") char (s), char (event_normalization_string &
         (event_normalization_mode (s, unweighted)))
    s = "Sigma"
    write (u, "(2(1x,A))") char (s), char (event_normalization_string &
         (event_normalization_mode (s, unweighted)))
    s = "sigma/N"
    write (u, "(2(1x,A))") char (s), char (event_normalization_string &
         (event_normalization_mode (s, unweighted)))

    write (u, "(A)")
    write (u, "(A)")  "* Normalization update"
    write (u, "(A)")

    sigma = 5
    n = 2

    w0 = 1

    w = w0
    call event_normalization_update (w, sigma, n, NORM_UNIT, NORM_UNIT)
    write (u, "(2(F6.3))")  w0, w
    w = w0
    call event_normalization_update (w, sigma, n, NORM_N_EVT, NORM_UNIT)
    write (u, "(2(F6.3))")  w0, w
    w = w0
    call event_normalization_update (w, sigma, n, NORM_SIGMA, NORM_UNIT)
    write (u, "(2(F6.3))")  w0, w
    w = w0
    call event_normalization_update (w, sigma, n, NORM_S_N, NORM_UNIT)
    write (u, "(2(F6.3))")  w0, w

    write (u, *)

    w0 = 0.5

    w = w0
    call event_normalization_update (w, sigma, n, NORM_UNIT, NORM_N_EVT)
    write (u, "(2(F6.3))")  w0, w
    w = w0
    call event_normalization_update (w, sigma, n, NORM_N_EVT, NORM_N_EVT)
    write (u, "(2(F6.3))")  w0, w
    w = w0
    call event_normalization_update (w, sigma, n, NORM_SIGMA, NORM_N_EVT)
    write (u, "(2(F6.3))")  w0, w
    w = w0
    call event_normalization_update (w, sigma, n, NORM_S_N, NORM_N_EVT)
    write (u, "(2(F6.3))")  w0, w

    write (u, *)

    w0 = 5.0

    w = w0
    call event_normalization_update (w, sigma, n, NORM_UNIT, NORM_SIGMA)
    write (u, "(2(F6.3))")  w0, w
    w = w0
    call event_normalization_update (w, sigma, n, NORM_N_EVT, NORM_SIGMA)
    write (u, "(2(F6.3))")  w0, w
    w = w0
    call event_normalization_update (w, sigma, n, NORM_SIGMA, NORM_SIGMA)
    write (u, "(2(F6.3))")  w0, w
    w = w0
    call event_normalization_update (w, sigma, n, NORM_S_N, NORM_SIGMA)
    write (u, "(2(F6.3))")  w0, w

    write (u, *)

    w0 = 2.5

    w = w0
    call event_normalization_update (w, sigma, n, NORM_UNIT, NORM_S_N)
    write (u, "(2(F6.3))")  w0, w
    w = w0
    call event_normalization_update (w, sigma, n, NORM_N_EVT, NORM_S_N)
    write (u, "(2(F6.3))")  w0, w
    w = w0
    call event_normalization_update (w, sigma, n, NORM_SIGMA, NORM_S_N)
    write (u, "(2(F6.3))")  w0, w
    w = w0
    call event_normalization_update (w, sigma, n, NORM_S_N, NORM_S_N)
    write (u, "(2(F6.3))")  w0, w

    write (u, "(A)")
    write (u, "(A)")  "* Test output end: eio_data_2"

  end subroutine eio_data_2

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{107}\nwdocspar
%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\section{Abstract I/O Handler}

This module defines an abstract object for event I/O and the
associated methods.

There are {\Tt{}output\nwendquote} and {\Tt{}input\nwendquote} methods which
write or read a single event from/to the I/O stream, respectively.
The I/O stream itself may be a file, a common block, or an externally
linked structure, depending on the concrete implementation.

A {\Tt{}write\nwendquote} method prints the current content of the
implementation-dependent event record in human-readable form.

The {\Tt{}init{\_}in\nwendquote}/{\Tt{}init{\_}out\nwendquote} and {\Tt{}final\nwendquote} prepare
and finalize the I/O stream, respectively.  There is also a
{\Tt{}switch{\_}inout\nwendquote} method which turns an input stream into an output
stream where events can be appended.

Optionally, output files can be split in chunks of well-defined size.  The
{\Tt{}split{\_}out\nwendquote} method takes care of this.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{108}\moddef{\code{}eio{\_}base.f90\edoc{}}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
\LA{}File header\RA{}

module eio_base

  use kinds, only: i64
\LA{}Use strings\RA{}
  use io_units
  use diagnostics
  use model_data
  use event_base
  use eio_data

\LA{}Standard module head\RA{}

\LA{}EIO base: public\RA{}

\LA{}EIO base: types\RA{}

\LA{}EIO base: interfaces\RA{}

contains

\LA{}EIO base: procedures\RA{}

end module eio_base
\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{109}\nwdocspar
\subsection{Type}
We can assume that most implementations will need the file extension as a
fixed string and, if they support file splitting, the current file index.

The fallback model is useful for implementations that are able to read
unknown files which may contain hadrons etc., not in the current
hard-interaction model.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{110}\moddef{EIO base: public}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  public :: eio_t
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{111}\moddef{EIO base: types}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  type, abstract :: eio_t
     type(string_t) :: sample
     type(string_t) :: extension
     type(string_t) :: filename
     logical :: has_file = .false.
     logical :: split = .false.
     integer :: split_n_evt = 0
     integer :: split_n_kbytes = 0
     integer :: split_index = 0
     integer :: split_count = 0
     class(model_data_t), pointer :: fallback_model => null ()
   contains
   \LA{}EIO base: eio: TBP\RA{}
  end type eio_t

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{112}Write to screen.  If possible, this should display the contents of the
current event, i.e., the last one that was written or read.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{113}\moddef{EIO base: eio: TBP}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure (eio_write), deferred :: write
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{114}\moddef{EIO base: interfaces}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  abstract interface
     subroutine eio_write (object, unit)
       import
       class(eio_t), intent(in) :: object
       integer, intent(in), optional :: unit
     end subroutine eio_write
  end interface

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{115}Finalize.  This should write/read footer data and close input/output
channels.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{116}\moddef{EIO base: eio: TBP}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure (eio_final), deferred :: final
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{117}\moddef{EIO base: interfaces}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  abstract interface
     subroutine eio_final (object)
       import
       class(eio_t), intent(inout) :: object
     end subroutine eio_final
  end interface

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{118}Determine splitting parameters from the event sample data.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{119}\moddef{EIO base: eio: TBP}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure :: set_splitting => eio_set_splitting
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{120}\moddef{EIO base: procedures}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine eio_set_splitting (eio, data)
    class(eio_t), intent(inout) :: eio
    type(event_sample_data_t), intent(in) :: data
    eio%split = data%split_n_evt > 0 .or. data%split_n_kbytes > 0
    if (eio%split) then
       eio%split_n_evt = data%split_n_evt
       eio%split_n_kbytes = data%split_n_kbytes
       eio%split_index = data%split_index
       eio%split_count = 0
    end if
  end subroutine eio_set_splitting

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{121}Update the byte count and check if it has increased.  We use integer
division to determine the number of {\Tt{}n{\_}kbytes\nwendquote} blocks that are in
the event file.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{122}\moddef{EIO base: eio: TBP}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure :: update_split_count => eio_update_split_count
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{123}\moddef{EIO base: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine eio_update_split_count (eio, increased)
    class(eio_t), intent(inout) :: eio
    logical, intent(out) :: increased
    integer :: split_count_old
    if (eio%split_n_kbytes > 0) then
       split_count_old = eio%split_count
       eio%split_count = eio%file_size_kbytes () / eio%split_n_kbytes
       increased = eio%split_count > split_count_old
    end if
  end subroutine eio_update_split_count

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{124}Generate a filename, taking a possible split index into account.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{125}\moddef{EIO base: eio: TBP}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure :: set_filename => eio_set_filename
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{126}\moddef{EIO base: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine eio_set_filename (eio)
    class(eio_t), intent(inout) :: eio
    character(32) :: buffer
    if (eio%split) then
       write (buffer, "(I0,'.')")  eio%split_index
       eio%filename = eio%sample // "." // trim (buffer) // eio%extension
       eio%has_file = .true.
    else
       eio%filename = eio%sample // "." // eio%extension
       eio%has_file = .true.
    end if
  end subroutine eio_set_filename

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{127}Set the fallback model.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{128}\moddef{EIO base: eio: TBP}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure :: set_fallback_model => eio_set_fallback_model
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{129}\moddef{EIO base: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine eio_set_fallback_model (eio, model)
    class(eio_t), intent(inout) :: eio
    class(model_data_t), intent(in), target :: model
    eio%fallback_model => model
  end subroutine eio_set_fallback_model

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{130}Initialize for output.  We provide process names.  This should
open an event file if appropriate and write header data.  Some methods
may require event sample data.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{131}\moddef{EIO base: eio: TBP}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure (eio_init_out), deferred :: init_out
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{132}\moddef{EIO base: interfaces}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  abstract interface
     subroutine eio_init_out (eio, sample, data, success, extension)
       import
       class(eio_t), intent(inout) :: eio
       type(string_t), intent(in) :: sample
       type(event_sample_data_t), intent(in), optional :: data
       logical, intent(out), optional :: success
       type(string_t), intent(in), optional :: extension
     end subroutine eio_init_out
  end interface

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{133}Initialize for input.  We provide process names.  This should open an event
file if appropriate and read header data.  The {\Tt{}md5sum\nwendquote} can be used to check
the integrity of the configuration, it it provides a checksum to compare with.
In case the extension has changed the extension is also given as an argument.

The {\Tt{}data\nwendquote} argument is {\Tt{}intent(inout)\nwendquote}: we may read part of it and
keep other parts and/or check them against the data in the file.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{134}\moddef{EIO base: eio: TBP}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure (eio_init_in), deferred :: init_in
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{135}\moddef{EIO base: interfaces}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  abstract interface
     subroutine eio_init_in (eio, sample, data, success, extension)
       import
       class(eio_t), intent(inout) :: eio
       type(string_t), intent(in) :: sample
       type(event_sample_data_t), intent(inout), optional :: data
       logical, intent(out), optional :: success
       type(string_t), intent(in), optional :: extension
     end subroutine eio_init_in
  end interface

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{136}Re-initialize for output.  This should change the status of any event file
from input to output and position it for appending new events.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{137}\moddef{EIO base: eio: TBP}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure (eio_switch_inout), deferred :: switch_inout
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{138}\moddef{EIO base: interfaces}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  abstract interface
     subroutine eio_switch_inout (eio, success)
       import
       class(eio_t), intent(inout) :: eio
       logical, intent(out), optional :: success
     end subroutine eio_switch_inout
  end interface

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{139}This is similar: split the output, i.e., close the current file and open a
new one.  The default implementation does nothing.  For the feature to work,
an implementation must override this.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{140}\moddef{EIO base: eio: TBP}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure :: split_out => eio_split_out
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{141}\moddef{EIO base: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine eio_split_out (eio)
    class(eio_t), intent(inout) :: eio
  end subroutine eio_split_out

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{142}Determine the file size in kilobytes.  More exactly, determine the
size in units of 1024 storage units, as returned by the INQUIRE statement.

The implementation returns zero if there is no file.  The
{\Tt{}has{\_}file\nwendquote} flag is set by the {\Tt{}set{\_}filename\nwendquote} method, so we can be
confident that the {\Tt{}inquire\nwendquote} call is meaningful.  If this algorithm
doesn't apply for a particular format, we still can override the
procedure.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{143}\moddef{EIO base: eio: TBP}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure :: file_size_kbytes => eio_file_size_kbytes
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{144}\moddef{EIO base: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  function eio_file_size_kbytes (eio) result (kbytes)
    class(eio_t), intent(in) :: eio
    integer :: kbytes
    integer(i64) :: bytes
    if (eio%has_file) then
       inquire (file = char (eio%filename), size = bytes)
       if (bytes > 0) then
          kbytes = bytes / 1024
       else
          kbytes = 0
       end if
    else
       kbytes = 0
    end if
  end function eio_file_size_kbytes

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{145}Output an event.  All data can be taken from the {\Tt{}event\nwendquote} record.
The index {\Tt{}i{\_}prc\nwendquote} identifies the process among the processes that
are contained in the current sample.  The {\Tt{}reading\nwendquote} flag, if present,
indicates that the event was read from file, not generated.

The {\Tt{}passed\nwendquote} flag tells us that this event has passed the selection
criteria.  Depending on the event format, we may choose to skip events
that have not passed.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{146}\moddef{EIO base: eio: TBP}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure (eio_output), deferred :: output
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{147}\moddef{EIO base: interfaces}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  abstract interface
     subroutine eio_output (eio, event, i_prc, reading, passed, pacify)
       import
       class(eio_t), intent(inout) :: eio
       class(generic_event_t), intent(in), target :: event
       integer, intent(in) :: i_prc
       logical, intent(in), optional :: reading, passed, pacify
     end subroutine eio_output
  end interface

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{148}Input an event.  This should fill all event data that cannot be inferred
from the associated process.

The input is broken down into two parts.  First we read the {\Tt{}i{\_}prc\nwendquote}
index.  So we know which process to expect in the subsequent event.
If we have reached end of file, we also will know.
Then, we read the event itself.

The parameter {\Tt{}iostat\nwendquote} is supposed to be set as the Fortran standard
requires, negative for EOF and positive for error.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{149}\moddef{EIO base: eio: TBP}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure (eio_input_i_prc), deferred :: input_i_prc
  procedure (eio_input_event), deferred :: input_event
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{150}\moddef{EIO base: interfaces}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  abstract interface
     subroutine eio_input_i_prc (eio, i_prc, iostat)
       import
       class(eio_t), intent(inout) :: eio
       integer, intent(out) :: i_prc
       integer, intent(out) :: iostat
     end subroutine eio_input_i_prc
  end interface

  abstract interface
     subroutine eio_input_event (eio, event, iostat)
       import
       class(eio_t), intent(inout) :: eio
       class(generic_event_t), intent(inout), target :: event
       integer, intent(out) :: iostat
     end subroutine eio_input_event
  end interface

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{151}\nwdocspar
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{152}\moddef{EIO base: eio: TBP}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure (eio_skip), deferred :: skip
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{153}\moddef{EIO base: interfaces}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  abstract interface
     subroutine eio_skip (eio, iostat)
       import
       class(eio_t), intent(inout) :: eio
       integer, intent(out) :: iostat
     end subroutine eio_skip
  end interface

\eatline

\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{170}\nwdocspar
\subsubsection{Test type for event I/O}
The contents simulate the contents of an external file.  We have the
{\Tt{}sample\nwendquote} string as the file name and the array of momenta
{\Tt{}event{\_}p\nwendquote} as the list of events.  The
second index is the event index.  The {\Tt{}event{\_}i\nwendquote} component is the pointer
to the current event, {\Tt{}event{\_}n\nwendquote} is the total number of stored events.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{171}\moddef{EIO base: test types}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  type, extends (eio_t) :: eio_test_t
     integer :: event_n = 0
     integer :: event_i = 0
     integer :: i_prc = 0
     type(vector4_t), dimension(:,:), allocatable :: event_p
   contains
   \LA{}EIO base: eio test: TBP\RA{}
  end type eio_test_t

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{172}Write to screen.  Pretend that this is an actual event format.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{173}\moddef{EIO base: eio test: TBP}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure :: write => eio_test_write
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{174}\moddef{EIO base: test auxiliary}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine eio_test_write (object, unit)
    class(eio_test_t), intent(in) :: object
    integer, intent(in), optional :: unit
    integer :: u, i
    u = given_output_unit (unit)
    write (u, "(1x,A)")  "Test event stream"
    if (object%event_i /= 0) then
       write (u, "(1x,A,I0,A)")  "Event #", object%event_i, ":"
       do i = 1, size (object%event_p, 1)
          call vector4_write (object%event_p(i, object%event_i), u)
       end do
    end if
  end subroutine eio_test_write

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{175}Finalizer.  For the test case, we just reset the event count,
but keep the stored ``events''.  For the real implementations, the events
would be stored on an external medium, so we would delete the object
contents.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{176}\moddef{EIO base: eio test: TBP}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure :: final => eio_test_final
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{177}\moddef{EIO base: test auxiliary}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine eio_test_final (object)
    class(eio_test_t), intent(inout) :: object
    object%event_i = 0
  end subroutine eio_test_final

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{178}Initialization: We store the process IDs and the energy from the beam-data
object.  We also allocate the momenta (i.e., the simulated event record) for a
fixed maximum size of 10 events, 2 momenta each.  There is only a single
process.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{179}\moddef{EIO base: eio test: TBP}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure :: init_out => eio_test_init_out
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{180}\moddef{EIO base: test auxiliary}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine eio_test_init_out (eio, sample, data, success, extension)
    class(eio_test_t), intent(inout) :: eio
    type(string_t), intent(in) :: sample
    type(event_sample_data_t), intent(in), optional :: data
    logical, intent(out), optional :: success
    type(string_t), intent(in), optional :: extension
    eio%sample = sample
    eio%event_n = 0
    eio%event_i = 0
    allocate (eio%event_p (2, 10))
    if (present (success))  success = .true.
  end subroutine eio_test_init_out

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{181}Initialization for input.  Nothing to do for the test type.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{182}\moddef{EIO base: eio test: TBP}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure :: init_in => eio_test_init_in
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{183}\moddef{EIO base: test auxiliary}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine eio_test_init_in (eio, sample, data, success, extension)
    class(eio_test_t), intent(inout) :: eio
    type(string_t), intent(in) :: sample
    type(event_sample_data_t), intent(inout), optional :: data
    logical, intent(out), optional :: success
    type(string_t), intent(in), optional :: extension
    if (present (success))  success = .true.
  end subroutine eio_test_init_in

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{184}Switch from output to input.  Again, nothing to do for the test type.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{185}\moddef{EIO base: eio test: TBP}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure :: switch_inout => eio_test_switch_inout
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{186}\moddef{EIO base: test auxiliary}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine eio_test_switch_inout (eio, success)
    class(eio_test_t), intent(inout) :: eio
    logical, intent(out), optional :: success
    if (present (success))  success = .true.
  end subroutine eio_test_switch_inout

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{187}Output.  Increment the event counter and store the momenta of the current
event.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{188}\moddef{EIO base: eio test: TBP}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure :: output => eio_test_output
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{189}\moddef{EIO base: test auxiliary}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine eio_test_output (eio, event, i_prc, reading, passed, pacify)
    class(eio_test_t), intent(inout) :: eio
    class(generic_event_t), intent(in), target :: event
    logical, intent(in), optional :: reading, passed, pacify
    integer, intent(in) :: i_prc
    type(particle_set_t), pointer :: pset
    type(particle_t) :: prt
    eio%event_n = eio%event_n + 1
    eio%event_i = eio%event_n
    eio%i_prc = i_prc
    pset => event%get_particle_set_ptr ()
    prt = pset%get_particle (3)
    eio%event_p(1, eio%event_i) = prt%get_momentum ()
    prt = pset%get_particle (4)
    eio%event_p(2, eio%event_i) = prt%get_momentum ()
  end subroutine eio_test_output

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{190}Input.  Increment the event counter and retrieve the momenta of the current
event.  For the test case, we do not actually modify the current event.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{191}\moddef{EIO base: eio test: TBP}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure :: input_i_prc => eio_test_input_i_prc
  procedure :: input_event => eio_test_input_event
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{192}\moddef{EIO base: test auxiliary}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine eio_test_input_i_prc (eio, i_prc, iostat)
    class(eio_test_t), intent(inout) :: eio
    integer, intent(out) :: i_prc
    integer, intent(out) :: iostat
    i_prc = eio%i_prc
    iostat = 0
  end subroutine eio_test_input_i_prc

  subroutine eio_test_input_event (eio, event, iostat)
    class(eio_test_t), intent(inout) :: eio
    class(generic_event_t), intent(inout), target :: event
    integer, intent(out) :: iostat
    eio%event_i = eio%event_i + 1
    iostat = 0
  end subroutine eio_test_input_event

\eatline
\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{193}\nwdocspar
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{194}\moddef{EIO base: eio test: TBP}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure :: skip => eio_test_skip
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{195}\moddef{EIO base: test auxiliary}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine eio_test_skip (eio, iostat)
    class(eio_test_t), intent(inout) :: eio
    integer, intent(out) :: iostat
    iostat = 0
  end subroutine eio_test_skip

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{196}\nwdocspar
\subsubsection{Test I/O methods}
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{197}\moddef{EIO base: execute tests}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  call test (eio_base_1, "eio_base_1", &
       "read and write event contents", &
       u, results)
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{198}\moddef{EIO base: test declarations}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  public :: eio_base_1
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{199}\moddef{EIO base: tests}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine eio_base_1 (u)
    integer, intent(in) :: u
    class(generic_event_t), pointer :: event
    class(eio_t), allocatable :: eio
    integer :: i_prc,  iostat
    type(string_t) :: sample

    write (u, "(A)")  "* Test output: eio_base_1"
    write (u, "(A)")  "*   Purpose: generate and read/write an event"
    write (u, "(A)")

    write (u, "(A)")  "* Initialize test process"

    call eio_prepare_test (event, unweighted = .false.)

    write (u, "(A)")
    write (u, "(A)")  "* Generate and write an event"
    write (u, "(A)")

    sample = "eio_test1"

    allocate (eio_test_t :: eio)

    call eio%init_out (sample)
    call event%generate (1, [0._default, 0._default])
    call eio%output (event, 42)
    call eio%write (u)
    call eio%final ()

    write (u, "(A)")
    write (u, "(A)")  "* Re-read the event"
    write (u, "(A)")

    call eio%init_in (sample)
    call eio%input_i_prc (i_prc, iostat)
    call eio%input_event (event, iostat)
    call eio%write (u)
    write (u, "(A)")
    write (u, "(1x,A,I0)")  "i = ", i_prc

    write (u, "(A)")
    write (u, "(A)")  "* Generate and append another event"
    write (u, "(A)")

    call eio%switch_inout ()
    call event%generate (1, [0._default, 0._default])
    call eio%output (event, 5)
    call eio%write (u)
    call eio%final ()

    write (u, "(A)")
    write (u, "(A)")  "* Re-read both events"
    write (u, "(A)")

    call eio%init_in (sample)
    call eio%input_i_prc (i_prc, iostat)
    call eio%input_event (event, iostat)
    call eio%input_i_prc (i_prc, iostat)
    call eio%input_event (event, iostat)
    call eio%write (u)
    write (u, "(A)")
    write (u, "(1x,A,I0)")  "i = ", i_prc

    write (u, "(A)")
    write (u, "(A)")  "* Cleanup"

    call eio%final ()
    deallocate (eio)

    call eio_cleanup_test (event)

    write (u, "(A)")
    write (u, "(A)")  "* Test output end: eio_base_1"

  end subroutine eio_base_1

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{200}\nwdocspar
%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\section{Event Generation Checkpoints}
This is an output-only format.  Its only use is to write screen
messages every $n$ events, to inform the user about progress.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{201}\moddef{\code{}eio{\_}checkpoints.f90\edoc{}}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
\LA{}File header\RA{}

module eio_checkpoints

\LA{}Use strings\RA{}
  use io_units
  use diagnostics
  use cputime
  use event_base
  use eio_data
  use eio_base

\LA{}Standard module head\RA{}

\LA{}EIO checkpoints: public\RA{}

\LA{}EIO checkpoints: parameters\RA{}

\LA{}EIO checkpoints: types\RA{}

contains

\LA{}EIO checkpoints: procedures\RA{}

end module eio_checkpoints
\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{202}\nwdocspar
\subsection{Type}
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{203}\moddef{EIO checkpoints: public}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  public :: eio_checkpoints_t
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{204}\moddef{EIO checkpoints: types}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  type, extends (eio_t) :: eio_checkpoints_t
     logical :: active = .false.
     logical :: running = .false.
     integer :: val = 0
     integer :: n_events = 0
     integer :: n_read = 0
     integer :: i_evt = 0
     logical :: blank = .false.
     type(timer_t) :: timer
   contains
   \LA{}EIO checkpoints: eio checkpoints: TBP\RA{}
  end type eio_checkpoints_t

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{205}\nwdocspar
\subsection{Specific Methods}
Set parameters that are specifically used for checkpointing.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{206}\moddef{EIO checkpoints: eio checkpoints: TBP}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure :: set_parameters => eio_checkpoints_set_parameters
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{207}\moddef{EIO checkpoints: procedures}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine eio_checkpoints_set_parameters (eio, checkpoint, blank)
    class(eio_checkpoints_t), intent(inout) :: eio
    integer, intent(in) :: checkpoint
    logical, intent(in), optional :: blank
    eio%val = checkpoint
    if (present (blank))  eio%blank = blank
  end subroutine eio_checkpoints_set_parameters

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{208}\nwdocspar
\subsection{Common Methods}
Output.  This is not the actual event format, but a readable account
of the current status.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{209}\moddef{EIO checkpoints: eio checkpoints: TBP}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure :: write => eio_checkpoints_write
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{210}\moddef{EIO checkpoints: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine eio_checkpoints_write (object, unit)
    class(eio_checkpoints_t), intent(in) :: object
    integer, intent(in), optional :: unit
    integer :: u
    u = given_output_unit (unit)
    if (object%active) then
       write (u, "(1x,A)")  "Event-sample checkpoints:  active"
       write (u, "(3x,A,I0)")  "interval  = ", object%val
       write (u, "(3x,A,I0)")  "n_events  = ", object%n_events
       write (u, "(3x,A,I0)")  "n_read    = ", object%n_read
       write (u, "(3x,A,I0)")  "n_current = ", object%i_evt
       write (u, "(3x,A,L1)")  "blanking  = ", object%blank
       call object%timer%write (u)
    else
       write (u, "(1x,A)")  "Event-sample checkpoints:  off"
    end if
  end subroutine eio_checkpoints_write

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{211}Finalizer: trivial.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{212}\moddef{EIO checkpoints: eio checkpoints: TBP}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure :: final => eio_checkpoints_final
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{213}\moddef{EIO checkpoints: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine eio_checkpoints_final (object)
    class(eio_checkpoints_t), intent(inout) :: object
    object%active = .false.
  end subroutine eio_checkpoints_final

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{214}Activate checkpointing for event generation or writing.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{215}\moddef{EIO checkpoints: eio checkpoints: TBP}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure :: init_out => eio_checkpoints_init_out
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{216}\moddef{EIO checkpoints: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine eio_checkpoints_init_out (eio, sample, data, success, extension)
    class(eio_checkpoints_t), intent(inout) :: eio
    type(string_t), intent(in) :: sample
    type(string_t), intent(in), optional :: extension
    type(event_sample_data_t), intent(in), optional :: data
    logical, intent(out), optional :: success
    if (present (data)) then
       if (eio%val > 0) then
          eio%active = .true.
          eio%i_evt = 0
          eio%n_read = 0
          eio%n_events = data%n_evt * data%nlo_multiplier
       end if
    end if
    if (present (success))  success = .true.
  end subroutine eio_checkpoints_init_out

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{217}No checkpointing for event reading.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{218}\moddef{EIO checkpoints: eio checkpoints: TBP}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure :: init_in => eio_checkpoints_init_in
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{219}\moddef{EIO checkpoints: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine eio_checkpoints_init_in (eio, sample, data, success, extension)
    class(eio_checkpoints_t), intent(inout) :: eio
    type(string_t), intent(in) :: sample
    type(string_t), intent(in), optional :: extension
    type(event_sample_data_t), intent(inout), optional :: data
    logical, intent(out), optional :: success
    call msg_bug ("Event checkpoints: event input not supported")
    if (present (success))  success = .false.
  end subroutine eio_checkpoints_init_in

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{220}Switch from input to output: also not supported.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{221}\moddef{EIO checkpoints: eio checkpoints: TBP}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure :: switch_inout => eio_checkpoints_switch_inout
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{222}\moddef{EIO checkpoints: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine eio_checkpoints_switch_inout (eio, success)

    call msg_bug ("Event checkpoints: in-out switch not supported")
    if (present (success))  success = .false.
  end subroutine eio_checkpoints_switch_inout

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{223}Checkpoints: display progress for the current event, if applicable.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{224}\moddef{EIO checkpoints: eio checkpoints: TBP}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure :: output => eio_checkpoints_output
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{225}\moddef{EIO checkpoints: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine eio_checkpoints_output (eio, event, i_prc, reading, passed, pacify)
    class(eio_checkpoints_t), intent(inout) :: eio
    class(generic_event_t), intent(in), target :: event
    integer, intent(in) :: i_prc
    logical, intent(in), optional :: reading, passed, pacify
    logical :: rd
    rd = .false.;  if (present (reading))  rd = reading
    if (eio%active) then
       if (.not. eio%running)  call eio%startup ()
       if (eio%running) then
          eio%i_evt = eio%i_evt + 1
          if (rd) then
             eio%n_read = eio%n_read + 1
          else if (mod (eio%i_evt, eio%val) == 0) then
             call eio%message (eio%blank)
          end if
          if (eio%i_evt == eio%n_events)  call eio%shutdown ()
       end if
    end if
  end subroutine eio_checkpoints_output

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{226}When the first event is called, we have to initialize the screen output.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{227}\moddef{EIO checkpoints: eio checkpoints: TBP}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure :: startup => eio_checkpoints_startup
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{228}\moddef{EIO checkpoints: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine eio_checkpoints_startup (eio)
    class(eio_checkpoints_t), intent(inout) :: eio
    if (eio%active .and. eio%i_evt < eio%n_events) then
       call msg_message ("")
       call msg_message (checkpoint_bar)
       call msg_message (checkpoint_head)
       call msg_message (checkpoint_bar)
       write (msg_buffer, checkpoint_fmt) 0., 0, eio%n_events - eio%i_evt, "???"
       call msg_message ()
       eio%running = .true.
       call eio%timer%start ()
    end if
  end subroutine eio_checkpoints_startup

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{229}This message is printed at every checkpoint.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{230}\moddef{EIO checkpoints: eio checkpoints: TBP}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure :: message => eio_checkpoints_message
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{231}\moddef{EIO checkpoints: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine eio_checkpoints_message (eio, testflag)
    class(eio_checkpoints_t), intent(inout) :: eio
    logical, intent(in), optional :: testflag
    real :: t
    type(time_t) :: time_remaining
    type(string_t) :: time_string
    call eio%timer%stop ()
    t = eio%timer
    call eio%timer%restart ()
    time_remaining = &
         nint (t / (eio%i_evt - eio%n_read) * (eio%n_events - eio%i_evt))
    time_string = time_remaining%to_string_ms (blank = testflag)
    write (msg_buffer, checkpoint_fmt) &
         100 * (eio%i_evt - eio%n_read) / real (eio%n_events - eio%n_read), &
         eio%i_evt - eio%n_read, &
         eio%n_events - eio%i_evt, &
         char (time_string)
    call msg_message ()
  end subroutine eio_checkpoints_message

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{232}When the last event is called, wrap up.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{233}\moddef{EIO checkpoints: eio checkpoints: TBP}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure :: shutdown => eio_checkpoints_shutdown
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{234}\moddef{EIO checkpoints: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine eio_checkpoints_shutdown (eio)
    class(eio_checkpoints_t), intent(inout) :: eio
    if (mod (eio%i_evt, eio%val) /= 0) then
       write (msg_buffer, checkpoint_fmt) &
            100., eio%i_evt - eio%n_read, 0, "0m:00s"
       call msg_message ()
    end if
    call msg_message (checkpoint_bar)
    call msg_message ("")
    eio%running = .false.
  end subroutine eio_checkpoints_shutdown

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{235}\moddef{EIO checkpoints: eio checkpoints: TBP}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure :: input_i_prc => eio_checkpoints_input_i_prc
  procedure :: input_event => eio_checkpoints_input_event
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{236}\moddef{EIO checkpoints: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine eio_checkpoints_input_i_prc (eio, i_prc, iostat)
    class(eio_checkpoints_t), intent(inout) :: eio
    integer, intent(out) :: i_prc
    integer, intent(out) :: iostat
    call msg_bug ("Event checkpoints: event input not supported")
    i_prc = 0
    iostat = 1
  end subroutine eio_checkpoints_input_i_prc

  subroutine eio_checkpoints_input_event (eio, event, iostat)
    class(eio_checkpoints_t), intent(inout) :: eio
    class(generic_event_t), intent(inout), target :: event
    integer, intent(out) :: iostat

    iostat = 1
  end subroutine eio_checkpoints_input_event

\eatline
\eatline

\subsubsection{Test I/O methods}
We test the implementation of all I/O methods.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{250}\moddef{EIO checkpoints: execute tests}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  call test (eio_checkpoints_1, "eio_checkpoints_1", &
       "read and write event contents", &
       u, results)
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{251}\moddef{EIO checkpoints: test declarations}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  public :: eio_checkpoints_1
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{252}\moddef{EIO checkpoints: tests}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine eio_checkpoints_1 (u)
    integer, intent(in) :: u
    class(generic_event_t), pointer :: event
    class(eio_t), allocatable :: eio
    type(event_sample_data_t) :: data
    type(string_t) :: sample
    integer :: i, n_events

    write (u, "(A)")  "* Test output: eio_checkpoints_1"
    write (u, "(A)")  "*   Purpose: generate a number of events &
         &with screen output"
    write (u, "(A)")

    write (u, "(A)")  "* Initialize test process"

    call eio_prepare_test (event)

    write (u, "(A)")
    write (u, "(A)")  "* Generate events"
    write (u, "(A)")

    sample = "eio_checkpoints_1"

    allocate (eio_checkpoints_t :: eio)

    n_events = 10
    call data%init (1, 0)
    data%n_evt = n_events

    select type (eio)
    type is (eio_checkpoints_t)
       call eio%set_parameters (checkpoint = 4)
    end select

    call eio%init_out (sample, data)

    do i = 1, n_events
       call event%generate (1, [0._default, 0._default])
       call eio%output (event, i_prc = 0)
    end do

    write (u, "(A)")  "* Checkpointing status"
    write (u, "(A)")

    call eio%write (u)
    call eio%final ()

    write (u, "(A)")
    write (u, "(A)")  "* Cleanup"

    call eio_cleanup_test (event)

    write (u, "(A)")
    write (u, "(A)")  "* Test output end: eio_checkpoints_1"

  end subroutine eio_checkpoints_1

\eatline

  use kinds, only: i64
\LA{}Use strings\RA{}
  use io_units

  use cputime
  use event_base
  use eio_data
  use eio_base

\LA{}Standard module head\RA{}

\LA{}EIO callback: public\RA{}

\LA{}EIO callback: types\RA{}

contains

\LA{}EIO callback: procedures\RA{}

end module eio_callback
\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{255}\nwdocspar
\subsection{Type}
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{256}\moddef{EIO callback: public}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  public :: eio_callback_t
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{257}\moddef{EIO callback: types}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  type, extends (eio_t) :: eio_callback_t
     class(event_callback_t), allocatable :: callback
     integer(i64) :: i_evt = 0
     integer :: i_interval = 0
     integer :: n_interval = 0
!      type(timer_t) :: timer
   contains
   \LA{}EIO callback: eio callback: TBP\RA{}
  end type eio_callback_t

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{258}\nwdocspar
\subsection{Specific Methods}
Set parameters that are specifically used for callback: the procedure
and the number of events to wait until the procedure is called (again).
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{259}\moddef{EIO callback: eio callback: TBP}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure :: set_parameters => eio_callback_set_parameters
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{260}\moddef{EIO callback: procedures}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine eio_callback_set_parameters (eio, callback, count_interval)
    class(eio_callback_t), intent(inout) :: eio
    class(event_callback_t), intent(in) :: callback
    integer, intent(in) :: count_interval
    allocate (eio%callback, source = callback)
    eio%n_interval = count_interval
  end subroutine eio_callback_set_parameters

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{261}\nwdocspar
\subsection{Common Methods}
Output.  This is not the actual event format, but a readable account
of the current status.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{262}\moddef{EIO callback: eio callback: TBP}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure :: write => eio_callback_write
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{263}\moddef{EIO callback: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine eio_callback_write (object, unit)
    class(eio_callback_t), intent(in) :: object
    integer, intent(in), optional :: unit
    integer :: u
    u = given_output_unit (unit)
    write (u, "(1x,A)")  "Event-sample callback:"
    write (u, "(3x,A,I0)")  "interval  = ", object%n_interval
    write (u, "(3x,A,I0)")  "evt count = ", object%i_evt
!        call object%timer%write (u)
  end subroutine eio_callback_write

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{264}Finalizer: trivial.

    class(eio_callback_t), intent(inout) :: object
  end subroutine eio_callback_final

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{267}Activate checkpointing for event generation or writing.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{268}\moddef{EIO callback: eio callback: TBP}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure :: init_out => eio_callback_init_out
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{269}\moddef{EIO callback: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine eio_callback_init_out (eio, sample, data, success, extension)
    class(eio_callback_t), intent(inout) :: eio
    type(string_t), intent(in) :: sample
    type(string_t), intent(in), optional :: extension
    type(event_sample_data_t), intent(in), optional :: data
    logical, intent(out), optional :: success
    eio%i_evt = 0
    eiO%i_interval = 0
    if (present (success))  success = .true.
  end subroutine eio_callback_init_out

\eatline

    call msg_bug ("Event callback: event input not supported")
    if (present (success))  success = .false.
  end subroutine eio_callback_init_in

\eatline

\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{274}\moddef{EIO callback: eio callback: TBP}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup

\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{275}\moddef{EIO callback: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup

    class(eio_callback_t), intent(inout) :: eio
    logical, intent(out), optional :: success
    call msg_bug ("Event callback: in-out switch not supported")
    if (present (success))  success = .false.
  end subroutine eio_callback_switch_inout

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{276}The actual callback.  First increment counters, then call the
procedure if the counter hits the interval.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{277}\moddef{EIO callback: eio callback: TBP}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure :: output => eio_callback_output
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{278}\moddef{EIO callback: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine eio_callback_output (eio, event, i_prc, reading, passed, pacify)
    class(eio_callback_t), intent(inout) :: eio
    class(generic_event_t), intent(in), target :: event
    integer, intent(in) :: i_prc
    logical, intent(in), optional :: reading, passed, pacify
    eio%i_evt = eio%i_evt + 1
    if (eio%n_interval > 0) then
       eio%i_interval = eio%i_interval + 1
       if (eio%i_interval >= eio%n_interval) then
          call eio%callback%proc (eio%i_evt, event)
          eio%i_interval = 0
       end if
    end if
  end subroutine eio_callback_output

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{279}No input.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{280}\moddef{EIO callback: eio callback: TBP}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup

    i_prc = 0

This is an output-only format.  For each event, we print the indices
that identify process, process part (MCI group), and term.  As
numerical information we print the squared matrix element (trace) and
the event weight.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{286}\moddef{\code{}eio{\_}weights.f90\edoc{}}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup

\LA{}Standard module head\RA{}

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{287}\nwdocspar
\subsection{Type}
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{288}\moddef{EIO weights: public}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  public :: eio_weights_t
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{289}\moddef{EIO weights: types}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  type, extends (eio_t) :: eio_weights_t
     logical :: writing = .false.
     integer :: unit = 0

   contains
   \LA{}EIO weights: eio weights: TBP\RA{}
  end type eio_weights_t

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{290}\nwdocspar
\subsection{Specific Methods}
Set pacify flags.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{291}\moddef{EIO weights: eio weights: TBP}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure :: set_parameters => eio_weights_set_parameters
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{292}\moddef{EIO weights: procedures}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine eio_weights_set_parameters (eio, pacify)
    class(eio_weights_t), intent(inout) :: eio
    logical, intent(in), optional :: pacify
    if (present (pacify))  eio%pacify = pacify
    eio%extension = "weights.dat"
  end subroutine eio_weights_set_parameters

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{293}\nwdocspar
\subsection{Common Methods}
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegindocs{294}Output.  This is not the actual event format, but a readable account
of the current object status.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{295}\moddef{EIO weights: eio weights: TBP}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure :: write => eio_weights_write
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{296}\moddef{EIO weights: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine eio_weights_write (object, unit)
    class(eio_weights_t), intent(in) :: object
    integer, intent(in), optional :: unit
    integer :: u
    u = given_output_unit (unit)
    write (u, "(1x,A)")  "Weight stream:"
    if (object%writing) then
       write (u, "(3x,A,A)")  "Writing to file   = ", char (object%filename)
       write (u, "(3x,A,L1)") "Reduced I/O prec. = ", object%pacify
    else
       write (u, "(3x,A)")  "[closed]"
    end if
  end subroutine eio_weights_write

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{297}Finalizer: close any open file.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{298}\moddef{EIO weights: eio weights: TBP}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure :: final => eio_weights_final
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{299}\moddef{EIO weights: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine eio_weights_final (object)
    class(eio_weights_t), intent(inout) :: object
    if (object%writing) then
       write (msg_buffer, "(A,A,A)")  "Events: closing weight stream file '", &
            char (object%filename), "'"
       call msg_message ()
       close (object%unit)
       object%writing = .false.
    end if
  end subroutine eio_weights_final

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{300}Initialize event writing.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{301}\moddef{EIO weights: eio weights: TBP}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure :: init_out => eio_weights_init_out
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{302}\moddef{EIO weights: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine eio_weights_init_out (eio, sample, data, success, extension)
    class(eio_weights_t), intent(inout) :: eio
    type(string_t), intent(in) :: sample
    type(string_t), intent(in), optional :: extension
    type(event_sample_data_t), intent(in), optional :: data
    logical, intent(out), optional :: success
    if (present(extension)) then
       eio%extension = extension
    else
       eio%extension = "weights.dat"
    end if
    eio%filename = sample // "." // eio%extension
    eio%unit = free_unit ()
    write (msg_buffer, "(A,A,A)")  "Events: writing to weight stream file '", &
         char (eio%filename), "'"
    call msg_message ()
    eio%writing = .true.
    open (eio%unit, file = char (eio%filename), &
         action = "write", status = "replace")
    if (present (success))  success = .true.
  end subroutine eio_weights_init_out

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{303}Initialize event reading.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{304}\moddef{EIO weights: eio weights: TBP}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure :: init_in => eio_weights_init_in
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{305}\moddef{EIO weights: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine eio_weights_init_in (eio, sample, data, success, extension)
    class(eio_weights_t), intent(inout) :: eio
    type(string_t), intent(in) :: sample
    type(string_t), intent(in), optional :: extension
    type(event_sample_data_t), intent(inout), optional :: data
    logical, intent(out), optional :: success
    call msg_bug ("Weight stream: event input not supported")
    if (present (success))  success = .false.
  end subroutine eio_weights_init_in

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{306}Switch from input to output: reopen the file for reading.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{307}\moddef{EIO weights: eio weights: TBP}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure :: switch_inout => eio_weights_switch_inout
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{308}\moddef{EIO weights: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine eio_weights_switch_inout (eio, success)
    class(eio_weights_t), intent(inout) :: eio
    logical, intent(out), optional :: success
    call msg_bug ("Weight stream: in-out switch not supported")
    if (present (success))  success = .false.
  end subroutine eio_weights_switch_inout

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{309}Output an event.  Write first the event indices, then weight and two
values of the squared matrix element: {\Tt{}sqme{\_}ref\nwendquote} is the value stored
in the event record, and {\Tt{}sqme{\_}prc\nwendquote} is the one stored in the process
instance.  (They can differ: when recalculating, the former is read
from file and the latter is the result of the new calculation.)

For the alternative entries, the {\Tt{}sqme\nwendquote} value is always obtained by
a new calculation, and thus qualifies as {\Tt{}sqme{\_}prc\nwendquote}.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{310}\moddef{EIO weights: eio weights: TBP}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure :: output => eio_weights_output
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{311}\moddef{EIO weights: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine eio_weights_output (eio, event, i_prc, reading, passed, pacify)
    class(eio_weights_t), intent(inout) :: eio
    class(generic_event_t), intent(in), target :: event
    integer, intent(in) :: i_prc
    logical, intent(in), optional :: reading, passed, pacify
    integer :: n_alt, i
    real(default) :: weight, sqme_ref, sqme_prc
    if (eio%writing) then
       weight = event%get_weight_prc ()
       sqme_ref = event%get_sqme_ref ()
       sqme_prc = event%get_sqme_prc ()
       n_alt = event%get_n_alt ()
1      format (I0,3(1x,ES17.10),3(1x,I0))
2      format (I0,3(1x,ES15.8),3(1x,I0))
       if (eio%pacify) then
          write (eio%unit, 2)  0, weight, sqme_prc, sqme_ref, &
               i_prc
       else
          write (eio%unit, 1)  0, weight, sqme_prc, sqme_ref, &
               i_prc
       end if
       do i = 1, n_alt
          weight = event%get_weight_alt(i)
          sqme_prc = event%get_sqme_alt(i)
          if (eio%pacify) then
             write (eio%unit, 2)  i, weight, sqme_prc
          else
             write (eio%unit, 1)  i, weight, sqme_prc
          end if
       end do
    else
       call eio%write ()
       call msg_fatal ("Weight stream file is not open for writing")
    end if
  end subroutine eio_weights_output

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{312}Input an event.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{313}\moddef{EIO weights: eio weights: TBP}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure :: input_i_prc => eio_weights_input_i_prc
  procedure :: input_event => eio_weights_input_event
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{314}\moddef{EIO weights: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine eio_weights_input_i_prc (eio, i_prc, iostat)
    class(eio_weights_t), intent(inout) :: eio
    integer, intent(out) :: i_prc
    integer, intent(out) :: iostat
    call msg_bug ("Weight stream: event input not supported")
    i_prc = 0
    iostat = 1
  end subroutine eio_weights_input_i_prc

  subroutine eio_weights_input_event (eio, event, iostat)
    class(eio_weights_t), intent(inout) :: eio
    class(generic_event_t), intent(inout), target :: event
    integer, intent(out) :: iostat
    call msg_bug ("Weight stream: event input not supported")
    iostat = 1
  end subroutine eio_weights_input_event

\eatline
