  public :: vamp2_3
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{305}\moddef{vamp2: tests}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine vamp2_3 (u)
    integer, intent(in) :: u
    type(vamp2_t) :: mc_integrator
    class(rng_t), allocatable :: rng
    class(vamp2_func_t), allocatable :: func
    real(default), dimension(2), parameter :: x_lower = 0., &
         x_upper = 1.
    real(default) :: result, abserr
    integer :: unit

    write (u, "(A)") "* Test output: vamp2_3"
    write (u, "(A)") "*   Purpose:  intgeration of two-dimensional &
       & function with two channels"
    write (u, "(A)")

    write (u, "(A)") "* Initialise random number generator (default seed)"
    write (u, "(A)")

    allocate (rng_stream_t :: rng)
    call rng%init ()

    call rng%write (u)

    write (u, "(A)")
    write (u, "(A)") "* Initialise MC integrator with n_channel = 1 and n_dim = 3"
    write (u, "(A)")

    allocate (vamp2_test_func_2_t :: func)
    call func%init (n_dim = 2, n_channel = 2)
    mc_integrator = vamp2_t (2, 2)
    call mc_integrator%write (u)

    write (u, "(A)")
    write (u, "(A)") "* Initialise grid with n_calls = 20000"
    write (u, "(A)")

    call mc_integrator%set_limits (x_lower, x_upper)
    call mc_integrator%set_calls (20000)

    write (u, "(A)")
    write (u, "(A)") "* Integrate with n_it = 3 and n_calls = 20000 (Adaptation)"
    write (u, "(A)")

    call mc_integrator%integrate (func, rng, 3, result=result, abserr=abserr)
    write (u,  "(2x,A," // FMT_12 // ",A," // FMT_12 // ")") "Result: ", result, " +/- ", abserr

    write (u, "(A)")
    write (u, "(A)") "* Write grid to file vamp2_3.grids"
    write (u, "(A)")

    unit = free_unit ()
    open (unit, file = "vamp2_3.grids", &
         action = "write", status = "replace")
    call mc_integrator%write_grids (unit)
    close (unit)

    write (u, "(A)")
    write (u, "(A)") "* Read grid from file vamp2_3.grids"
    write (u, "(A)")

    call mc_integrator%final ()

    unit = free_unit ()
    open (unit, file = "vamp2_3.grids", &
         action = "read", status = "old")
    call mc_integrator%read_grids (unit)
    close (unit)

    write (u, "(A)")
    write (u, "(A)") "* Integrate with n_it = 3 and n_calls = 5000 (Precision)"
    write (u, "(A)")

    call mc_integrator%set_calls (5000)
    call mc_integrator%integrate (func, rng, 3, result=result, abserr=abserr)
    write (u,  "(2x,A," // FMT_12 // ",A," // FMT_12 // ")") "Result: ", result, " +/- ", abserr

    write (u, "(A)")
    write (u, "(A)") "* Cleanup"

    call mc_integrator%final ()
    call rng%final ()
    deallocate (rng)
  end subroutine vamp2_3

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{306}Integrate a function with two-dimensional argument and two channels.
Use chained weights, although we average over each weight itself.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{307}\moddef{vamp2: execute tests}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  call test (vamp2_4, "vamp2_4", "VAMP2 intgeration of two-dimensional &
       & function with two channels with chains", u, results)
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{308}\moddef{vamp2: test declaration}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  public :: vamp2_4
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{309}\moddef{vamp2: tests}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine vamp2_4 (u)
    integer, intent(in) :: u
    type(vamp2_t) :: mc_integrator
    class(rng_t), allocatable :: rng
    class(vamp2_func_t), allocatable :: func
    real(default), dimension(2), parameter :: x_lower = 0., &
         x_upper = 1.
    real(default) :: result, abserr
    integer :: unit

    write (u, "(A)") "* Test output: vamp2_4"
    write (u, "(A)") "*   Purpose:  intgeration of two-dimensional &
       & function with two channels with chains"
    write (u, "(A)")

    write (u, "(A)") "* Initialise random number generator (default seed)"
    write (u, "(A)")

    allocate (rng_stream_t :: rng)
    call rng%init ()

    call rng%write (u)

    write (u, "(A)")
    write (u, "(A)") "* Initialise MC integrator with n_channel = 2 and n_dim = 2"
    write (u, "(A)")

    allocate (vamp2_test_func_2_t :: func)
    call func%init (n_dim = 2, n_channel = 2)
    mc_integrator = vamp2_t (2, 2)
    call mc_integrator%write (u)

    write (u, "(A)")
    write (u, "(A)") "* Initialise grid with n_calls = 20000 and set chains"
    write (u, "(A)")

    call mc_integrator%set_limits (x_lower, x_upper)
    call mc_integrator%set_calls (20000)
    call mc_integrator%set_chain (2, [1, 2])

    write (u, "(A)")
    write (u, "(A)") "* Integrate with n_it = 3 and n_calls = 10000 (Adaptation)"
    write (u, "(A)")

    call mc_integrator%integrate (func, rng, 3, result=result, abserr=abserr)
    write (u,  "(2x,A," // FMT_12 // ",A," // FMT_12 // ")") "Result: ", result, " +/- ", abserr

    write (u, "(A)")
    write (u, "(A)") "* Write grid to file vamp2_4.grids"
    write (u, "(A)")

    unit = free_unit ()
    open (unit, file = "vamp2_4.grids", &
         action = "write", status = "replace")
    call mc_integrator%write_grids (unit)
    close (unit)

    write (u, "(A)")
    write (u, "(A)") "* Read grid from file vamp2_4.grids"
    write (u, "(A)")

    call mc_integrator%final ()

    unit = free_unit ()
    open (unit, file = "vamp2_4.grids", &
         action = "read", status = "old")
    call mc_integrator%read_grids (unit)
    close (unit)

    write (u, "(A)")
    write (u, "(A)") "* Integrate with n_it = 3 and n_calls = 5000 (Precision)"
    write (u, "(A)")

    call mc_integrator%set_calls (5000)
    call mc_integrator%integrate (func, rng, 3, result=result, abserr=abserr)
    write (u,  "(2x,A," // FMT_12 // ",A," // FMT_12 // ")") "Result: ", result, " +/- ", abserr

    write (u, "(A)")
    write (u, "(A)") "* Cleanup"

    call mc_integrator%final ()
    call rng%final ()
    deallocate (rng)
  end subroutine vamp2_4

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{310}\nwdocspar
\nwenddocs{}\nwfilename{../../../src/mci/mci.nw}\nwbegindocs{0}%% -*- ess-noweb-default-code-mode: f90-mode; noweb-default-code-mode: f90-mode; -*-
% WHIZARD code as NOWEB source: integration and event generation
%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\chapter{Multi-Channel Integration}
\includemodulegraph{mci}

The abstract representation of multi-channel
Monte Carlo algorithms for integration and event generation.
\begin{description}
\item[Module {\Tt{}mci{\_}base\nwendquote}:]
  The abstract types and their methods.  It provides a test integrator
  that is referenced in later unit tests.
\item[iterations]
  Container for defining integration call and pass settings.
\item[integration\_results]
  This module handles results from integrating processes.  It records passes
  and iterations, calculates statistical averages, and provides the user
  output of integration results.
\end{description}

These are the implementations:
\begin{description}
\item[Module {\Tt{}mci{\_}midpoint\nwendquote}:]
  A simple integrator that uses the midpoint rule to sample the
  integrand uniformly over the unit hypercube.  There is only one
  integration channel, so this can be matched only to single-channel
  phase space.
\item[Module {\Tt{}mci{\_}vamp\nwendquote}:]
  Interface for the VAMP package.
\end{description}


%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\clearpage
\section{Generic Integrator}
This module provides a multi-channel integrator (MCI) base type, a
corresponding configuration type, and methods for integration and event
generation.

\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{1}\moddef{\code{}mci{\_}base.f90\edoc{}}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
\LA{}File header\RA{}

module mci_base

  use kinds
  use io_units
  use format_utils, only: pac_fmt
  use format_defs, only: FMT_14, FMT_17
  use diagnostics
  use cputime
  use phs_base
  use rng_base

\LA{}Standard module head\RA{}

\LA{}MCI base: public\RA{}

\LA{}MCI base: types\RA{}

\LA{}MCI base: interfaces\RA{}

contains

\LA{}MCI base: procedures\RA{}

end module mci_base
\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{2}\nwdocspar
\subsection{MCI: integrator}
The MCI object contains the methods for integration and event generation.
For the actual work and data storage, it spawns an MCI instance object.

The base object contains the number of integration dimensions and the number
of channels as configuration data.  Further configuration data are stored in
the concrete extensions.

The MCI sum contains all relevant information about the integrand.  It can be
used for comparing the current configuration against a previous one.  If they
match, we can skip an actual integration.  (Implemented only for the VAMP
version.)

There is a random-number generator (its state with associated methods)
available as {\Tt{}rng\nwendquote}.  It may or may not be used for integration.  It
will be used for event generation.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{3}\moddef{MCI base: public}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  public :: mci_t
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{4}\moddef{MCI base: types}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  type, abstract :: mci_t
     integer :: n_dim = 0
     integer :: n_channel = 0
     integer :: n_chain = 0
     integer, dimension(:), allocatable :: chain
     real(default), dimension(:), allocatable :: chain_weights
     character(32) :: md5sum = ""
     logical :: integral_known = .false.
     logical :: error_known = .false.
     logical :: efficiency_known = .false.
     real(default) :: integral = 0
     real(default) :: error = 0
     real(default) :: efficiency = 0
     logical :: use_timer = .false.
     type(timer_t) :: timer
     class(rng_t), allocatable :: rng
   contains
   \LA{}MCI base: mci: TBP\RA{}
  end type mci_t

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{5}Finalizer: the random-number generator may need one.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{6}\moddef{MCI base: mci: TBP}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure :: base_final => mci_final
  procedure (mci_final), deferred :: final
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{7}\moddef{MCI base: procedures}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine mci_final (object)
    class(mci_t), intent(inout) :: object
    if (allocated (object%rng))  call object%rng%final ()
  end subroutine mci_final

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{8}Output: basic and extended output.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{9}\moddef{MCI base: mci: TBP}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure :: base_write => mci_write
  procedure (mci_write), deferred :: write
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{10}\moddef{MCI base: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine mci_write (object, unit, pacify, md5sum_version)
    class(mci_t), intent(in) :: object
    integer, intent(in), optional :: unit
    logical, intent(in), optional :: pacify
    logical, intent(in), optional :: md5sum_version
    logical :: md5sum_ver
    integer :: u, i, j
    character(len=7) :: fmt
    call pac_fmt (fmt, FMT_17, FMT_14, pacify)
    u = given_output_unit (unit)
    md5sum_ver = .false.
    if (present (md5sum_version))  md5sum_ver = md5sum_version
    if (object%use_timer .and. .not. md5sum_ver) then
       write (u, "(2x)", advance="no")
       call object%timer%write (u)
    end if
    if (object%integral_known) then
       write (u, "(3x,A," // fmt // ")") &
            "Integral             = ", object%integral
    end if
    if (object%error_known) then
       write (u, "(3x,A," // fmt // ")") &
            "Error                = ", object%error
    end if
    if (object%efficiency_known) then
       write (u, "(3x,A," // fmt // ")")  &
            "Efficiency           = ", object%efficiency
    end if
    write (u, "(3x,A,I0)")  "Number of channels   = ", object%n_channel
    write (u, "(3x,A,I0)")  "Number of dimensions = ", object%n_dim
    if (object%n_chain > 0) then
       write (u, "(3x,A,I0)")  "Number of chains     = ", object%n_chain
       write (u, "(3x,A)")  "Chains:"
       do i = 1, object%n_chain
          write (u, "(5x,I0,':')", advance = "no")  i
          do j = 1, object%n_channel
             if (object%chain(j) == i) &
                  write (u, "(1x,I0)", advance = "no")  j
          end do
          write (u, "(A)")
       end do
    end if
  end subroutine mci_write

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{11}Print an informative message when starting integration.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{12}\moddef{MCI base: mci: TBP}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure (mci_startup_message), deferred :: startup_message
  procedure :: base_startup_message => mci_startup_message
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{13}\moddef{MCI base: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine mci_startup_message (mci, unit, n_calls)
    class(mci_t), intent(in) :: mci
    integer, intent(in), optional :: unit, n_calls
    if (mci%n_chain > 0) then
       write (msg_buffer, "(A,3(1x,I0,1x,A))") &
            "Integrator:", mci%n_chain, "chains,", &
            mci%n_channel, "channels,", &
            mci%n_dim, "dimensions"
    else
       write (msg_buffer, "(A,3(1x,I0,1x,A))") &
            "Integrator:", &
            mci%n_channel, "channels,", &
            mci%n_dim, "dimensions"
    end if
    call msg_message (unit = unit)
  end subroutine mci_startup_message

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{14}Dump type-specific info to a logfile.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{15}\moddef{MCI base: mci: TBP}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure(mci_write_log_entry), deferred :: write_log_entry
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{16}\moddef{MCI base: interfaces}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  abstract interface
     subroutine mci_write_log_entry (mci, u)
       import
       class(mci_t), intent(in) :: mci
       integer, intent(in) :: u
     end subroutine mci_write_log_entry
  end interface

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{17}In order to avoid dependencies on definite MCI implementations,
we introduce a MD5 sum calculator.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{18}\moddef{MCI base: mci: TBP}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure(mci_compute_md5sum), deferred :: compute_md5sum
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{19}\moddef{MCI base: interfaces}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  abstract interface
     subroutine mci_compute_md5sum (mci, pacify)
       import
       class(mci_t), intent(inout) :: mci
       logical, intent(in), optional :: pacify
     end subroutine mci_compute_md5sum
  end interface

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{20}Record the index of the MCI object within a process.  For
multi-component processes with more than one integrator, the
integrator should know about its own index, so file names can be
unique, etc.  The default implementation does nothing, however.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{21}\moddef{MCI base: mci: TBP}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure :: record_index => mci_record_index
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{22}\moddef{MCI base: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine mci_record_index (mci, i_mci)
    class(mci_t), intent(inout) :: mci
    integer, intent(in) :: i_mci
  end subroutine mci_record_index

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{23}There is no Initializer for the abstract type, but a generic setter
for the number of channels and dimensions.  We make two aliases
available, to be able to override it.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{24}\moddef{MCI base: mci: TBP}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure :: set_dimensions => mci_set_dimensions
  procedure :: base_set_dimensions => mci_set_dimensions
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{25}\moddef{MCI base: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine mci_set_dimensions (mci, n_dim, n_channel)
    class(mci_t), intent(inout) :: mci
    integer, intent(in) :: n_dim
    integer, intent(in) :: n_channel
    mci%n_dim = n_dim
    mci%n_channel = n_channel
  end subroutine mci_set_dimensions

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{26}Declare particular dimensions as flat.  This information can be used
to simplify integration.  When generating events, the flat dimensions
should be sampled with uniform and uncorrelated distribution.  It
depends on the integrator what to do with that information.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{27}\moddef{MCI base: mci: TBP}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure (mci_declare_flat_dimensions), deferred :: declare_flat_dimensions
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{28}\moddef{MCI base: interfaces}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  abstract interface
     subroutine mci_declare_flat_dimensions (mci, dim_flat)
       import
       class(mci_t), intent(inout) :: mci
       integer, dimension(:), intent(in) :: dim_flat
     end subroutine mci_declare_flat_dimensions
  end interface

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{29}Declare particular channels as equivalent, possibly allowing for
permutations or reflections of dimensions.  We use the information
stored in the {\Tt{}phs{\_}channel{\_}t\nwendquote} object array that the phase-space module
provides.

(We do not test this here, deferring the unit test to the {\Tt{}mci{\_}vamp\nwendquote}
implementation where we actually use this feature.)
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{30}\moddef{MCI base: mci: TBP}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure (mci_declare_equivalences), deferred :: declare_equivalences
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{31}\moddef{MCI base: interfaces}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  abstract interface
     subroutine mci_declare_equivalences (mci, channel, dim_offset)
       import
       class(mci_t), intent(inout) :: mci
       type(phs_channel_t), dimension(:), intent(in) :: channel
       integer, intent(in) :: dim_offset
     end subroutine mci_declare_equivalences
  end interface

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{32}Declare particular channels as chained together.  The implementation may use
this array for keeping their weights equal to each other, etc.

The chain array is an array sized by the number of channels.  For each
channel, there is an integer entry that indicates the correponding
chains.  The total number of chains is the maximum value of this
entry.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{33}\moddef{MCI base: mci: TBP}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure :: declare_chains => mci_declare_chains
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{34}\moddef{MCI base: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine mci_declare_chains (mci, chain)
    class(mci_t), intent(inout) :: mci
    integer, dimension(:), intent(in) :: chain
    allocate (mci%chain (size (chain)))
    mci%n_chain = maxval (chain)
    allocate (mci%chain_weights (mci%n_chain), source = 0._default)
    mci%chain = chain
  end subroutine mci_declare_chains

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{35}Collect channel weights according to chains and store them in the
{\Tt{}chain{\_}weights\nwendquote} for output.  We sum up the weights for all channels that
share the same {\Tt{}chain\nwendquote} index and store the results in the {\Tt{}chain{\_}weights\nwendquote}
array.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{36}\moddef{MCI base: mci: TBP}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure :: collect_chain_weights => mci_collect_chain_weights
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{37}\moddef{MCI base: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine mci_collect_chain_weights (mci, weight)
    class(mci_t), intent(inout) :: mci
    real(default), dimension(:), intent(in) :: weight
    integer :: i, c
    if (allocated (mci%chain)) then
       mci%chain_weights = 0
       do i = 1, size (mci%chain)
          c = mci%chain(i)
          mci%chain_weights(c) = mci%chain_weights(c) + weight(i)
       end do
    end if
  end subroutine mci_collect_chain_weights

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{38}Check if there are chains.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{39}\moddef{MCI base: mci: TBP}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure :: has_chains => mci_has_chains
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{40}\moddef{MCI base: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  function mci_has_chains (mci) result (flag)
    class(mci_t), intent(in) :: mci
    logical :: flag
    flag = allocated (mci%chain)
  end function mci_has_chains

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{41}Output of the chain weights, kept separate from the main {\Tt{}write\nwendquote} method.

[The formatting will work as long as the number of chains is less than
  $10^{10}$\ldots]
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{42}\moddef{MCI base: mci: TBP}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure :: write_chain_weights => mci_write_chain_weights
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{43}\moddef{MCI base: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine mci_write_chain_weights (mci, unit)
    class(mci_t), intent(in) :: mci
    integer, intent(in), optional :: unit
    integer :: u, i, n, n_digits
    character(4) :: ifmt
    u = given_output_unit (unit)
    if (allocated (mci%chain_weights)) then
       write (u, "(1x,A)")  "Weights of channel chains (groves):"
       n_digits = 0
       n = size (mci%chain_weights)
       do while (n > 0)
          n = n / 10
          n_digits = n_digits + 1
       end do
       write (ifmt, "(A1,I1)") "I", n_digits
       do i = 1, size (mci%chain_weights)
          write (u, "(3x," // ifmt // ",F13.10)")  i, mci%chain_weights(i)
       end do
    end if
  end subroutine mci_write_chain_weights

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{44}Set the MD5 sum, independent of initialization.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{45}\moddef{MCI base: mci: TBP}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure :: set_md5sum => mci_set_md5sum
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{46}\moddef{MCI base: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine mci_set_md5sum (mci, md5sum)
    class(mci_t), intent(inout) :: mci
    character(32), intent(in) :: md5sum
    mci%md5sum = md5sum
  end subroutine mci_set_md5sum

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{47}Initialize a new integration pass.  This is not necessarily
meaningful, so we provide an empty base method.  The {\Tt{}mci{\_}vamp\nwendquote}
implementation overrides this.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{48}\moddef{MCI base: mci: TBP}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure :: add_pass => mci_add_pass
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{49}\moddef{MCI base: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine mci_add_pass (mci, adapt_grids, adapt_weights, final_pass)
    class(mci_t), intent(inout) :: mci
    logical, intent(in), optional :: adapt_grids
    logical, intent(in), optional :: adapt_weights
    logical, intent(in), optional :: final_pass
  end subroutine mci_add_pass

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{50}Allocate an instance with matching type.  This must be deferred.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{51}\moddef{MCI base: mci: TBP}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure (mci_allocate_instance), deferred :: allocate_instance
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{52}\moddef{MCI base: interfaces}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  abstract interface
     subroutine mci_allocate_instance (mci, mci_instance)
       import
       class(mci_t), intent(in) :: mci
       class(mci_instance_t), intent(out), pointer :: mci_instance
     end subroutine mci_allocate_instance
  end interface

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{53}Import a random-number generator.  We transfer the allocation of an
existing generator state into the object.  The generator state may
already be initialized, or we can reset it by its {\Tt{}init\nwendquote}
method.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{54}\moddef{MCI base: mci: TBP}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure :: import_rng => mci_import_rng
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{55}\moddef{MCI base: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine mci_import_rng (mci, rng)
    class(mci_t), intent(inout) :: mci
    class(rng_t), intent(inout), allocatable :: rng
    call move_alloc (rng, mci%rng)
  end subroutine mci_import_rng

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{56}Activate or deactivate the timer.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{57}\moddef{MCI base: mci: TBP}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure :: set_timer => mci_set_timer
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{58}\moddef{MCI base: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine mci_set_timer (mci, active)
    class(mci_t), intent(inout) :: mci
    logical, intent(in) :: active
    mci%use_timer = active
  end subroutine mci_set_timer

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{59}Start and stop signal for the timer, if active.  The elapsed time
can then be retrieved from the MCI record.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{60}\moddef{MCI base: mci: TBP}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure :: start_timer => mci_start_timer
  procedure :: stop_timer => mci_stop_timer
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{61}\moddef{MCI base: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine mci_start_timer (mci)
    class(mci_t), intent(inout) :: mci
    if (mci%use_timer)  call mci%timer%start ()
  end subroutine mci_start_timer

  subroutine mci_stop_timer (mci)
    class(mci_t), intent(inout) :: mci
    if (mci%use_timer)  call mci%timer%stop ()
  end subroutine mci_stop_timer

\eatline
\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{62}Sampler test.  Evaluate the sampler a given number of times.  Results are
discarded, so we don't need the MCI instance which would record them.

The evaluation channel is iterated, and the {\Tt{}x\nwendquote} parameters are randomly
chosen.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{63}\moddef{MCI base: mci: TBP}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure :: sampler_test => mci_sampler_test
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{64}\moddef{MCI base: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine mci_sampler_test (mci, sampler, n_calls)
    class(mci_t), intent(inout) :: mci
    class(mci_sampler_t), intent(inout), target :: sampler
    integer, intent(in) :: n_calls
    real(default), dimension(:), allocatable :: x_in, f
    real(default), dimension(:,:), allocatable :: x_out
    real(default) :: val
    integer :: i, c
    allocate (x_in (mci%n_dim))
    allocate (f (mci%n_channel))
    allocate (x_out (mci%n_dim, mci%n_channel))
    do i = 1, n_calls
       c = mod (i, mci%n_channel) + 1
       call mci%rng%generate_array (x_in)
       call sampler%evaluate (c, x_in, val, x_out, f)
    end do
  end subroutine mci_sampler_test

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{65}Integrate: this depends on the implementation. We foresee a pacify
flag to take care of small numerical noise on different platforms.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{66}\moddef{MCI base: mci: TBP}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure (mci_integrate), deferred :: integrate
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{67}\moddef{MCI base: interfaces}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  abstract interface
     subroutine mci_integrate (mci, instance, sampler, &
          n_it, n_calls, results, pacify)
       import
       class(mci_t), intent(inout) :: mci
       class(mci_instance_t), intent(inout), target :: instance
       class(mci_sampler_t), intent(inout), target :: sampler
       integer, intent(in) :: n_it
       integer, intent(in) :: n_calls
       logical, intent(in), optional :: pacify
       class(mci_results_t), intent(inout), optional :: results
     end subroutine mci_integrate
  end interface

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{68}Event generation.  Depending on the implementation,
event generation may or may not require a previous integration pass.

Instead of a black-box {\Tt{}simulate\nwendquote} method, we require an initializer,
a finalizer, and procedures for generating a single event.  This
allows us to interface simulation event by event from the outside, and
it facilitates the further processing of an event after successful
generation.  For integration, this is not necessary.

The initializer has {\Tt{}intent(inout)\nwendquote} for the {\Tt{}mci\nwendquote} passed object.  The
reason is that the initializer can read integration results and grids from
file, where the results can modify the {\Tt{}mci\nwendquote} record.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{69}\moddef{MCI base: mci: TBP}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure (mci_prepare_simulation), deferred :: prepare_simulation
\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{70}\moddef{MCI base: interfaces}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  abstract interface
     subroutine mci_prepare_simulation (mci)
       import
       class(mci_t), intent(inout) :: mci
     end subroutine mci_prepare_simulation
  end interface

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{71}\nwdocspar
The generated event will reside in in the {\Tt{}instance\nwendquote} object (overall
results and weight) and in the {\Tt{}sampler\nwendquote} object (detailed data).  In
the real application, we can subsequently call methods of the
{\Tt{}sampler\nwendquote} in order to further process the generated event.

The {\Tt{}target\nwendquote} attributes are required by the VAMP implementation,
which uses pointers to refer to the instance and sampler objects from
within the integration function.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{72}\moddef{MCI base: mci: TBP}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure (mci_generate), deferred :: generate_weighted_event
  procedure (mci_generate), deferred :: generate_unweighted_event
\eatline
\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{73}\moddef{MCI base: interfaces}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  abstract interface
     subroutine mci_generate (mci, instance, sampler)
       import
       class(mci_t), intent(inout) :: mci
       class(mci_instance_t), intent(inout), target :: instance
       class(mci_sampler_t), intent(inout), target :: sampler
     end subroutine mci_generate
  end interface

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{74}This is analogous, but we rebuild the event from the information
stored in {\Tt{}state\nwendquote} instead of generating it.

Note: currently unused outside of tests, might be deleted later.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{75}\moddef{MCI base: mci: TBP}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure (mci_rebuild), deferred :: rebuild_event
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{76}\moddef{MCI base: interfaces}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  abstract interface
     subroutine mci_rebuild (mci, instance, sampler, state)
       import
       class(mci_t), intent(inout) :: mci
       class(mci_instance_t), intent(inout) :: instance
       class(mci_sampler_t), intent(inout) :: sampler
       class(mci_state_t), intent(in) :: state
     end subroutine mci_rebuild
  end interface

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{77}\nwdocspar
Pacify: reduce numerical noise.  The base implementation does nothing.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{78}\moddef{MCI base: mci: TBP}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure :: pacify => mci_pacify
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{79}\moddef{MCI base: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine mci_pacify (object, efficiency_reset, error_reset)
    class(mci_t), intent(inout) :: object
    logical, intent(in), optional :: efficiency_reset, error_reset
  end subroutine mci_pacify

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{80}\nwdocspar
Return the value of the integral, error, efficiency, and time per call.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{81}\moddef{MCI base: mci: TBP}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure :: get_integral => mci_get_integral
  procedure :: get_error => mci_get_error
  procedure :: get_efficiency => mci_get_efficiency
  procedure :: get_time => mci_get_time
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{82}\moddef{MCI base: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  function mci_get_integral (mci) result (integral)
    class(mci_t), intent(in) :: mci
    real(default) :: integral
    if (mci%integral_known) then
       integral = mci%integral
    else
       call msg_bug ("The integral is unknown. This is presumably a" // &
            "WHIZARD bug.")
    end if
  end function mci_get_integral

  function mci_get_error (mci) result (error)
    class(mci_t), intent(in) :: mci
    real(default) :: error
    if (mci%error_known) then
       error = mci%error
    else
       error = 0
    end if
  end function mci_get_error

  function mci_get_efficiency (mci) result (efficiency)
    class(mci_t), intent(in) :: mci
    real(default) :: efficiency
    if (mci%efficiency_known) then
       efficiency = mci%efficiency
    else
       efficiency = 0
    end if
  end function mci_get_efficiency

  function mci_get_time (mci) result (time)
    class(mci_t), intent(in) :: mci
    real(default) :: time
    if (mci%use_timer) then
       time = mci%timer
    else
       time = 0
    end if
  end function mci_get_time

\eatline
\eatline
\eatline
\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{83}Return the MD5 sum of the configuration.  This may be overridden in
an extension, to return a different MD5 sum.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{84}\moddef{MCI base: mci: TBP}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure :: get_md5sum => mci_get_md5sum
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{85}\moddef{MCI base: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  pure function mci_get_md5sum (mci) result (md5sum)
    class(mci_t), intent(in) :: mci
    character(32) :: md5sum
    md5sum = mci%md5sum
  end function mci_get_md5sum

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{86}\nwdocspar
\subsection{MCI instance}
The base type contains an array of channel weights.  The value {\Tt{}mci{\_}weight\nwendquote}
is the combined MCI weight that corresponds to a particular sampling point.

For convenience, we also store the {\Tt{}x\nwendquote} and Jacobian values for this sampling
point.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{87}\moddef{MCI base: public}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  public :: mci_instance_t
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{88}\moddef{MCI base: types}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  type, abstract :: mci_instance_t
     logical :: valid = .false.
     real(default), dimension(:), allocatable :: w
     real(default), dimension(:), allocatable :: f
     real(default), dimension(:,:), allocatable :: x
     integer :: selected_channel = 0
     real(default) :: mci_weight = 0
     real(default) :: integrand  = 0
     logical :: negative_weights = .false.
   contains
   \LA{}MCI base: mci instance: TBP\RA{}
  end type mci_instance_t

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{89}Output: deferred
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{90}\moddef{MCI base: mci instance: TBP}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure (mci_instance_write), deferred :: write
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{91}\moddef{MCI base: interfaces}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  abstract interface
     subroutine mci_instance_write (object, unit, pacify)
       import
       class(mci_instance_t), intent(in) :: object
       integer, intent(in), optional :: unit
       logical, intent(in), optional :: pacify
     end subroutine mci_instance_write
  end interface

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{92}A finalizer, just in case.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{93}\moddef{MCI base: mci instance: TBP}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure (mci_instance_final), deferred :: final
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{94}\moddef{MCI base: interfaces}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  abstract interface
     subroutine mci_instance_final (object)
       import
       class(mci_instance_t), intent(inout) :: object
     end subroutine mci_instance_final
  end interface

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{95}Init: basic initializer for the arrays, otherwise deferred.  Assigning
the {\Tt{}mci\nwendquote} object is also deferred, because it depends on the concrete type.

The weights are initialized with an uniform normalized value.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{96}\moddef{MCI base: mci instance: TBP}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure (mci_instance_base_init), deferred :: init
  procedure :: base_init => mci_instance_base_init
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{97}\moddef{MCI base: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine mci_instance_base_init (mci_instance, mci)
    class(mci_instance_t), intent(out) :: mci_instance
    class(mci_t), intent(in), target :: mci
    allocate (mci_instance%w (mci%n_channel))
    allocate (mci_instance%f (mci%n_channel))
    allocate (mci_instance%x (mci%n_dim, mci%n_channel))
    if (mci%n_channel > 0) then
       call mci_instance%set_channel_weights &
            (spread (1._default, dim=1, ncopies=mci%n_channel))
    end if
    mci_instance%f = 0
    mci_instance%x = 0
  end subroutine mci_instance_base_init

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{98}Explicitly set the array of channel weights.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{99}\moddef{MCI base: mci instance: TBP}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure :: set_channel_weights => mci_instance_set_channel_weights
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{100}\moddef{MCI base: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine mci_instance_set_channel_weights (mci_instance, weights, sum_non_zero)
    class(mci_instance_t), intent(inout) :: mci_instance
    real(default), dimension(:), intent(in) :: weights
    logical, intent(out), optional :: sum_non_zero
    real(default) :: wsum
    wsum = sum (weights)
    if (wsum /= 0) then
       mci_instance%w = weights / wsum
       if (present (sum_non_zero)) sum_non_zero = .true.
    else
       if (present (sum_non_zero)) sum_non_zero = .false.
       call msg_warning ("MC sampler initialization:&
            & sum of channel weights is zero")
    end if
  end subroutine mci_instance_set_channel_weights

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{101}Compute the overall weight factor for a configuration of $x$ values and
Jacobians $f$.  The $x$ values come in {\Tt{}n{\_}channel\nwendquote} rows with {\Tt{}n{\_}dim\nwendquote}
entries each.  The $f$ factors constitute an array with {\Tt{}n{\_}channel\nwendquote} entries.

We assume that the $x$ and $f$ arrays are already stored inside the MC
instance.  The result is also stored there.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{102}\moddef{MCI base: mci instance: TBP}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure (mci_instance_compute_weight), deferred :: compute_weight
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{103}\moddef{MCI base: interfaces}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  abstract interface
     subroutine mci_instance_compute_weight (mci, c)
       import
       class(mci_instance_t), intent(inout) :: mci
       integer, intent(in) :: c
     end subroutine mci_instance_compute_weight
  end interface

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{104}Record the integrand as returned by the sampler.  Depending on the
implementation, this may merely copy the value, or do more complicated things.

We may need the MCI weight for the actual computations, so this should
be called after the previous routine.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{105}\moddef{MCI base: mci instance: TBP}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure (mci_instance_record_integrand), deferred :: record_integrand
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{106}\moddef{MCI base: interfaces}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  abstract interface
     subroutine mci_instance_record_integrand (mci, integrand)
       import
       class(mci_instance_t), intent(inout) :: mci
       real(default), intent(in) :: integrand
     end subroutine mci_instance_record_integrand
  end interface

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{107}Sample a point directly: evaluate the sampler, then compute the weight and
the weighted integrand.  Finally, record the integrand within the MCI instance.

If a signal (interrupt) was raised recently, we abort the calculation before
entering the sampler.  Thus, a previous calculation will have
completed and any data are already recorded, but any new point can be
discarded.  If the {\Tt{}abort\nwendquote} flag is present, we may delay the interrupt, so
we can do some cleanup.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{108}\moddef{MCI base: mci instance: TBP}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure :: evaluate => mci_instance_evaluate
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{109}\moddef{MCI base: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine mci_instance_evaluate (mci, sampler, c, x)
    class(mci_instance_t), intent(inout) :: mci
    class(mci_sampler_t), intent(inout) :: sampler
    integer, intent(in) :: c
    real(default), dimension(:), intent(in) :: x
    real(default) :: val
    call sampler%evaluate (c, x, val, mci%x, mci%f)
    mci%valid = sampler%is_valid ()
    if (mci%valid) then
       call mci%compute_weight (c)
       call mci%record_integrand (val)
    end if
  end subroutine mci_instance_evaluate

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{110}Initiate and terminate simulation.  In contrast to integration, we implement
these as methods of the process instance, since the {\Tt{}mci\nwendquote} configuration
object is unchanged.

The safety factor reduces the acceptance probability for unweighted
events.  The implementation of this feature depends on the concrete type.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{111}\moddef{MCI base: mci instance: TBP}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure (mci_instance_init_simulation), deferred :: init_simulation
  procedure (mci_instance_final_simulation), deferred :: final_simulation
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{112}\moddef{MCI base: interfaces}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  abstract interface
     subroutine mci_instance_init_simulation (instance, safety_factor)
       import
       class(mci_instance_t), intent(inout) :: instance
       real(default), intent(in), optional :: safety_factor
     end subroutine mci_instance_init_simulation
  end interface

  abstract interface
     subroutine mci_instance_final_simulation (instance)
       import
       class(mci_instance_t), intent(inout) :: instance
     end subroutine mci_instance_final_simulation
  end interface

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{113}Assuming that the sampler is in a completely defined state, just
extract the data that {\Tt{}evaluate\nwendquote} would compute.  Also record the integrand.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{114}\moddef{MCI base: mci instance: TBP}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure :: fetch => mci_instance_fetch
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{115}\moddef{MCI base: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine mci_instance_fetch (mci, sampler, c)
    class(mci_instance_t), intent(inout) :: mci
    class(mci_sampler_t), intent(in) :: sampler
    integer, intent(in) :: c
    real(default) :: val
    mci%valid = sampler%is_valid ()
    if (mci%valid) then
       call sampler%fetch (val, mci%x, mci%f)
       call mci%compute_weight (c)
       call mci%record_integrand (val)
    end if
  end subroutine mci_instance_fetch

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{116}The value, i.e., the weighted integrand, is the integrand (which
should be taken as-is from the sampler) multiplied by the MCI weight.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{117}\moddef{MCI base: mci instance: TBP}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure :: get_value => mci_instance_get_value
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{118}\moddef{MCI base: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  function mci_instance_get_value (mci) result (value)
    class(mci_instance_t), intent(in) :: mci
    real(default) :: value
    if (mci%valid) then
       value = mci%integrand * mci%mci_weight
    else
       value = 0
    end if
  end function mci_instance_get_value

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{119}This is an extra routine.  By default, the event weight is equal to
the value returned by the previous routine.  However, if we select a
channel for event generation not just based on the channel weights,
the event weight has to account for this bias, so the event weight
that applies to event generation is different.  In that case, we
should override the default routine.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{120}\moddef{MCI base: mci instance: TBP}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure :: get_event_weight => mci_instance_get_value
\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{121}Excess weight can occur during unweighted event generation, if the
assumed maximum value of the integrand is too small.  This excess
should be normalized in the same way as the event weight above (which
for unweighted events becomes unity).
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{122}\moddef{MCI base: mci instance: TBP}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure (mci_instance_get_event_excess), deferred :: get_event_excess
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{123}\moddef{MCI base: interfaces}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  abstract interface
     function mci_instance_get_event_excess (mci) result (excess)
       import
       class(mci_instance_t), intent(in) :: mci
       real(default) :: excess
     end function mci_instance_get_event_excess
  end interface

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{124}\nwdocspar
\subsection{MCI state}
This object can hold the relevant information that allows us to
reconstruct the MCI instance without re-evaluating the sampler completely.

We store the {\Tt{}x{\_}in\nwendquote} MC input parameter set, which coincides with the
section of the complete {\Tt{}x\nwendquote} array that belongs to a particular
channel.  We also store the MC function value.  When we want to
reconstruct the state, we can use the input array to recover the
complete {\Tt{}x\nwendquote} and {\Tt{}f\nwendquote} arrays (i.e., the kinematics), but do not
need to recompute the MC function value (the dynamics).

The {\Tt{}mci{\_}state{\_}t\nwendquote} may be extended, to allow storing/recalling more
information.  In that case, we would override the type-bound
procedures.  However, the base type is also a concrete type and
self-contained.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{125}\moddef{MCI base: public}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  public :: mci_state_t
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{126}\moddef{MCI base: types}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  type :: mci_state_t
     integer :: selected_channel = 0
     real(default), dimension(:), allocatable :: x_in
     real(default) :: val
   contains
   \LA{}MCI base: mci state: TBP\RA{}
  end type mci_state_t

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{127}Output:
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{128}\moddef{MCI base: mci state: TBP}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure :: write => mci_state_write
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{129}\moddef{MCI base: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine mci_state_write (object, unit)
    class(mci_state_t), intent(in) :: object
    integer, intent(in), optional :: unit
    integer :: u
    u = given_output_unit (unit)
    write (u, "(1x,A)")  "MCI state:"
    write (u, "(3x,A,I0)")  "Channel   = ", object%selected_channel
    write (u, "(3x,A,999(1x,F12.10))")  "x (in)    =", object%x_in
    write (u, "(3x,A,ES19.12)")  "Integrand = ", object%val
  end subroutine mci_state_write

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{130}To store the object, we take the relevant section of the {\Tt{}x\nwendquote}
array.  The channel used for storing data is taken from the
{\Tt{}instance\nwendquote} object, but it could be arbitrary in principle.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{131}\moddef{MCI base: mci instance: TBP}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure :: store => mci_instance_store
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{132}\moddef{MCI base: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine mci_instance_store (mci, state)
    class(mci_instance_t), intent(in) :: mci
    class(mci_state_t), intent(out) :: state
    state%selected_channel = mci%selected_channel
    allocate (state%x_in (size (mci%x, 1)))
    state%x_in = mci%x(:,mci%selected_channel)
    state%val = mci%integrand
  end subroutine mci_instance_store

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{133}Recalling the state, we must consult the sampler in order to fully
reconstruct the {\Tt{}x\nwendquote} and {\Tt{}f\nwendquote} arrays.  The integrand value is known,
and we also give it to the sampler, bypassing evaluation.

The final steps are equivalent to the {\Tt{}evaluate\nwendquote} method above.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{134}\moddef{MCI base: mci instance: TBP}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure :: recall => mci_instance_recall
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{135}\moddef{MCI base: procedures}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine mci_instance_recall (mci, sampler, state)
    class(mci_instance_t), intent(inout) :: mci
    class(mci_sampler_t), intent(inout) :: sampler
    class(mci_state_t), intent(in) :: state
    if (size (state%x_in) == size (mci%x, 1) &
         .and. state%selected_channel <= size (mci%x, 2)) then
       call sampler%rebuild (state%selected_channel, &
            state%x_in, state%val, mci%x, mci%f)
       call mci%compute_weight (state%selected_channel)
       call mci%record_integrand (state%val)
    else
       call msg_fatal ("Recalling event: mismatch in channel or dimension")
    end if
  end subroutine mci_instance_recall

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{136}\nwdocspar
\subsection{MCI sampler}
A sampler is an object that implements a multi-channel parameterization of the
unit hypercube.  Specifically, it is able to compute, given a channel and a
set of $x$ MC parameter values, a the complete set of $x$ values and
associated Jacobian factors $f$ for all channels.

Furthermore, the sampler should return a single real value, the integrand, for
the given point in the hypercube.

It must implement a method {\Tt{}evaluate\nwendquote} for performing the above
computations.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{137}\moddef{MCI base: public}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  public :: mci_sampler_t
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{138}\moddef{MCI base: types}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  type, abstract :: mci_sampler_t
   contains
   \LA{}MCI base: mci sampler: TBP\RA{}
  end type mci_sampler_t

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{139}Output, deferred to the implementation.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{140}\moddef{MCI base: mci sampler: TBP}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure (mci_sampler_write), deferred :: write
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{141}\moddef{MCI base: interfaces}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  abstract interface
     subroutine mci_sampler_write (object, unit, testflag)
       import
       class(mci_sampler_t), intent(in) :: object
       integer, intent(in), optional :: unit
       logical, intent(in), optional :: testflag
     end subroutine mci_sampler_write
  end interface

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{142}The evaluation routine.  Input is the channel index {\Tt{}c\nwendquote} and the
one-dimensional parameter array {\Tt{}x{\_}in\nwendquote}.  Output are the integrand value
{\Tt{}val\nwendquote}, the two-dimensional parameter array {\Tt{}x\nwendquote} and the Jacobian array
{\Tt{}f\nwendquote}.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{143}\moddef{MCI base: mci sampler: TBP}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure (mci_sampler_evaluate), deferred :: evaluate
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{144}\moddef{MCI base: interfaces}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  abstract interface
     subroutine mci_sampler_evaluate (sampler, c, x_in, val, x, f)
       import
       class(mci_sampler_t), intent(inout) :: sampler
       integer, intent(in) :: c
       real(default), dimension(:), intent(in) :: x_in
       real(default), intent(out) :: val
       real(default), dimension(:,:), intent(out) :: x
       real(default), dimension(:), intent(out) :: f
     end subroutine mci_sampler_evaluate
  end interface

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{145}Query the validity of the sampling point.  Can be called after
{\Tt{}evaluate\nwendquote}.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{146}\moddef{MCI base: mci sampler: TBP}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  procedure (mci_sampler_is_valid), deferred :: is_valid
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{147}\moddef{MCI base: interfaces}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  abstract interface
     function mci_sampler_is_valid (sampler) result (valid)
       import
       class(mci_sampler_t), intent(in) :: sampler
       logical :: valid
     end function mci_sampler_is_valid
  end interface

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{148}The shortcut.  Again, the channel index {\Tt{}c\nwendquote} and the parameter
array {\Tt{}x{\_}in\nwendquote} are input.  However, we also provide the integrand
value {\Tt{}val\nwendquote}, and we just require that the complete parameter array
{\Tt{}x\nwendquote} and Jacobian array {\Tt{}f\nwendquote} are recovered.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{149}\moddef{MCI base: mci sampler: TBP}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup

\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{150}\moddef{MCI base: interfaces}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup

     subroutine mci_sampler_rebuild (sampler, c, x_in, val, x, f)
       import
       class(mci_sampler_t), intent(inout) :: sampler
       integer, intent(in) :: c
       real(default), dimension(:), intent(in) :: x_in
       real(default), intent(in) :: val
       real(default), dimension(:,:), intent(out) :: x
       real(default), dimension(:), intent(out) :: f
     end subroutine mci_sampler_rebuild
  end interface

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{151}This routine should extract the important data from a sampler that
has been filled by other means.  We fetch the integrand value {\Tt{}val\nwendquote},
the two-dimensional parameter array {\Tt{}x\nwendquote} and the Jacobian array {\Tt{}f\nwendquote}.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{152}\moddef{MCI base: mci sampler: TBP}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup

       import
       class(mci_sampler_t), intent(in) :: sampler

       real(default), dimension(:,:), intent(out) :: x
       real(default), dimension(:), intent(out) :: f
     end subroutine mci_sampler_fetch
  end interface

\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{154}\nwdocspar
\subsection{Results record}
This is an abstract type which allows us to implement callback: each
integration results can optionally be recorded to an instance of this
object.  The actual object may store a new result, average results,
etc.  It may also display a result on-line or otherwise, whenever
the {\Tt{}record\nwendquote} method is called.

   \LA{}MCI base: mci results: TBP\RA{}
  end type mci_results_t

\eatline

flag, which could serve any purpose.

\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{170}\nwdocspar
\subsubsection{Test implementation of the configuration type}
The concrete type contains the number of requested calls and the integral
result, to be determined.

The {\Tt{}max{\_}factor\nwendquote} entry is set for the actual test integration, where the
integrand is not unity but some other constant value.  This value should be
set here, such that the actual maximum of the integrand is known when
vetoing unweighted events.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{171}\moddef{MCI base: public test auxiliary}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  public :: mci_test_t
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{172}\moddef{MCI base: test types}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  type, extends (mci_t) :: mci_test_t
     integer :: divisions = 0
     integer :: tries = 0
     real(default) :: max_factor = 1
   contains
     procedure :: final => mci_test_final
     procedure :: write => mci_test_write
     procedure :: startup_message => mci_test_startup_message
     procedure :: write_log_entry => mci_test_write_log_entry
     procedure :: compute_md5sum => mci_test_compute_md5sum
     procedure :: declare_flat_dimensions => mci_test_ignore_flat_dimensions
     procedure :: declare_equivalences => mci_test_ignore_equivalences
     procedure :: set_divisions => mci_test_set_divisions
     procedure :: set_max_factor => mci_test_set_max_factor
     procedure :: allocate_instance => mci_test_allocate_instance
     procedure :: integrate => mci_test_integrate
     procedure :: prepare_simulation => mci_test_ignore_prepare_simulation
     procedure :: generate_weighted_event => mci_test_generate_weighted_event
     procedure :: generate_unweighted_event => &
          mci_test_generate_unweighted_event
     procedure :: rebuild_event => mci_test_rebuild_event
  end type mci_test_t

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{173}Finalizer: base version is sufficient
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{174}\moddef{MCI base: tests}\endmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine mci_test_final (object)
    class(mci_test_t), intent(inout) :: object
    call object%base_final ()
  end subroutine mci_test_final

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{175}Output: trivial
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{176}\moddef{MCI base: tests}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup
  subroutine mci_test_write (object, unit, pacify, md5sum_version)
    class(mci_test_t), intent(in) :: object
    integer, intent(in), optional :: unit
    logical, intent(in), optional :: pacify
    logical, intent(in), optional :: md5sum_version
    integer :: u
    u = given_output_unit (unit)
    write (u, "(1x,A)")  "Test integrator:"
    call object%base_write (u, pacify, md5sum_version)
    if (object%divisions /= 0) then
       write (u, "(3x,A,I0)")  "Number of divisions  = ", object%divisions
    end if
    if (allocated (object%rng))  call object%rng%write (u)
  end subroutine mci_test_write

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{177}Short version.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{178}\moddef{MCI base: tests}\plusendmoddef\nwstartdeflinemarkup\nwenddeflinemarkup

    integer, intent(in), optional :: unit, n_calls
    call mci%base_startup_message (unit = unit, n_calls = n_calls)
    write (msg_buffer, "(A,1x,I0,1x,A)") &
         "Integrator: Test:", mci%divisions, "divisions"
    call msg_message (unit = unit)
  end subroutine mci_test_startup_message
